as is stated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya-āraṇyaka by the passage नो षु त्वा वाघतश्चनेत्येतस्य द्विपदां चोद्धरति राथंतरं च प्रगाथमथ हास्य नकिः सुदासो रथमित्येतं प्रगाथमुद्धृत्य त्वामिदा ह्यो नर इत्येतं प्रगाथं प्रत्यवदधाति (*no ṣu tvā vāghataścanetyetasya dvipadāṃ coddharati rāthaṃtaraṃ ca pragāthamatha hāsya nakiḥ sudāso rathamityetaṃ pragāthamuddhṛtya tvāmidā hyo nara ityetaṃ pragāthaṃ pratyavadadhāti*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). **NOTE** On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika and on the fifth day, at the time of reciting the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, the Pragātha नो षु त्वा वाघतः (*no ṣu tvā vāghataḥ*) (this Ṛk and the Ṛk that follows it) and one Ṛk of the Dvipadā-Virāṭ metre, रायस्कामः (*rāyaskāmaḥ*), are to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra नो षु त्वा वाघतश्चनेति सद्विपद उपसमस्येद्द्विपदां (*no ṣu tvā vāghataścaneti sadvipada upasamasyeddvipadāṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-3). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśa, when the Marutvatīya-śastra mantras are recited, after the recitation of the Marutvatī Pragātha mantras that are to be recited in the basic rite, the Pragātha mantra नकिः सुदासः (*nakiḥ sudāsaḥ*) (Ṛks 10 and 11) is to be recited. That the same Pragātha mantra is to be recited on the third and sixth days of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra नकिः सुदासो रथमिति मरुत्वतीया ऊर्ध्वं निश्यात् (*nakiḥ sudāso rathamiti marutvatīyā ūrdhvaṃ niśyāt*) and by the sūtra एवं स्थितान् प्रगाथान् पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवयोरन्वहं पुनःपुनरावर्तयेयुः (*evaṃ sthitān pragāthān pṛṣṭhyābhiplavayoranvahaṃ punaḥpunarāvartayeyuḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-3). In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the Pragātha mantra उद्दिन्न्वस्य रिच्यते (*uddinnvasya ricyate*) (Ṛks 12-13) is to be recited, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra उदिन्न्वस्य रिच्यते भूये इत् (*udinnvasya ricyate bhūye it*) (Ā. Sū. 5-16). In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa, the Pragātha mantra कस्तमिंद्र (*kastamiṃdra*) (Ṛks 14, 15) is to be recited, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra कस्तमिंद्र त्वावसुं सद्यो ह जातः (*kastamiṃdra tvāvasuṃ sadyo ha jātaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 5-16). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa, and also on the days from the second day of the sacrifice called Ahargaṇa onward, the Pragātha mentioned above is to be recited, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra कस्तमिंद्र त्वावसुं कन्न्वो अतसीनां (*kastamiṃdra tvāvasuṃ kannvo atasīnāṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4) and by the sūtra आरंभणीयोः पर्यासान् कद्वत्कोऽहरहःशस्यानीति होत्रकाः (*āraṃbhaṇīyoḥ paryāsān kadvatko 'harahaḥśasyānīti hotrakāḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-1). On the third day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, on the side of the Vairūpa-sāman, the two Pragāthas beginning यदिंद्र यावतः (*yadiṃdra yāvataḥ*) (Ṛks 18-31) are to be recited as Stotrīya and Anurūpa, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra यदिंद्र यावतस्त्वमिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रीयानुरूपौ (*yadiṃdra yāvatastvamiti pragāthau stotrīyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 7-18). **NOTE** In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, on the day called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the three Ṛks beginning तरणिरित्सिषासति (*taraṇiritsiṣāsati*) (Ṛks 20-23) are to be recited as an alternative Tṛca, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra तरोभिर्वो विदद्वसुं तरणिरित्सिषासति (*tarobhirvo vidadvasuṃ taraṇiritsiṣāsati*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4). In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited

### Printed p. 100

on the side of the Rathantara-sāman, the Pragātha mantra beginning अभि त्वा शूर (*abhi tvā śūra*) is to be recited as the Stotriya mantras, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमोऽभि त्वा पूर्व पीतये इति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'bhi tvā pūrva pītaye iti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 7-15?). **NOTE** This Pragātha mantra is to be recited for the Āśvina-śastra mantras also, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमो बहवः सूरचक्षसः इति प्रगाथाः (*abhi tvā śūra nonumo bahavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ iti pragāthāḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 6-5). In the Mahāvrata rite, when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, this Pragātha mantra is to be recited on the southern side, as is stated by the passage of the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya-āraṇyaka अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमोऽभि त्वा पूर्वपीतये इति रथंतरस्य स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ प्रगाथौ (*abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'bhi tvā pūrvapītaye iti rathaṃtarasya stotriyānurūpau pragāthau*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2). **NOTE** Among the Āśvina-śastra mantras also the Pragātha mantra इंद्र क्रतुं नः (*iṃdra kratuṃ naḥ*) (Ṛks 26-27) is to be recited, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra इंद्र क्रतुं न आ भराभि त्वा शूर नोनुमः (*iṃdra kratuṃ na ā bharābhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 6-5). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsi, the Pragātha mantra mentioned above is to be recited as the alternative Stotriya Pragātha mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra इंद्र क्रतुं न आ भरेंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भर (*iṃdra kratuṃ na ā bhareṃdra jyeṣṭhaṃ na ā bhara*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4).

Sūkta 32. Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 2; Sūkta 32. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 3; Varga 17, 18, 19, 20, 21. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 26. **NOTE** Seer: Vasiṣṭha for Ṛks 1-25 and the latter half of 26 and 27; Vasiṣṭha or Śakti for the first half of 26. Deity: Indra. Metre: Ṛks 1, 2, 4-27, Pragātha (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī, even Ṛks Satobṛhatī); Ṛk 3, Dvipadā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मो षु त्वा॑ वा॒घत॑श्च॒नारे अ॒स्मन्नि री॑रमन् ।  
> आ॒रात्ता॑च्चित्सध॒मादं॑ न॒ आ ग॑ही॒ह वा॒ सन्नुप॑ श्रुधि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मो इति । सु । त्वा । वाघतः । चन । आरे । अस्मत् । नि । रीरमन् ।  
> आरात्तात् । चित् । सधमादं । नः । आ । गहि । इह । वा । सन् । उप । श्रुधि ॥१॥

### Printed p. 101

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वयो वाघतश्चन यजमाना अस्मदस्मत्ते आरे दूरे मो नि रीरमन् । नि नितरां रमयंतु । अतस्त्वमारात्ताच्चिद्दूरेऽपि वर्तमानोऽस्मदीयं सधमादं यज्ञमा गहि । आगच्छ । इह वात्रापि वा सन् विद्यमान उप श्रुधि । अस्मदीयं स्तोत्रमुपशृणु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, may the other sacrificers (वाघतश्चन (*vāghataścana*)) not detain you far from us; may they not make you rest far away. Therefore you, even if you are staying far off, come to our sacrifice, which is the place of joint rejoicing; or if you are here, present, listen to our praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वाघतश्चन (*vāghataścana*)—any other sacrificers
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—than us
- आरे (*āre*)—in a distant place
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मो नि रीरमन् (*mo ni rīraman*)—let them not detain
- आरात्ताच्चित् (*ārāttāccit*)—even from the most distant place
- नः सधमादं (*naḥ sadhamādaṃ*)—to our sacrifice
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come
- इह वा (*iha vā*)—or in this very place of sacrifice
- सन् (*san*)—being
- उप श्रुधि (*upa śrudhi*)—listen to our praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let no other sacrificers detain you in a place farther away than we are. Be pleased to come to our sacrifice even from the most distant place. Staying right in this place of sacrifice, listen to our praises.

##### English translation
Let not, Indra, (other) worshippers detain you far from us : come from whatever distance to our assembly : present at this ceremony, hear our (prayers).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मे हि ते॑ ब्रह्म॒कृतः॑ सु॒ते सचा॒ मधौ॒ न मक्ष॒ आस॑ते ।  
> इंद्रे॒ कामं॑ जरि॒तारो॑ वसू॒यवो॒ रथे॒ न पाद॒मा  ॑
> दधुः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमे । हि । ते । ब्रह्मकृतः । सुते । सचा । मधौ । न । मक्षः । आसते ।  
> इंद्रे । कामं । जरितारः । वसुयवः । रथे । न । पादं । आ । दधुः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 102

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे ब्रह्मकृतः स्तोत्रकृतो मधौ न मधुनीव मक्षो मक्षिकाः सचा सहासते । उपविशंति । अथ परोक्षस्तुतिः । वसूयवो धनकामा जरितारः स्तोतारः काममिष्टमिंद्रे रथे न पादं रथे पादमिवा दधुः । समर्पयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, for you, when the Soma has been pressed, these praise-makers (ब्रह्मकृतः (*brahmakṛtaḥ*)) sit together like flies (मक्षः (*makṣaḥ*)) on honey. Now comes the indirect praise: the wealth-seeking praisers (जरितारः (*jaritāraḥ*)) lay their desire on Indra as one sets the foot on a chariot; that is, they entrust it to him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) ते (*te*)—for you
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma juice is pressed
- इमे ब्रह्मकृतः (*ime brahmakṛtaḥ*)—these praisers
- मधौ (*madhau*)—when honey is poured out
- मक्षः न (*makṣaḥ na*)—as bees swarm
- सचा (*sacā*)—all gathering together
- आसते हि (*āsate hi*)—sit
- रथे (*rathe*)—on a chariot
- पादं न (*pādaṃ na*)—as one sets the foot for support
- वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)—seekers of wealth
- जरितारः (*jaritāraḥ*)—the praisers
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—their desire
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—in Indra
- आ दधुः (*ā dadhuḥ*)—cause to rest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the Soma juice is pressed for you, these praisers all gather and sit together, as bees swarm when honey is poured out. As one sets the foot on a chariot for support, the wealth-seeking praisers cause their desire to rest in Indra alone and obtain his protection.

##### English translation
When the libation is effused for you, these offerers of sacrifice swarm like flies round honey : the pious praisers, desiring riches, fix their hope upon Indra, like a foot upon a chariot.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रा॒यस्का॑मो॒ वज्र॑हस्तं सु॒दक्षि॑णं पु॒त्रो न पि॒तरं॑ हुवे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रायःऽकामः । वज्रहस्तं । सुदक्षिणं । पुत्रः । न । पितरं । हुवे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रायस्कामो धनकामोऽहं सुदक्षिणं शोभनदानं वज्रहस्तमिंद्रं पुत्रो न पुत्र इव पितरं हुवे । ह्वयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: I, desiring wealth, call Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand and gives well, as a son calls his father.

### Printed p. 103

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—a son who seeks help
- पितरं न (*pitaraṃ na*)—as he calls his father for help
- रायस्कामः (*rāyaskāmaḥ*)—I, who desire wealth
- सुदक्षिणं (*sudakṣiṇaṃ*)—the excellent giver
- वज्रहस्तं (*vajrahastaṃ*)—Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand
- हुवे (*huve*)—I call for help

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a son who seeks help calls his father for help, I, who desire wealth, call for help upon Indra, the excellent giver, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand.

##### English translation
Desirous of riches. I call upon the benevolent wielder of the thunderbolt, as a son upon a father.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मे इंद्रा॑य सुन्विरे॒ सोमा॑सो॒ दध्या॑शिरः ।  
> ता आ मदा॑य वज्रहस्त पी॒तये॒ हरि॑भ्यां या॒ह्योक॒  
> आ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमे । इंद्राय । सुन्विरे । सोमासः । दधिऽआशिरः ।  
> तान् । आ । मदाय । वज्रहस्त । पीतये । हरिऽभ्यां । याहि । ओकः । आ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्रहस्त दध्याशिरो दधिमिश्रणा इमे सोमासः सोमा इंद्राय तुभ्यं सुन्विरे । सुता बभूवुः । तान् सोमान्मदाय मदार्थं पीतये पानायौको यज्ञसदनमाभि हरिभ्यामश्वाभ्यामा याहि । आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, these Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for you. For your delight, to drink those Somas, come with your two bay horses to the sacrificial seat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt
- दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*)—mixed with curds
- इमे सोमासः (*ime somāsaḥ*)—these Soma juices
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for you, the lord of all
- सुन्विरे (*sunvire*)—have been pressed and are ready
- तान् (*tān*)—those Soma juices
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for your delight
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—to drink
- ओकः आ (*okaḥ ā*)—facing our sacrificial seat
- हरिभ्यां (*haribhyāṃ*)—with your horses
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come

### Printed p. 104

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, these Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed and made ready for you, the lord of all. To drink these Soma juices for your delight, be pleased to come with your horses facing our sacrificial seat.

##### English translation
These Soma juices, mixed with curds, are poured out to Indra : come, wielder of the thunderbolt; with your horses to our dwelling, to drink there for (your) exhilaration.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रव॒च्छ्रुत्क॑र्ण ईयते॒ वसू॑नां॒ नू चि॑न्नो मर्धिष॒द्गिरः॑ ।  
> स॒द्यश्चि॒द्यः स॒हस्रा॑णि श॒ता दद॒न्नकि॒र्दित्सं॑त॒मा मि॑नत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रवत् । श्रुत्ऽकर्णः । ईयते । वसूनां । नु । चित् । नः । मर्धिषत् । गिरः ।  
> सद्यः । चित् । यः । सहस्राणि । सता । ददत् । नकिः । दित्संतं । आ । मिनत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्रुत्कर्णो याच्ञाश्रवणरूपकर्ण इंद्रो वसूनां वसूनीयते । याच्यते नोऽस्मदीया गिरो याच्ञावाक्यानि श्रवत् । शृणोतु । नू चिन्नैव मर्धिषत् । हिंसतु । अश्रवणेन याच्ञावाक्यानि निष्फलानि न करोतीत्यर्थः । अपि चेंद्रः सद्यश्चित् सद्य एव याच्ञानंतरमेव सहस्राणि शतानि च ददत् । प्रयच्छेत् । दित्संतं दातुमिच्छंतं तमिंद्रं नकिरा मिनत् । न हिंस्यात् । कश्चिदपि न वारयेदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: Indra, whose ear is, as it were, an ear that hears petitions, is asked for riches. May he hear our words of petition; may he never harm them, that is, he does not make our petitions fruitless by not hearing them. Moreover, Indra gives thousands and hundreds immediately, right after the petition. No one may harm that Indra who wishes to give; that is, no one may hold him back.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रुत्कर्णः (*śrutkarṇaḥ*)—Indra, whose ears hear our praise and our petition
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—for riches
- ईयते (*īyate*)—is petitioned
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words of petition
- श्रवत् (*śravat*)—hears
- नू चित् मर्धिषत् (*nū cit mardhiṣat*)—surely never causes the breaking of our sacrifice
- सद्यश्चित् (*sadyaścit*)—immediately upon the prayer
- सहस्राणि (*sahasrāṇi*)—in thousands
- शता (*śatā*)—in hundreds
- ददत् (*dadat*)—gives
- दित्संतं (*ditsaṃtaṃ*)—that Indra, who wishes to give
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one
- आ मिनत् (*ā minat*)—can harm and obstruct

### Printed p. 105

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, whose ears hear our praise and our petition, is asked for riches, and he hears our words of petition. He never causes the breaking of our sacrifice. As soon as he is prayed to by us, he gives us hundreds and thousands. No one can harm that Indra who wishes to give, and no one can obstruct him.

##### English translation
May Indra, whose ear is ready to hear, listen, to the suppliant for riches, and never disappoint our prayers : he who is the giver of hundreds and thousands : may no one ever hinder him when willing to give.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स वी॒रो अप्र॑तिष्कुत॒ इंद्रे॑ण शूशुवे॒ नृभिः॑ ।  
> यस्ते॑ गभी॒रा सव॑नानि वृत्रहन्त्सु॒नोत्या च॒ धाव॑ति ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । वीरः । अप्रतिऽस्कुतः । इंद्रेण । शूशुवे । नृऽभिः ।  
> यः । ते । गभीरा । सवनानि । वृत्रहन् । सुनोति । आ । च । धावति ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहन् ते त्वदर्थं यः पुमान् गभीरा गभीराणि सवनानि सोमान् सुनोति आ धावति च त्वां स्तुतिभिरुपधावति च स वीर इंद्रेण हेतुनाप्रतिष्कुतः केनाप्यप्रतिगतोऽप्रतिशब्दितो वा भवेत् । नृभिः परिचारकैः शूशुवे । उपगम्यते च । श्वयतिर्गतिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O slayer of Vṛtra, the man who for you presses the deep, that is, copious, Soma-pressings, and who approaches you swiftly with praises, that hero, by reason of Indra, becomes one whom no one opposes or answers back; he is served by attendants, that is, he is approached. The root श्वयतिर्गतिकर्मा (*śvayatirgatikarmā*) has the sense of going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- गभीरा (*gabhīrā*)—copious
- सवनानि (*savanāni*)—Somas
- सुनोति (*sunoti*)—presses
- आ धावति च (*ā dhāvati ca*)—and (the one who) approaches you swiftly with praises
- सः वीरः (*saḥ vīraḥ*)—that same valiant man
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—by the help of you, the lord
- अप्रतिष्कुतः (*apratiṣkutaḥ*)—unopposed by anyone
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by attendants and other people
- शूशुवे (*śūśuve*)—is served

### Printed p. 106

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, the man who for you presses copious Somas and who approaches you swiftly with praises, that same valiant man, by the help of you, the lord, is not brought down by anyone's blow and is served by attendants and other people.

##### English translation
Slayer of Vritra, the hero who offers sacrifices to you, who eagerly approaches you (with praises), he, (protected) by Indra, is unresisted (by any one), and is honoured by men.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भवा॒ वरू॑थं मघवन्म॒घोनां॒ यत्स॒मजा॑सि॒ शर्ध॑तः ।  
> वि त्वाह॑तस्य॒ वेद॑नं भजेम॒ह्या दू॒णाशो॑ भरा॒ गयं॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भव । वरूथं । मघऽवन् । मघोनां । यत् । सम्ऽअजासि । शर्धतः ।  
> वि । त्वाऽहतस्य । वेदनं । भजेमहि । आ । दुःऽनशः । भर । गयं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र मघोनां हविष्मतां वरूथमुपद्रवाणां वारकं वर्म भव । यद्यस्त्वं शर्धत उत्सहमानान् शत्रून् समजासि संप्रेरयेः । अपि च त्वाहतस्य त्वया हतस्य शत्रोर्वेदनं धनं वि भजेमहि । विशेषेण लभेमहि । किंच दुर्नशो नाशयितुमशक्यस्त्वं गयं गृहं धनं वा भर । अस्मभ्यमाहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O wealthy Indra, be armour that wards off calamities for those who have offerings, since you drive forth the enemies who rise up. May we also obtain in a special way the wealth of an enemy slain by you. And you, who cannot be destroyed, bring us a house or wealth; that is, bring it to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—by whatever greatness
- शर्धतः (*śardhataḥ*)—the violent enemies of ours
- समजासि (*samajāsi*)—you strike and drive away (by that same power)
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—to the sacrificers who have offerings
- वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—as protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- त्वाहतस्य (*tvāhatasya*)—of the enemies slain by you
- वेदनं (*vedanaṃ*)—the wealth
- वि भजेमहि (*vi bhajemahi*)—may we divide
- दुर्नशः (*durnaśaḥ*)—you, who are indestructible
- गयं (*gayaṃ*)—to us house and the like
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring

### Printed p. 107

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, by that same power with which you strike and drive away our violent enemies, be a protector to the sacrificers who have offerings. May we divide the wealth of the enemies slain by you. You who are indestructible, bring us house and the like.

##### English translation
Be a defence, Maghavan, to the wealthy (offerers of oblations), for you are the discomfiter of (our) adversaries : may we divide the spoil of the enemy slain by you : do you. who are indestructible, bring it to our dwelling.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒नोता॑ सोम॒पाव्ने॒ सोम॒मिंद्रा॑य व॒ज्रिणे॑ ।  
> पच॑ता प॒क्तीरव॑से कृणु॒ध्वमित्पृ॒णन्नित्पृ॑ण॒ते मयः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुनोत । सोमऽपाव्ने । सोमं । इंद्राय । वज्रिणे ।  
> पचत । पक्तीः । अवसे । कृणुध्वं । इत् । पृणन् । इत् । पृणते । मयः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदीयाः पुरुषाः वज्रिणे सोमपाव्ने सोमस्य पात्र इंद्राय सोमं सुनोत । अभिषुणुत । अवस इंद्रं तर्पयितुं पक्तीः पक्तव्यान् पुरोडाशादीन् पचत च । कृणुध्वमित् । इंद्रप्रियकराणि कर्माणि च कुरुतैव । इंद्रो हि मयः सुखं पृणन्निद्यजमानाय प्रयच्छन्नेव पृणते हवींषीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O my men, press Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the drinker of Soma. To satisfy Indra, cook also the things that are to be cooked, the sacrificial cakes and the like, and perform just those rites that please Indra. For Indra, giving happiness to the sacrificer, bestows it on the one who offers oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O sacrificers and others) वज्रिणे (*vajriṇe*)—who has the thunderbolt
- सोमपाव्ने (*somapāvne*)—who drinks Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- सुनोत (*sunota*)—press
- अवसे (*avase*)—to satisfy Indra
- पक्तीः (*paktīḥ*)—the sacrificial cakes and the like
- पचत (*pacata*)—cook
- कृणुध्वमित् (*kṛṇudhvamit*)—perform just the rites that satisfy Indra
- (that Indra indeed) पृणते (*pṛṇate*)—to the one who offers oblations
- मयः (*mayaḥ*)—happiness
- पृणन्नित् (*pṛṇannit*)—surely provides

### Printed p. 108

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers and others, press Soma for Indra, who has the thunderbolt and who drinks Soma. To satisfy Indra, cook the sacrificial cakes and the like. Perform just the rites that satisfy Indra. That Indra, indeed, surely provides happiness to the one who offers oblations.

##### English translation
Pour out the libation to Indra, the thunderer, the drinker of the Soma : prepare the baked (cakes) to satisfy him : do (what is agreeable to him), for he bestows happiness on (the worshipper) who pleases him.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा स्रे॑धत सोमिनो॒ दक्ष॑ता म॒हे कृ॑णु॒ध्वं रा॒य आ॒तुजे॑ ।  
> त॒रणि॒रिज्ज॑यति॒ क्षेति॒ पुष्य॑ति॒ न दे॒वासः॑ कव॒त्नवे॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । स्रेधत । सोमिनः । दक्षत । महे । कृणुध्वं । राये । आऽतुजे ।  
> तरणिः । इत् । जयति । क्षेति । पुष्यति । न । देवासः । कवत्नवे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदीया जनाः सोमिनः सोमवतो यागान्मा स्रेधत । मा हिंसिष्ट । दक्षत । यागादिकं कर्तुमुत्सहध्वं च । महे महत आतुजे । तुजिर्हिंसाकर्मा दानकर्मा वा । शत्रूणामभिहिंसकाय धनानां प्रदात्रे वेंद्राय राये धनलाभार्थं कृणुध्वं । कर्माणि कुरुत च । तरणिरित् कर्मसु त्वरित एव जयति शत्रून् । क्षेति । गृहे निवसति च । पुष्यति । प्रजया पशुभिश्च पुष्टो भवति । कवत्नवे कुत्सितक्रियायै । कवोऽपसृष्टस्यातेः सातत्यगमनकर्मणो रूपं कवत्नुरिति ॥ देवासो देवा न भवंतीति शेषः । सुखप्राप्तये भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O my people, do not hinder the sacrifices that have Soma; do not harm them. Be energetic also in performing the sacrifice and the rest. For the great Indra, the one who harms the enemies or the one who gives wealth, perform rites for the gain of wealth. The swift one wins over the enemies in the rites, dwells in his house, and thrives in offspring and cattle. कवत्नवे (*kavatnave*) means for a bad action. The gods do not become so; the meaning is that they become for the attainment of happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O sacrificers and others) सोमिनः (*sominaḥ*)—the sacrifices that have Soma
- मा स्रेधत (*mā sredhata*)—do not stop
- दक्षत (*dakṣata*)—carry out the sacrificial rites with energy
- महे (*mahe*)—for the great
- अतुजे (*atuje*)—Indra, the harmer of enemies
- राये (*rāye*)—for the gain of wealth
- कृणुध्वं (*kṛṇudhvaṃ*)—rites

### Printed p. 109

- तरणिरित् (*taraṇirit*)—he alone who carries out the rite with skill
- क्षेति (*kṣeti*)—dwells in his house
- जयति (*jayati*)—he alone conquers
- पुष्यति (*puṣyati*)—is nourished with sons and the rest
- कवत्नवे (*kavatnave*)—for one deprived of rites
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- न (*na*)—do not become helpers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers and others, do not stop the sacrifices that have Soma. Carry out the sacrificial rites with energy. Perform rites for the gain of wealth, addressed to Indra, who is mighty and the harmer of enemies. Only he who carries out the rite with skill dwells in his house. He alone conquers. He thrives with sons and the rest. To one deprived of rites the gods do not become helpers.

##### English translation
Offerers of the libation, do not hesitate : be active : sacrifice to the mighty benefactor for the sake of riches : the assiduous worshipper conquers (his enemies), dwells in a habitation, and prospers : the gods favour not the imperfect rite.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नकिः॑ सु॒दासो॒ रथं॒ पर्या॑स॒ न री॑रमत् ।  
> इंद्रो॒ यस्या॑वि॒ता यस्य॑ म॒रुतो॒ गम॒त्स गोम॑ति व्र॒जे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नकिः । सुदासः । रथं । परि । आस । न । रीरमत् ।  
> इंद्रः । यस्य । अविता । यस्य । मरुतः । गमत् । सः । गोऽमति । व्रजे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुदासः शोभनदानस्य यजमानस्य रथं नकिः पर्यास । कश्चिन्न पर्यास्यति । न रीरमत् । न रमयति च । आत्मार्थं न कश्चिदेनं गृह्णातीत्यर्थः । अपि च यस्येंद्रोऽविता रक्षिता यस्य च मरुतोऽवितारः स गोमति गोयुक्ते व्रजे गोष्ठे गमत् । गच्छेत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: no one will overturn the chariot of Sudās, the sacrificer of good gifts, and no one will stop it; that is, no one seizes him for his own purposes. Moreover, he whose protector is Indra and whose protectors are the Maruts will go to the cow-filled pen, the cowshed; the word गमत् (*gamat*) means "would go".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुदासः (*sudāsaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who is an excellent giver
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one at all
- पर्यास (*paryāsa*)—can face it and turn it back
- न रीरमत् (*na rīramat*)—no one can obstruct it
- यस्य (*yasya*)—to which sacrificer
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अविता (*avitā*)—is protector
- यस्य (*yasya*)—to whom
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts (are protectors)
- सः (*saḥ*)—that sacrificer
- गोमति (*gomati*)—filled with cattle
- व्रजे (*vraje*)—the cowshed
- गमत् (*gamat*)—will reach

### Printed p. 110

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

No one at all can face and turn back the chariot of the sacrificer who is an excellent giver. No one can obstruct it. The sacrificer to whom Indra is protector and to whom the Maruts are protectors will reach a cowshed filled with cattle.

##### English translation
No one overturns, no one arrests, the chariot of the liheral sacrificer , he, of whom Indra is the protector, of whom the Maruts (are the defenders): will walk in pastures filled with cattle.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गम॒द्वाजं॑ वा॒जय॑न्निंद्र॒ मर्त्यो॒ यस्य॒ त्वम॑वि॒ता भुवः॑ ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ बोध्यवि॒ता रथा॑नाम॒स्माकं॑ शूर नृ॒णां ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गमत् । वाजं । वाजयन् । इंद्र । मर्त्यः । यस्य । त्वं । अविता । भुवः ।  
> अस्माकं । बोधि । अविता । रथानां । अस्माकं । शूर । नृणां ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं यस्य मर्त्यस्याविता रक्षिता भुवः भवेः स मर्त्यो वाजयन् स्तोत्रेण त्वां बलिनं कुर्वन् वाजमन्नं गमत् । गच्छेत् । अपि च हे शूर अस्माकं वासिष्ठानां रथानामविता रक्षिता बोधि । भव ॥ भवतेर्लोटि रूपं । भकारस्य बकारश्छांदसः ॥ अस्माकं नृणां पुत्रादीनां चाविता भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, the mortal whose protector you become, strengthening you with praise, would attain वाजं (*vājaṃ*), food. And, O hero, be the protector of our, the Vāsiṣṭhas', chariots; बोधि (*bodhi*) means "be", a form of the root meaning "to be" in the imperative, with a Vedic change of letter. Be also the protector of our men, that is, of our sons and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यस्य (*yasya*)—for whichever man
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you are
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—that same man
- वाजयन् (*vājayan*)—making you strong by praise
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- गमत् (*gamat*)—may he attain
- शूर (*śūra*)—O heroic Indra
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—of us, born in the family of Vasiṣṭha
- रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)—for the chariots
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know that you must be
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—of our
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—sons and the rest, be protector

### Printed p. 111

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the man for whom you are protector, that same man, making you strong by praise, may attain food. O heroic Indra, know that you must be protector of our chariots, we who are born in the family of Vasiṣṭha. Be protector also of our sons and the rest.

##### English translation
Let the man of whom you, Indra, are the protector, invigorating (you with praise), enjoy (abundant) food : be the preserver, hero, of our chariots, (the preserver) of our people.

#### Ṛk 12

**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदिन्न्व॑स्य रिच्य॒तेंऽशो॒ धनं॒ न जि॒ग्युषः॑ ।  
> य इंद्रो॒ हरि॑वा॒न्न द॑भंति॒ तं रिपो॒ दक्षं॑ दधाति सो॒मिनि॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । इत् । नु । अस्य । रिच्यते । अंशः । धनं । न । जिग्युषः ।  
> यः । इंद्रः । हरिवान् । न । दभंति । तं । रिपः । दक्षं । दधाति । सोमिनि ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्यांशो यज्ञे सोमस्य भागोऽतिरिच्यतेऽन्येभ्योऽपि देवेभ्यः। इंद्रस्य त्रिष्वपि सवनेषु सोमपानमस्ति माध्यंदिनं हि सर्वमैंद्रमिति। जिग्युषो जितवतो धनं न धनमिव। उदिन्न्विति त्रयः पूरणाः। अपि च यो हरिवानिंद्रः सोमिनि यजमाने दक्षं बलं दधाति संदधाति, तं रिपो रिपवो न दभंति। न हिंसंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: this Indra's share, his portion of Soma in the sacrifice, exceeds even that of the other gods. Indra has the drinking of Soma in all three pressings, for the midday pressing is wholly Indra's. The share is like the wealth of one who has won. The three words at the beginning of the verse are expletives. Moreover, the enemies do not harm that Indra, lord of the bay horses, who places strength in the sacrificer who has Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जिग्युषः (*jigyuṣaḥ*)—of the victorious man
- धनं न (*dhanaṃ na*)—like the wealth
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- अंशः (*aṃśaḥ*)—the share of Soma in the sacrifice
- उदिन्न्व रिच्यते (*udinnva ricyate*)—certainly exceeds the shares of the other gods
- हरिवान् (*harivān*)—possessing the horses called Hari
- यः इंद्रः (*yaḥ iṃdraḥ*)—the Indra who
- सोमिनि (*somini*)—in the sacrificer
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—strength
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—fills in
- तं (*taṃ*)—such an Indra
- रिपः (*ripaḥ*)—enemies
- न दभंति (*na dabhaṃti*)—do not harm

### Printed p. 112

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the wealth of a victorious man increases, so the share of Soma that belongs to Indra in the sacrifice exceeds the shares of the other gods. Enemies do not harm that Indra, possessing the horses called Hari, who fills the sacrificer with strength.

##### English translation
Verily (Indra's) share (of the Soma) exceeds (that of other deities) like the wealth of the victorious : enemies overcome not him, who is the lord of bay steeds, who gives strength to the offerer of the libation.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मंत्र॒मख॑र्वं॒ सुधि॑तं सु॒पेश॑सं॒ दधा॑त य॒ज्ञिये॒ष्वा ।  
> पू॒र्वीश्च॒न प्रसि॑तयस्तरंति॒ तं य इंद्रे॒ कर्म॑णा॒ भुव॑त् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंत्रं । अखर्वं । सुधितं । सुपेशसं । दधात । यज्ञियेषु । आ ।  
> पूर्वीः । चन । प्रसितयः । तरंति । तं । यः । इंद्रे । कर्मणा । भुवत् ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जनाः अखर्वमनल्पं सुधितं सुहितं सुपेशसं शोभनरूपं मंत्रं स्तोत्रं यज्ञियेषु यजनीयेषु देवेषु मध्य इंद्राय दधात । विधत्त । यो जनः कर्मणा स्तुत्यादिरूपेणेंद्र इंद्रस्य चित्ते भुवत् भवेत् तं जनं पूर्वीर्बह्व्यः प्रसितयः पाशादीनि बंधनानि । चनेति समुदायो नेत्यर्थे वर्तते । न तरंति । न व्याप्नुवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O people, offer to Indra, among the gods worthy of sacrifice, a hymn of praise that is ample, well placed and graceful in form. The man who, by action in the form of praise and the like, abides in Indra, in Indra's mind, many bonds, such as nooses and the like, do not overcome that man. The word चन (*cana*) taken together stands in the sense of "not".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O sacrificers and others) अखर्वं (*akharvaṃ*)—of ample greatness
- सुधितं (*sudhitaṃ*)—well recited
- सुपेशसं (*supeśasaṃ*)—of excellent form
- मंत्रं (*maṃtraṃ*)—the hymn of praise
- यज्ञियेषु (*yajñiyeṣu*)—among the gods worthy of sacrifice, addressed to Indra
- आ दधात (*ā dadhāta*)—offer
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*)—by acts of praise and the like
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—with his mind offered to Indra
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—is devoted
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—of many kinds
- प्रसितयः चन (*prasitayaḥ cana*)—even bonds
- तरंति (*taraṃti*)—fall away without clinging

### Printed p. 113

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers and others, offer a hymn of praise that is of ample greatness, well recited and of excellent form, among the gods worthy of sacrifice, addressed to Indra. The sacrificer who by acts of praise and the like is devoted, with his mind offered to Indra, even bonds of many kinds fall away from him without clinging.

##### English translation
Address (to Indra) amongst the gods, the ample, well-uttered, and graceful prayer : many bonds entangle not him who, by his devotion, abides in Indra.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कस्तमिं॑द्र॒ त्वाव॑सु॒ना मर्त्यो॑ दधर्षति ।  
> श्र॒द्धा इत्ते॑ मघव॒न्पार्ये॑ दि॒वि वा॒जी वाजं॑ सिषासति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कः । तं । इंद्र । त्वावसुं । आ । मर्त्यः । दधर्षति ।  
> श्रद्धा । इत् । ते । मघवन् । पार्ये । दिवि । वाजी । वाजं । सिसासति ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तव चित्ते यो भवेत् त्वावसुं । त्वं वसुर्व्यापको यस्येति बहुव्रीहिः । तं जनं को मर्त्य आ दधर्षति । आधर्षेत् । हे मघवन् ते त्वदर्थं यः श्रद्धा श्रद्धया युक्तः सन् वाजी हविष्मान् भवेत् पार्ये दिवि सौत्येऽहनि स वाजमन्नं बलं वा सिषासति । सेवते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, the man who is in your mind is त्वावसुं (*tvāvasuṃ*), a possessive compound meaning "he of whom you are the all-pervading wealth". What mortal assails such a man? O Maghavan, he who, endowed with faith, becomes the possessor of the oblation for you, on the day of the Soma pressing he enjoys food or strength; सिषासति (*siṣāsati*) means "enjoys".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वावसुं (*tvāvasuṃ*)—who has you alone as his protector
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- कः मर्त्यः (*kaḥ martyaḥ*)—what mortal indeed
- आ दधर्षति (*ā dadharṣati*)—can injure him?
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, possessor of wealth
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- (यः (*yaḥ*)—who) श्रद्धा (*śraddhā*)—endowed with faith
- वाजी (*vājī*)—becomes the possessor of the oblation
- (he), पार्ये इत् दिवि (*pārye it divi*)—on the very day of the Soma offering
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सिषासति (*siṣāsati*)—enjoys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, what mortal indeed can injure the sacrificer who has you alone as his protector? O Indra, possessor of wealth, he who, endowed with faith, becomes the possessor of the oblation and offers the oblation to you, enjoys (obtains) food on the very day of the Soma offering.

### Printed p. 114

##### English translation
What mortal, Indra, injures him who has you for his support ? He who offers you (sacrificial) food, Maghavan, with faith, he obtair s food on the day of the libation.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒घोनः॑ स्म वृत्र॒हत्ये॑षु चोदय॒ यो दद॑ति प्रि॒या वसु॑ ।  
> तव॒ प्रणी॑ती हर्यश्व सू॒रिभि॒र्विश्वा॑ तरेम दुरि॒ता ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मघोनः । स्म । वृत्रहत्येषु । चोदय । ये । ददति । प्रिया । वसु ।  
> तव । प्रऽनीती । हरिअश्व । सूरिभिः । विश्वा । तरेम । दुःइता ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र मघोनो धनवतस्ते । त्वदर्थमित्यर्थः । प्रिया प्रियाणि वसु वसूनि धनानि ये जना ददति प्रयच्छंति ताञ्जनान् वृत्रहत्येषु संग्रामेषु चोदय । प्रेरय । हे हर्यश्व तव प्रणीती प्रणीत्या प्रणयनेन सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिः पुत्रादिभिः सार्धं विश्वा विश्वानि दुरिता दुरितानि तरेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, those men who give to you, the wealthy, dear riches, that is, riches for your sake, urge those men on in the battles, in the conflicts. O lord of the bay horses, by your leading, together with the praisers, our sons and the rest, may we cross all evils.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यो (*yo*)—the sacrificers who
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—to you, the wealthy
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—beneficial
- वसु (*vasu*)—riches and the like
- ददति स्म (*dadati sma*)—offer
- (them) वृत्रहत्येषु (*vṛtrahatyeṣu*)—in battles
- चोदय (*codaya*)—urge so that they become powerful
- हर्यश्व (*haryaśva*)—O Indra, possessing the horses called Hari
- तव (*tava*)—your
- प्रणीती (*praṇītī*)—by the loving leadership
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—we, together with our sons and the rest who are praisers
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- दुरिता (*duritā*)—sorrows
- तरेमु (*taremu*)—may we cross

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, urge in battles, so that they become powerful, those sacrificers who offer beneficial riches and the like to you, the wealthy. O Indra, possessing the horses called Hari, by your loving leadership may we, together with our sons and the rest who are praisers, cross all sorrows.

##### English translation
Animate (those men) for the destruction of their foes, who offer treasures which are dear to you, the abounder in wealth : may we, lord of bay

### Printed p. 115

steeds, along with (your) worshippers, pass over all difficulties by your guidance.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तवेदिं॑द्राव॒मं वसु॒ त्वं पु॑ष्यसि मध्य॒मं ।  
> स॒त्रा विश्व॑स्य पर॒मस्य॑ राजसि॒ नकि॑ष्ट्वा॒ गोषु॑ वृण्वते ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । इत् । इंद्र । अवमं । वसु । त्वं । पुष्यसि । मध्यमं ।  
> सत्रा । विश्वस्य । परमस्य । राजसि । नकिः । त्वा । गोषु । वृण्वते ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अवममधमं त्रपुसीसादिकं वसु धनं । यद्वा । भौमं वस्ववमं । तवेत्तवैव । त्वं त्वमेव मध्यमं वसु रजतहिरण्यादिकमांतरिक्षं वा पुष्यसि । विश्वस्य सर्वस्य परमस्योत्तमस्यापि रत्नादेर्दिव्यस्य वा वसुनो राजसि । ईशिषे । सत्रा सत्यमेव । अपि च त्वा त्वां गोषु निमित्तेषु नकिर्वृण्वते । कोऽपि न वारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, अवमं (*avamaṃ*), the lowest wealth, lead, tin and the like, is yours alone; or else the earthly wealth is the lowest. You yourself nourish the middle wealth, silver, gold and the like, or the wealth of the atmosphere. You rule over all wealth, even the highest, such as jewels, or the heavenly wealth; सत्रा (*satrā*) means "truly". Moreover, no one holds you back in matters of cattle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अवमं (*avamaṃ*)—not the most excellent, lead and the like
- वसु (*vasu*)—whatever riches there are, all of them
- तवेत् (*tavet*)—are yours alone
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you yourself
- मध्यमं (*madhyamaṃ*)—the middling, silver and the like
- पुष्यसि (*puṣyasi*)—cause to increase
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all
- परमस्य (*paramasya*)—of the excellent, jewels and the like
- राजसि (*rājasi*)—you yourself are the lord
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—when striving for the sake of cattle
- नकिः वृण्वते (*nakiḥ vṛṇvate*)—no one can hinder

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whatever riches there are that are not the most excellent, lead and the like, all of them are yours alone. You yourself cause the middling riches, silver and the like, to increase. You yourself are the lord of all the excellent jewels and the like. When one strives for the sake of cattle, truly no one can hinder you.

##### English translation
Yours Indra, is the vast valuable wealth : you cherish the middling: you rule over all that which is the most precious : no one opposes you in (the recovering of the) cattle.

### Printed p. 116

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, the words अवम (*avama*), मध्यम (*madhyama*) and परम (*parama*) may also have the meanings the earth, the atmosphere and the excellent heaven. It may also be said that the purport is that Indra is the one lord of all the worlds, the earth and the rest.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं विश्व॑स्य धन॒दा अ॑सि श्रु॒तो य ईं॒ भवं॑त्या॒जयः॑ ।  
> तवा॒यं विश्वः॑ पुरुहूत॒ पार्थि॑वोऽव॒स्युर्नाम॑ भिक्षते ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । विश्वस्य । धनदाः । असि । श्रुतः । ये । ईं । भवंति । आजयः ।  
> तव । अयं । विश्वः । पुरुहूत । पार्थिवः । अवस्युः । नाम । भिक्षते ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं विश्वस्य सर्वस्य स्तोतुर्यजमानस्य वा धनदा धनस्य दाता सञ्श्रुतः प्रसिद्धोऽसि । य ईं य एत आजयो युद्धानि भवंति तेष्वपि धनदाः श्रुतोऽसि । हे पुरुहूत विश्वः सर्वोऽप्ययं पार्थिवो जनस्तव । त्वत्त इत्यर्थः । अवस्यू रक्षामिच्छन्नामान्नमुदकं वा । बर्हिर्नामेत्युदकनामसु पाठात् । भिक्षते । याचते । त्वामेवेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, you are renowned as the giver of wealth to all, to the praiser or the sacrificer; and in those battles that take place you are also renowned as the giver of wealth. O Indra, invoked by many, all these men of the earth, desiring protection, ask for नाम (*nāma*), food or water, since it is read among the names of water; तव (*tava*) here means "from you". The word "you alone" is to be supplied: they ask you alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—to all sacrificers
- धनदाः (*dhanadāḥ*)—as giver of wealth
- श्रुतः (*śrutaḥ*)—renowned
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- ये ईं (*ye īṃ*)—which renowned
- आजयः (*ājayaḥ*)—battles
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—occur, in those too you are the giver of wealth
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O Indra, worthy of the invocation of many
- पार्थिवः (*pārthivaḥ*)—belonging to the earth
- विश्वः अयं (*viśvaḥ ayaṃ*)—all these men
- तव अवस्युः (*tava avasyuḥ*)—desiring your protection
- नाम (*nāma*)—food and the like
- भिक्षते (*bhikṣate*)—ask for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are renowned as the giver of wealth to all sacrificers. In whatever renowned battles take place, you are the giver of wealth in them too. O Indra, worthy of the invocation of many, all men belonging to the earth, desiring your protection, ask for food and the like.

### Printed p. 117

##### English translation
You are celebrated as the giver of wealth to all, even where battles occur : all the people of the earth, desirous of protection, solicit you, the invoked of many.

#### Ṛk 18

**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र॒ याव॑त॒स्त्वमे॒ताव॑द॒हमीशी॑य ।  
> स्तो॒तार॒मिद्दि॑धिषेय रदावसो॒ न पा॑प॒त्वाय॑ रासीय ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । यावतः । त्वं । एतावत् । अहं । ईशीय ।  
> स्तोतारं । इत् । दिधिषेय । रदवसो इति रदवसो । न । पापत्वाय । रासीय ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यद्यतो यावतो धनस्य त्वमीशिषे एतावत् ॥ षष्ठ्या लुक् ॥ एतावतो धनस्याहमीशीय ईश्वरो भवेयं हे रदवसो । रदति ददाति वसूनीति रदवसुः । तथोऽहमस्मदीयं स्तोतारमिद्दिधिषेय । धनप्रदानेन धारयेयमेव । पापत्वाय न रासीय । न दद्यां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, of as much wealth as you are lord, of so much wealth may I be the lord, O रदवसो (*radavaso*); रदवसुः (*radavasuḥ*) means one who gives riches. So I would support our praiser by giving wealth. I would not give for the sake of wickedness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रदवसो (*radavaso*)—O wealthy one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—in whatever manner
- यावतः (*yāvataḥ*)—of whatever wealth
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you are the lord
- एतावत् (*etāvat*)—in the same manner, of all that wealth
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- ईशीय (*īśīya*)—if I were the lord
- स्तोतारमित् (*stotāramit*)—for praisers alone
- दिधिषेय (*didhiṣeya*)—I would be a supporter by giving wealth
- पापत्वाय (*pāpatvāya*)—for sinful deeds
- न रासीय (*na rāsīya*)—surely I would not give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, in whatever manner you are lord of whatever wealth, if I too were lord of all that wealth in the same manner, I would be the supporter of praisers alone by giving wealth. For sinful deeds I would surely not give.

##### English translation
If I were lord of as much (affluence) as you are, Indra, then might I support (your) worshippers, dispenser of wealth, and not squander it upon wickedness.

### Printed p. 118

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शिक्षे॑य॒मिन्म॑हय॒ते दि॒वेदि॑वे रा॒य आ कु॑हचि॒द्विदे॑ ।  
> न॒हि त्वद॒न्यन्म॑घवन्न॒ आप्यं॒ वस्यो॒ अस्ति॑ पि॒ता च॒न ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शिक्षेयं । इत् । महयते । दिवेदिवे । रायः । आ । कुहचित्विदे ।  
> नहि । त्वत् । अन्यत् । मघवन् । नः । आप्यं । वस्यः । अस्ति । पिता । चन ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कुहचिद्विदे । कुत्रचिद्विद्यमानः कुहचिद्वित् । तस्मै । यत्र क्वापि विद्यमानायेत्यर्थः । महयते पूजयते जनाय दिवे दिवे प्रतिदिनं रायो धनानि शिक्षेयमित् । दद्यामेव । आकारः पूरणः । एवमिंद्रस्य वाक्यं श्रुत्वा संतुष्ट ऋषिर्वदति । हे मघवन् त्वत्तोऽन्यदस्माकमाप्यं ज्ञातेयं न ह्यस्ति । वस्यः प्रशस्यः पिता चन पालयिता च त्वदन्यो नास्तीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: कुहचिद्विदे (*kuhacidvide*) means one who exists somewhere, that is, to one who exists anywhere at all. To the worshipper I would give wealth day after day; शिक्षेयमित् (*śikṣeyamit*) means "I would surely give", and the आ (*ā*) is an expletive. Hearing thus the word of Indra, the pleased seer says: O Maghavan, we have no other kin than you, and no other excellent, praiseworthy protector, like a father, than you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कुहचिद्विदे (*kuhacidvide*)—wherever he may be
- महयते (*mahayate*)—to the sacrificer who is a worshipper
- दिवे दिवे (*dive dive*)—every day
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- आ शिक्षेयमित् (*ā śikṣeyamit*)—I shall surely give (Indra declares)
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- त्वत् (*tvat*)—than you
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—other
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—benefactors
- नहि अस्ति (*nahi asti*)—there are none
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*)—excellent
- पिता चन (*pitā cana*)—nor is there a protector

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer, hearing the word of Indra, "Wherever the sacrificer who is a worshipper may be, I shall surely give him riches every day", speaks thus: "O wealthy Indra, we have no other benefactors than you. We have no excellent protector like you."

##### English translation
May I daily distribute wealth to the venerable wherever abiding : no other, Maghavan, than you is to be sought by us: (no other is to us) a most excellent protector.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त॒रणि॒रित्सि॑षासति॒ वाजं॒ पुरं॑ध्या यु॒जा ।  
> आ व॒ इंद्रं॑ पुरुहू॒तं न॑मो गि॒रा ने॒मिं तष्टे॑व सु॒द्र्वं॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तरणिः । इत् । सिसासति । वाजं । पुरंध्या । युजा ।  
> आ । वः । इंद्रं । पुरुहूतं । नमे । गिरा । नेमिं । तष्टाइव । सुद्र्वं ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तरणिरित् स्तुत्यादौ कर्मणि त्वरित एव पुमान् पुरंध्या महत्या धिया युजा सहायभूतया वाजमन्नं सिषासति । संभजते । पुरुहूतं बहुभिराहूतमिंद्रं वस्त्वां गिरा स्तुत्यादिना नमो नमनेन नेमिं चक्रस्य वलयं सुद्र्वं शोभनदारुं तष्टेव । यथा वर्धकिर्दारुनेमिमानमुंयते तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: the man who is prompt in works such as praise obtains food, with great intelligence as his helper and companion. **NOTE** To Indra, invoked by many, I bow with praise and the like, with homage, as a carpenter bends good wood for the felly, the rim of a wheel.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तरणिरित् (*taraṇirit*)—only he who is engaged in works of praise and the like
- पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*)—with great intelligence
- युजा (*yujā*)—joined
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सिषासति (*siṣāsati*)—obtains
- तष्टाइव (*taṣṭāiva*)—as a carpenter
- नेमिं (*nemiṃ*)—as a ring for the wheel
- सुद्र्वं (*sudrvaṃ*)—bends good wood
- पुरुहूतं (*puruhūtaṃ*)—worthy of the invocation of many
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—and lord of all
- वः (*vaḥ*)—in front of you
- गिरा (*girā*)—offering praise
- आ नमो (*ā namo*)—I bow and salute

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Only he who is engaged in works of praise and the like, joined with great intelligence, obtains food. As a carpenter bends good wood as a ring for the wheel, so I, offering praise, bow and salute in front of you, who are worthy of the invocation of many and the lord of all.

##### English translation
The prompt offerer (of praise), with solemn rites combined, acquires food : I bend down with adoration to you, Indra, the invoked of many, as a carpenter bends the wooden circumference of the wheel.

### Printed p. 120

#### Ṛk 21

**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न दु॑ष्टु॒ती मर्त्यो॑ विंदते॒ वसु॒ न स्रेधं॑तं र॒यिर्न॑शत् ।  
> सु॒शक्ति॒रिन्म॑घव॒न्तुभ्यं॒ माव॑ते दे॒ष्णं यत्पार्ये॑ दि॒वि ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । दुःस्तुती । मर्त्यः । विंदते । वसु । न । स्रेधंतं । रयिः । नशत् ।  
> सुशक्तिः । इत् । मघवन् । तुभ्यं । मावते । देष्णं । यत् । पार्ये । दिवि ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मर्त्यो मनुष्यो दुःस्तुती दुःस्तुत्या वसु धनं न विंदते । इंद्रं स्तुवन्नेव वसु लभत इत्यर्थः । स्रेधंतं हिंसंतं इंद्रविषये स्तुत्यादिकर्माण्यकुर्वंतमित्यर्थः । रयिर्धनं न नशत् । न व्याप्नोति । हे मघवन् त्वया पार्ये दिवि सौत्ये दिवसे मावते मत्सदृशाय देष्णं दातव्यं यद्धनमस्ति तत्तुभ्यं त्वत्तः सुशक्तिरित् सुकर्मैव । विंदत इति व्यवहितमत्रानुषज्यतेऽध्याहारस्यांतिकत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: a mortal, a man, does not find wealth by ill praise; that is, only one who praises Indra gains wealth. Wealth does not reach one who harms, that is, one who performs no praise and the like in respect of Indra. O Maghavan, whatever wealth is to be given by you, on the day of the Soma pressing, to one like me, that wealth from you only one of good works obtains; the verb "obtains" is carried over from the preceding because the word to be supplied is near.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—a man
- दुःस्तुती (*duḥstutī*)—by praise joined with ill speech
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- न विंदते (*na viṃdate*)—does not obtain
- स्रेधंतं (*sredhaṃtaṃ*)—a man who does harm
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—wealth
- न नशत् (*na naśat*)—does not go and reach
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- पार्ये दिवि (*pārye divi*)—on the very day of the Soma offering
- मावते (*māvate*)—to a sacrificer like me
- देष्णं (*deṣṇaṃ*)—as fit to be given
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever wealth there is, that
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—from you
- सुशक्तिरित् (*suśaktirit*)—only one of good works can obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, a man does not obtain wealth by praise joined with ill speech. Wealth does not go and reach a man who does harm. O wealthy Indra, on the very day of the Soma offering, whatever wealth there is that is fit to be given to a sacrificer like me, only one of good works can obtain it from you.

##### English translation
A man acquires not wealth by unbecoming praise : affluence devolves not upon one obstructing (sacrifice): in you, Maghavan, is the power whereby bounty (may be shown) to such as I ain on the day of the libation.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि त्वा॑ शूर नोनु॒मोऽदु॑ग्धा इव धे॒नवः॑ ।  
> ईशा॑नम॒स्य जग॑तः स्व॒र्दृश॒मीशा॑नमिंद्र त॒स्थुषः॑ ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । त्वा । शूर । नोनुमः । अदुग्धाःइव । धेनवः ।  
> ईशानं । अस्य । जगतः । स्वःदृशं । ईशानं । इंद्र । तस्थुषः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूरेंद्र अस्य जगतो जंगमस्येशानमीश्वरं तस्थुषः स्थावरस्य चेशानं । ईशानमिति पदस्यावृत्तिरादरार्था । स्वर्दृशं सर्वदृशं त्वा त्वामदुग्धा इव धेनवो यथादुग्धा धेनवः क्षीरपूर्णोधस्त्वेन वर्तंते तद्वत्सोमपूर्णचमसत्वेन वर्तमाना वयमभि नोनुमः । भृशमभिष्टुमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O hero Indra, you are the lord (ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)) of this moving world and also of what stands still (तस्थुषः (*tasthuṣaḥ*)). The word ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*) is repeated out of respect. स्वर्दृशं (*svardṛśaṃ*) means 'all-seeing'. As unmilked cows (अदुग्धाःइव । धेनवः (*adugdhāḥiva | dhenavaḥ*)) have udders full of milk, so we, holding cups (चमस (*camasa*)) full of Soma, praise you vehemently (अभि नोनुमः (*abhi nonumaḥ*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्य जगतः (*asya jagataḥ*)—of this moving world
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—you who are the lord
- तस्थुषः (*tasthuṣaḥ*)—of stationary things also
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—you who are the lord
- स्वर्दृशं (*svardṛśaṃ*)—who can see the whole world
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अदुग्धा इव (*adugdhā iva*)—like cows not yet milked
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—cows having udders full of milk (so we also, holding cups full of Soma)
- अभिनोनुमः (*abhinonumaḥ*)—we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, lord of this moving world and lord of stationary things as well, who can see the whole world: as cows before milking have udders full of milk, so we also, holding cups full of Soma, praise you.

##### English translation
We glorify you, hero, (Indra) the lord of all moveable and stationary things, the beholder of the universe, (with ladles filled with Soma), like (the udders of) unmilked cows.
#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न त्वावा॑ अ॒न्यो दि॒व्यो न पार्थि॑वो॒ न जा॒तो न ज॑निष्यते ।

### Printed p. 122

> अश्वायंतो मघवन्निंद्र वाजिनो गव्यंतस्त्वा हवामहे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । त्वावान् । अन्यः । दिव्यः । न । पार्थिवः । न । जातः । न । जनिष्यते ।  
> अश्वयंतः । मघवन् । इंद्र । वाजिनः । गव्यंतः । त्वा । हवामहे ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन्निंद्र दिव्यो दिवि भवस्त्वावान् त्वत्सदृशोऽन्यो न जायते । पार्थिवः पृथिव्यां भवोऽपि त्वावानन्यो न जायते । दिव्यः पार्थिवो वा त्वावानन्यो न जातः । न च जनिष्यते । पृथिव्यां दिवि च त्रिष्वपि लोकेषु त्वत्सदृशः कश्चिन्नास्तीत्यर्थः । अश्वायंतोऽश्वानिच्छंतो वाजिनो वाजमिच्छंतः । इच्छायामिनिप्रत्ययः । हविष्मंतो वा गव्यंतो गा इच्छंतश्च वयं त्वा त्वां हवामहे । ह्वयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, possessor of wealth, no other like you is born who belongs to heaven (दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)); none belonging to the earth (पार्थिवः (*pārthivaḥ*)) is born like you either. Neither a heavenly nor an earthly one like you has been born, nor will be born. The meaning is that in all three worlds, on earth and in heaven, there is none like you. We, desiring horses (अश्वयंतः (*aśvayaṃtaḥ*)), desiring food (वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*); the affix *ini* is used in the sense of desire), or else bearing oblations, and desiring cows (गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*)), invoke you (हवामहे (*havāmahe*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)—one born in the world of the gods
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—another
- त्वावान् (*tvāvān*)—like you
- न जातः (*na jātaḥ*)—has not been born
- पार्थिवः (*pārthivaḥ*)—one born on earth
- न (*na*)—has not been born like you
- न जनिष्यते (*na janiṣyate*)—nor will be born
- अश्मायंतः (*aśmāyaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire horses
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—those who desire food
- गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*)—we who wish for cows
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray to and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, none among the gods born in the world of the gods is like you. Among men too none has been born. Nor will anyone be born hereafter. We, who desire horses, food and cows, pray to you and call you.

##### English translation
No other such as you are, celestial or terrestrial, has been or will be born ; desirous of horses, of food, of cattle, affluent Indra, we invoke you.
#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भी ष॒तस्तदा भ॒रेंद्र॒ ज्यायः॒ कनी॑यसः ।  
> पु॒रू॒वसु॒र्हि म॑घवन्स॒नादसि॒ भरे॑भरे च॒ हव्यः॑ ॥ २४ ॥

### Printed p. 123

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । सतः । तत् । आ । भर । इंद्र । ज्यायः । कनीयसः ।  
> पुरुवसुः । हि । मघवन् । सनात् । असि । भरेभरे । च । हव्यः ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ज्यायो ज्यायन्निंद्र ॥ आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदितींद्रपदस्याविद्यमानवद्भावात् ज्याये इत्यस्य सर्वानुदात्तत्वाभावः । नकारस्य रुत्वं व्यत्ययान्नमभावो वा ॥ कनीयसः सतो मम तत्प्रसिद्धं धनमभ्या भर । हे मघवन् त्वं सनाच्चिरादेवारभ्य पुरूवसुर्हि बहुधनो ह्यसि । भरेभरे संग्रामे यज्ञे वा हव्यो हविष्यश्चासि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O elder Indra (ज्यायः (*jyāyaḥ*)). Because the vocative is treated as previously non-existent, the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) counts as non-existent, and so ज्याये (*jyāye*) does not lose its accent entirely; the न (*na*) becomes रु (*ru*), or the न (*na*) is lost by variation. To me, who am the younger (कनीयसः (*kanīyasaḥ*)), bring (अभ्या भर (*abhyā bhara*)) that well-known wealth. O Maghavan, from of old (सनात् (*sanāt*)) you are possessed of much wealth (पुरुवसुः (*puruvasuḥ*)), and in every battle or sacrifice (भरेभरे (*bharebhare*)) you are one to be invoked and offered oblations (हव्यः (*havyaḥ*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ज्यायः (*jyāyaḥ*)—O one greater than all
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कनीयसः (*kanīyasaḥ*)—who am lesser than you
- मम (*mama*)—to me
- तत् (*tat*)—that well-known wealth
- अभ्याभर (*abhyābhara*)—provide
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- सनात् (*sanāt*)—from very ancient times
- पुरूवसुर्हि (*purūvasurhi*)—you are indeed possessed of abundant wealth
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- भरेभरे (*bharebhare*)—in every battle
- हव्यः च (*havyaḥ ca*)—and you are worthy of worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, greater than all, provide that well-known wealth to me, who am lesser than you. O wealthy Indra, from very ancient times you have been possessed of abundant wealth. In every battle you are also worthy of worship.

##### English translation
Elder Indra, bring that (wealth to me), being the junior, for, Maghavan, you have from the beginning been possessed of infinate treasure, and are to be adored at repeated sacrifices.

> अ॒स्माकं॑ बोध्यवि॒ता म॑हाध॒ने भवा॑ वृ॒धः सखी॑नां ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्माकं । बोधि । अविता । महाधने । भव । वृधः । सखीनां ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् परा पराचीनानमित्राञ्छत्रून्नुदस्व । प्रेरय । सोऽस्मभ्यं वसु वसूनि सुवेदा सुलभानि कृधि । कुरु । महाधने संग्रामे । वाजसातौ महाधने इति संग्रामनामसु पाठात् । सखीनां स्तोतॄणामस्माकं वसिष्ठानामविता रक्षिता बोधि । भव । वृधो वर्धयिता च भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maghavan, drive away (परा नुदस्व (*parā nudasva*); send off) the enemies (अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)) who turn away. Make riches (वसु (*vasu*)) easy to obtain (सुवेदा (*suvedā*)) for us (कृधि (*kṛdhi*): do). महाधने (*mahādhane*) means in battle, since in the list of battle-names वाजसातौ महाधने (*vājasātau mahādhane*) is read. Be (बोधि (*bodhi*): be) the protector (अविता (*avitā*)) of us, the friends (सखीनां (*sakhīnāṃ*)) and praisers, the Vasiṣṭhas, and be the increaser (वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—our enemies
- परा नुदस्व (*parā nudasva*)—drive far away
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वसु (*vasu*)—riches
- सुवेदा (*suvedā*)—so that they are easily obtained
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make
- महाधने (*mahādhane*)—in battles fought for abundant wealth
- सखीनां (*sakhīnāṃ*)—who are praisers
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—to us
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know that you should be
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—as one who makes us prosper
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, drive our enemies far away. Make riches easy for us to obtain. Know that in battles fought to win abundant wealth you are to be the protector of us, the praisers. Be also the one who makes us prosper.

##### English translation
Drive away, Maghavan, our enemies : render riches easy of acquisition : be our preserver in war : be the augmenter of (the prosperity) of (your) friends.

> शिक्ष । नः । अस्मिन् । पुरुहूत । यामनि । जीवाः । ज्योतिः । अशीमहि ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र नोऽस्मभ्यं क्रतुं कर्म प्रज्ञानं वा भर । आहर । अपि च यथा
> पिता पुत्रेभ्यो धनं प्रयच्छति तथा नोऽस्मभ्यं शिक्ष । धनं देहि । हे पुरुहूत
> बहुभिराहूत यामनि यज्ञे जीवा वयं ज्योतिः सूर्यमशीमहि । प्रतिदिनं
> प्राप्नुयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, bring (भर (*bhara*): fetch) to us क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*), that is, work or knowledge. And as a father gives wealth to his sons, so give (शिक्ष (*śikṣa*): give wealth) to us. O Indra invoked by many (पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)), in this sacrifice (यामनि (*yāmani*)) may we, living (जीवाः (*jīvāḥ*)), obtain (अशीमहि (*aśīmahi*)) the light (ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)), the sun, every day."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—knowledge concerning ritual
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—provide
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way in which
- पिता (*pitā*)—a father
- पुत्रेभ्यः (*putrebhyaḥ*)—gives wealth to his sons, so
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—give wealth
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O Indra, worthy of the invocation of many
- अस्मिन् यामनि (*asmin yāmani*)—in this sacrifice
- जीवाः (*jīvāḥ*)—we who are engaged (in it)
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the light of the sun
- अशीमहि (*aśīmahi*)—may we obtain every day

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, provide us with knowledge concerning ritual. As a father gives wealth to his sons, give us wealth. O Indra, worthy of the invocation of many, may we who are engaged in this sacrifice obtain the light of the sun every day.

##### English translation
Bring to us, Indra, wisdom, as a father (gives knowledge) to his sons ; bestow wealth upon us on this occasion, you the invoked of many, so that we, living at the solemnity, may (long) enjoy the light (of existence).

> त्वया॑ व॒यं प्र॒वतः॒ शश्व॑तीर॒पोऽति॑ शूर तरामसि ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । नः । अज्ञाताः । वृजनाः । दुःआध्यः । मा । अशिवासः । अव । क्रमुः ।  
> त्वया । वयं । प्रवतः । शश्वतीः । अपः । अति । शूर । तरामसि ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अज्ञाता अज्ञातगमना वृजना हिंसका दुराध्यो नोऽस्मान्नाव
> क्रमुः । मावचिक्रमुः । हे शूर त्वया वयं वसिष्ठाः प्रवतः प्रवणकाः संतः शश्वतीर्बह्वीरपोऽति तरामसि । अतितराम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, let no unknown (अज्ञाता (*ajñātā*): of unknown movement), harmful (वृजना (*vṛjanā*)) evil-minded ones (दुराध्यः (*durādhyaḥ*)) overpower us (अव क्रमुः (*ava kramuḥ*): let them not overstep). O hero, we Vasiṣṭhas, with you, being possessed of a means of crossing (प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*): प्रवणकाः (*pravaṇakāḥ*)), may cross over (अति तरामसि (*ati tarāmasi*)) many waters (शश्वतीः अपः (*śaśvatīḥ apaḥ*))."
