##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) अज्ञाताः (*ajñātāḥ*)—those who move about without our knowing
- वृजनाः (*vṛjanāḥ*)—our harmers
- दुराध्यः (*durādhyaḥ*)—those who wish us evil, our enemies
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा अव क्रमुः (*mā ava kramuḥ*)—let them not assail
- अशिवासः (*aśivāsaḥ*)—those who cause us inauspiciousness
- मा (*mā*)—let them not assail us
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—protected by you
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, born in the Vasiṣṭha lineage
- प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*)—possessing a means of crossing
- शश्वतीः (*śaśvatīḥ*)—abundant
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- अति तरामसि (*ati tarāmasi*)—may we cross over

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let our enemies, who move secretly without our knowing, who harm us and wish us evil, not assail us. Let those who cause us inauspiciousness not assail us either. O valiant Indra, may we, protected by you and born in the Vasiṣṭha lineage, possessing a means of crossing, cross over abundant waters.

##### English translation
Let no unknown, wicked, malevolent, malignant (enemies) overpower us : may we, protected by you, cross over many waters.
## Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्वित्यंचे इति चतुर्दशर्चं षोडशं सूक्तं । आत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । श्वित्यंचः षळॊना संस्तवो वसिष्ठस्य सपुत्रस्येंद्रेण वा संवाद इति । आदितो नवानां वसिष्ठ ऋषिः । वसिष्ठपुत्राणां स्तूयमानत्वात्त एव देवता । विद्युतो ज्योतिरित्यादिभिर्दशम्यादिभिः स्वपुत्रैर्वसिष्ठः स्तूयते । अतो वसिष्ठो देवता । त एव ऋषयः । यो तेनोच्यते इति न्यायात् । अनुक्तत्वात्त्रिष्टुप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning श्वित्यंचे (*śvityaṃce*) has fourteen verses and is the sixteenth sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā (आत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका (*ātreyamanukramaṇikā*)) **NOTE** says: श्वित्यंचः षळॊना संस्तवो वसिष्ठस्य सपुत्रस्येंद्रेण वा संवाद इति (*śvityaṃcaḥ ṣaḷònā saṃstavo vasiṣṭhasya saputrasyeṃdreṇa vā saṃvāda iti*). For the first nine verses Vasiṣṭha is the seer. Because the sons of Vasiṣṭha are praised in them, they themselves are the deity. In the verses from the tenth on, beginning विद्युतो ज्योतिः (*vidyuto jyotiḥ*), Vasiṣṭha is praised by his own sons; hence Vasiṣṭha is the deity, and the sons are the seers, by the maxim यो तेनोच्यते (*yo tenocyate*) **NOTE**. Since no metre is stated, it is Triṣṭubh.

##### Anuvāda

The thirty-third sūkta. This sūkta beginning श्वित्यंचे (*śvityaṃce*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has fourteen Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says श्वित्यंचः षळॊना संस्तवो वसिष्ठस्य सपुत्रस्येंद्रेण वा संवादः (*śvityaṃcaḥ ṣaḷònā saṃstavo vasiṣṭhasya saputrasyeṃdreṇa vā saṃvādaḥ*). For the first nine Ṛks of this sūkta Vasiṣṭha is the seer. Since the matter of Vasiṣṭha's sons is stated in these nine Ṛks, the praise of Vasiṣṭha's sons is the deity of these Ṛks. In the next five Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning विद्युतो ज्योतिः (*vidyuto jyotiḥ*), the sage Vasiṣṭha is the subject, so the praise of Vasiṣṭha is the deity of those Ṛks. The sons of Vasiṣṭha are the seers. The metre is Triṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 127
Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 33; Aṣṭaka 5, Adhyāya 2, Vargas 22, 23, 24. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 14. संस्तवो वसिष्ठस्य सपुत्रस्येंद्रेण वा संवादः (*saṃstavo vasiṣṭhasya saputrasyeṃdreṇa vā saṃvādaḥ*). Ṛṣi: Ṛks 1-9 Vasiṣṭha; 10-14 the sons of Vasiṣṭha. Devatā: Ṛks 1-9 the sons of Vasiṣṭha; 10-14 Vasiṣṭha. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्वि॒त्यंचो॑ मा दक्षिण॒तस्क॑पर्दा धियंजि॒न्वासो॑ अ॒भि हि प्र॑मं॒दुः ।  
> उ॒त्तिष्ठ॑न्वोचे॒ परि॑ ब॒र्हिषो॒ न्यान्न मे॑ दू॒रादवि॑तवे॒ वसि॑ष्ठाः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्वित्यंचः । मा । दक्षिणतःकपर्दाः । धियंजिन्वासः । अभि । हि । प्रमंदुः ।  
> उत्तिष्ठन् । वोचे । परि । बर्हिषः । नॄन् । न । मे । दूरात् । अवितवे । वसिष्ठाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्वित्यंचः । श्वित्यं श्वेतवर्णमंचंतीति श्वित्यंचः । श्वेतवर्णा इत्यर्थः । धियंजिन्वासः कर्मणां पूरयितारो दक्षिणतस्कपर्दाः । दक्षिणे शिरसो भागे कपर्दाश्चूडा येषां ते दक्षिणतस्कपर्दाः । चूडाकर्मणि दक्षिणतो वसिष्ठानामिति स्मर्यते । मा मामभि प्रमंदुः । विद्याबलेनाभिप्रहर्षयन् । यतो मामभि प्रमंदुरतो बर्हिषो यज्ञात् । परीति पंचम्यर्थानुवादः । उत्तिष्ठन्नहं न्यान्यज्ञस्य नेतृन्वोचे । ब्रवीमि । मे मत्तो दूराद्वसिष्ठा वसिष्ठस्य मम पुत्रा आवितवे गंतुं नार्हंतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

श्वित्यंचः (*śvityaṃcaḥ*): those who go to (are) white-coloured, that is, white in colour. धियंजिन्वासः (*dhiyaṃjinvāsaḥ*): those who fulfil rites. दक्षिणतस्कपर्दाः (*dakṣiṇataskapardāḥ*): those whose tufts (cūḍā) are on the right part of the head; it is recalled in the tonsure rite, "on the right for the Vasiṣṭhas". मा मामभि प्रमंदुः (*mā māmabhi pramaṃduḥ*): they have delighted me by the power of their learning. Because they have delighted me, I, rising up from the sacred grass (the sacrifice), call the leaders of the rite; the word परि (*pari*) merely restates the ablative sense. The Vasiṣṭhas, my sons, are not fit to go far from me (this is to be supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्वित्यंचः (*śvityaṃcaḥ*)—those of white colour
- धियंजिन्वासः (*dhiyaṃjinvāsaḥ*)—those who fully carry out rites
- दक्षिणतस्कपर्दाः (*dakṣiṇataskapardāḥ*)—(my sons) who have the tuft on the right side of the head
- मा (*mā*)—me
- अभिप्रमंदुः (*abhipramaṃduḥ*)—have gladdened by their learning
- बर्हिषः परि (*barhiṣaḥ pari*)—from the place of sacrifice
- उत्तिष्ठन् (*uttiṣṭhan*)—rising
- न्यान् (*nyān*)—those leaders of the sacrifice
- वोचे (*voce*)—I call
- मे (*me*)—than me
- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—in a distant place
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—the sons of Vasiṣṭha
- अवितवे (*avitave*)—to go away
- न हि (*na hi*)—I do not allow

### Printed p. 128

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Vāsiṣṭhas, white in colour, who fully carry out rites and have the tuft on the right side of the head, have gladdened me by their learning. After rising from the place of sacrifice I call them, the leaders of the sacrifice. I do not allow these sons of Vasiṣṭha to be in a place farther than I am, or to go away from here.

##### English translation
The white-complexioned accomplishers of holy ceremonies, wearing the lock of hair on the right side, have afforded me delight, when, rising up, I call the leaders (of rites) to the sacred grass : the Vasishthas, (my sons) should never be far from me.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this sūkta a matter in the form of a dialogue between the sage Vasiṣṭha and his sons, or Indra, is stated. In Ṛks 1-9 the sage Vasiṣṭha speaks of his sons; in Ṛks 10-14 the sons of Vasiṣṭha speak of their father, the sage Vasiṣṭha.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दू॒रादिंद्र॑मनय॒न्ना सु॒तेन॑ ति॒रो वै॑शं॒तमति॒ पांत॑मु॒ग्रं ।  
> पाश॑द्युम्नस्य वाय॒ुतस्य॒ सोमा॑त्सु॒तादिंद्रो॑ऽवृणीता॒ वसि॑ष्ठान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दूरात् । इंद्रं । अनयन् । आ । सुतेन । तिरः । वैशंतं । अति । पांतं । उग्रं ।  
> पाशद्युम्नस्य । वायतस्य । सोमात् । सुतात् । इंद्रः । अवृणीत । वसिष्ठान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदा वसिष्ठस्य पुत्राः सुदासं राजानमयोजयन् तदैव पाशद्युम्नाख्योऽपि राजा सोमास्यष्टमुद्यमं चकार । तदा ते वसिष्ठपुत्राः पाशद्युम्नं तिरस्कृत्य तदीयो यागे सोमं पिबंतमिंद्रं मंत्रबलेन तस्मादाच्छिद्य सुदासो यज्ञे स्थापयामासुः । तदेतद्वृत्तांतं कीर्तयन् वसिष्ठः स्वसुताननेन मंत्रेण स्तौति ॥ वैशंतं । वेशंतः पल्वलं । अत्र वेशंतशब्देन सोमाधारक्षुद्रसरो लक्ष्यते । तत्स्थं सोमं पांतं पिबंतमुग्रमुद्गूर्णमिंद्रं सुतेन सुदासो यज्ञेऽभिषुतेन सोमेन हेतुना तिरः पाशद्युम्नं तिरस्कृत्य दूरादानयन् । वसिष्ठा मंत्रबले-

### Printed p. 129

> नानीतवंतः । इंद्रोऽपि वायतस्य वयतः पुत्रस्य पाशद्युम्नस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । वायतं पाशद्युम्नमत्यतिहाय सुदासो यज्ञेऽभिषुतात्सोमाद्देशोर्वसिष्ठान्वसिष्ठस्य पुत्रानवृणीत । पाशद्युम्नस्य सोमयागे चमसस्थं सोमं पिबन्नपींद्रस्तं पाशद्युम्नं तिरस्कृत्य मंत्रसामर्थ्यबलेन सुदासो यज्ञ आहवनकाले वसिष्ठानाजगामेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the sons of Vasiṣṭha engaged King Sudās in the sacrifice, the king named Pāśadyumna also undertook a Soma sacrifice. Then the sons of Vasiṣṭha slighted Pāśadyumna and, by the power of their mantra, took Indra, who was drinking Soma at his sacrifice, away from him and established him at Sudās's sacrifice. Vasiṣṭha praises his sons with this mantra, telling that event. वैशंतं (*vaiśaṃtaṃ*): वेशंतः (*veśaṃtaḥ*) is a small pool; here the word वेशंत (*veśaṃta*) denotes the small lake that holds the Soma. Indra, fierce and uplifted, was drinking the Soma in it; because of the Soma pressed at Sudās's sacrifice, they brought him from afar, slighting Pāśadyumna; the Vasiṣṭhas brought him by the power of the mantra. Indra too, leaving aside Pāśadyumna, the son of Vayata (the genitive is in the sense of the accusative), chose the sons of Vasiṣṭha, from the Soma pressed at Sudās's sacrifice. The meaning: though Indra was drinking the Soma in the cup at Pāśadyumna's Soma sacrifice, he slighted him and, by the strength of the mantra's power, came to the Vasiṣṭhas at the time of the invocation at Sudās's sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वैशंतं (*vaiśaṃtaṃ*)—the Soma in the cup, deep like a pool
- पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)—who was drinking
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—and fearsome
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- सुतेन (*sutena*)—on account of the Soma pressed at Sudās's sacrifice
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—slighting Pāśadyumna
- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—from very far
- आ अनयन् (*ā anayan*)—they brought
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra, however
- वायतः (*vāyataḥ*)—the son of Payata **NOTE**
- पाशद्युम्नस्य (*pāśadyumnasya*)—Pāśadyumna
- अति (*ati*)—abandoning
- सोमात् (*somāt*)—for Sudās's Soma
- वसिष्ठान् (*vasiṣṭhān*)—the sons of Vasiṣṭha, his priests
- अवृणीत (*avṛṇīta*)—chose and followed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who was drinking the Soma in the cup deep like a pool and is fearsome, was brought from very far by them, slighting Pāśadyumna, on account of the Soma pressed at Sudās's sacrifice; abandoning Pāśadyumna, he chose and followed the sons of Vasiṣṭha, the priests of Sudās, for the sake of Sudās's Soma.

##### English translation
Disgracing (Pashadyumna), they brought from afar the fierce Indra, when drinking the ladle of Soma at his sacrifice, to (receive) the libation (of Sudas): Indra, hastened from the effused Soma of Pashadyumna, the son of Vayata to the Vashisthas.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वेन्नु कं॒ सिंधु॑मेभिस्ततारे॒वेन्नु कं॑ भे॒दमे॑भिर्जघान ।  
> ए॒वेन्नु कं॑ दाशरा॒ज्ञे सु॒दासं॒ प्राव॒दिंद्रो॒ ब्रह्म॑णा वो वसिष्ठाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 130

> एव । इत् । नु । कं । सिंधुं । एभिः । ततार । एव । इत् । नु । कं । भेदं । एभिः । जघान ।  
> एव । इत् । नु । कं । दाशराज्ञे । सुदासं । प्र । आवत् । इंद्रः । ब्रह्मणा । वः । वसिष्ठाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवेत् यथा पाशद्युम्नस्य सवाख्ये सोमयागे चमसस्थं सोमं पिबंतमपींद्रं वसिष्ठैः सुदाः प्राप्तान् एवमेव सिंधुं नदीमेभिर्वसिष्ठैः कं सुखेन ततार । तीर्ण आसीत् । स्विति पूरणः । तथा च निगमांतरं । अर्णांसि चित्प्रथाना सुदासे । ऋ. ७-१८-५ । इति । एवेदेवमेव भेदं भेदनामकं शत्रुमेभिर्वसिष्ठैरेव जघान । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । एवेदेवमेव हे वसिष्ठाः वो युष्मदीयेन ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेण दाशराज्ञे दशभि राजभिः सह युद्धे प्रवृत्ते सति सुदासं राजानमिंद्रः प्रावत् । प्रारक्षत् । तथा च निगमांतरं । दश राजानः समिता अयज्यवः सुदासमिंद्रावरुणा न युयुधुः । ऋ. ७-८३-७ । इति । दाशराज्ञे परियत्ताय विश्वतः । ऋ. ७-८३-८ । इति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

एवेत् (*evet*): just as Indra, drinking Soma from the cup at Pāśadyumna's Soma sacrifice, called "sava", was brought by the Vasiṣṭhas to Sudās, in just this way Sudās with these Vasiṣṭhas crossed the river Sindhu कं (*kaṃ*), easily; *svit* (नु (*nu*)) is a filler. Another text says so: अर्णांसि चित्प्रथाना सुदासे (*arṇāṃsi citprathānā sudāse*) (Ṛ. 7-18-5). In just this way he slew the enemy named Bheda through these very Vasiṣṭhas. Then comes direct address: in just this way, O Vasiṣṭhas, by your prayer (stotra), when the war with the ten kings began, Indra protected King Sudās. Another text says so: दश राजानः समिता अयज्यवः सुदासमिंद्रावरुणा न युयुधुः । (*daśa rājānaḥ samitā ayajyavaḥ sudāsamiṃdrāvaruṇā na yuyudhuḥ |*) (Ṛ. 7-83-7), and दाशराज्ञे परियत्ताय विश्वतः (*dāśarājñe pariyattāya viśvataḥ*) (Ṛ. 7-83-8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एवेत् (*evet*)—in this very manner
- एभिः (*ebhiḥ*)—with these Vasiṣṭhas
- सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)—the river Sindhu
- कं (*kaṃ*)—comfortably
- ततार नु (*tatāra nu*)—(Sudās) crossed
- एवेत् (*evet*)—in this same way
- एभिः (*ebhiḥ*)—by the help of these very Vasiṣṭhas
- भेदं (*bhedaṃ*)—the enemy named Bheda
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—he killed
- एवेत् (*evet*)—just so
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—O sages born in the Vasiṣṭha family
- वः (*vaḥ*)—recited by you
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—satisfied by the praise
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दाशराज्ञे (*dāśarājñe*)—in the war with ten kings
- सुदासं (*sudāsaṃ*)—Sudās
- प्रावत् (*prāvat*)—protected

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vasiṣṭhas, just as, by your power, Indra, though drinking Soma elsewhere, left that place for Sudās and came to Sudās, in the same way, with you, this Sudās crossed the river easily. By this help of yours he killed the enemy named Bheda. Likewise, satisfied by the praise recited by you, Indra protected this Sudās also in the war waged together with ten kings.

##### English translation
In the same manner was he, (Sudas), enabled by them easily to cross the Sindhu river : in the same manner, through them he easily slew his foe :

### Printed p. 131
so in like manner, Vasishthas, through your prayers, did Indra defend Sudas in the war with the ten kings.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जुष्टी॑ नरो॒ ब्रह्म॑णा वः पित्र्या॒णामक्ष॑मव्ययं॒ न किला॑ रिषाथ ।  
> यच्छक्व॑रीषु बृह॒ता रवे॒णेंद्रे॒ शुष्म॒मद॑धाता वसिष्ठाः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जुष्टी । नरः । ब्रह्मणा । वः । पितॄणां । अक्षं । अव्ययं । न । किल । रिषाथ ।  
> यत् । शक्वरीषु । बृहता । रवेण । इंद्रे । शुष्मं । अदधात । वसिष्ठाः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरः वो युष्मदीयेन ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेण पित्र्याणां जुष्टी प्रीतिर्भवति । पित्र्याणामित्यनेन पारोक्ष्येण वसिष्ठस्यैव कीर्तनं । अहं प्रीतो भवामीत्यर्थः । अथेदानीं स्वमाश्रमं गंतुमुद्यतोऽहमक्षं रथस्याक्षमव्ययं । व्ययामि ॥ लडर्थे लज् ॥ चालयामीत्यर्थः । यूयं न किल रिषाथ न च क्षीणा भवथ हे वसिष्ठाः यद्यस्माच्छक्वरीष्वृक्षु बृहता श्रेष्ठेन रवेण साम्नेंद्रे शुष्मं बलमदधात अधारयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, by your prayer (stotra) there is delight (जुष्टी (*juṣṭī*)) of the fathers' kin. By the word पित्र्याणां (*pitryāṇāṃ*), in an indirect manner, it is Vasiṣṭha himself who is spoken of: the meaning is "I am pleased". Now, being ready to go to my own hermitage, I set the axle of the chariot in motion (अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*) is व्ययामि (*vyayāmi*), लज् (*laj*) used in the sense of *laḍ*; the meaning is "I move it"). You, O Vasiṣṭhas, are not harmed and do not become diminished, because in the Śakvarī verses, by the great, best sound, the Sāman, you placed strength (शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)) in Indra. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—O Vasiṣṭhas, the leaders
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—by the praise alone
- पित्र्याणां (*pitryāṇāṃ*)—for the fathers
- जुष्टी (*juṣṭī*)—satisfaction arises
- अक्षं (*akṣaṃ*)—the axle of the chariot
- अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*)—I have set in motion
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—O sages born in the Vasiṣṭha line
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- शक्वरीषु (*śakvarīṣu*)—offered with the excellent metres called Śakvarī
- बृहता (*bṛhatā*)—and excellent
- रवेण (*raveṇa*)—by your Sāman chanting
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—in Indra
- शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)—strength
- अदधात (*adadhāta*)—you filled (therefore) न किल रिषाथ (*na kila riṣātha*)—do not waste any time

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O leaders, Vasiṣṭhas, by your praise alone satisfaction arises for the fathers. I have set the axle of the chariot in motion. O sages of the Vasiṣṭha line, by that greatness of yours, by which you filled Indra with strength through your excellent Sāman chanting, offered with the recitation of the excellent metres called Śakvarī, therefore do not waste any time.

### Printed p. 132

##### English translation
By your prayers, leaders (of rites), is effected the gratification of your progenitors : I have set in motion the axle (of the chariot) : be not you inert, for by your sacred metres, Vasishthas, (chaunted) with a loud voice, you sustain vigour in Indra.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद्द्यामि॒वेत्तृ॒ष्णजो॑ नाथि॒तासोऽदी॑धयुर्दाशरा॒ज्ञे वृ॒तासः॑ ।  
> वसि॑ष्ठस्य स्तुव॒त इंद्रो॑ अश्रोदु॒रुं तृत्सु॑भ्यो अकृणोदु लो॒कं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । द्याम्ऽइव । इत् । तृष्णजः । नाथितासः । अदीधयुः । दाशराज्ञे । वृतासः ।  
> वसिष्ठस्य । स्तुवतः । इंद्रः । अश्रोत् । उरुं । तृत्सुभ्यः । अकृणोत् । ऊं इति । लोकं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृष्णजो जाततृष्णा वृतासस्तृत्सुभी राजभिर्वृता नाथितासो वृष्टिं याचमाना वसिष्ठा द्यामिवादित्यमिवेंद्रं दाशराज्ञे दशानां राज्ञां संग्राम उददीधयुः । उददीधयन् । स्तुवतो वसिष्ठस्य स्तोत्रमिंद्रोऽश्रोत् । आशृणोच्च । उरुं विस्तीर्णं लोकं तृत्सुभ्यो राजभ्योऽकृणोत् । अकरोच्च । आददाच्चेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Vasiṣṭhas, thirsting (तृष्णजः (*tṛṣṇajaḥ*)), surrounded by the Tṛtsu kings (वृतासः (*vṛtāsaḥ*)), begging for rain (नाथितासः (*nāthitāsaḥ*)), made Indra shine forth like the heaven, that is, like the sun, in the war of the ten kings. Indra heard the praise of the praising Vasiṣṭha, and made a wide (extended) space for the Tṛtsu kings; he made it, and he took it. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तृष्णजः (*tṛṣṇajaḥ*)—those afflicted with thirst
- वृतासः (*vṛtāsaḥ*)—those surrounded by kings called Tṛtsu
- नाथितासः (*nāthitāsaḥ*)—the Vasiṣṭhas who were begging for rain
- दाशराज्ञे (*dāśarājñe*)—in the war with ten kings
- (Indra) द्यां इव (*dyāṃ iva*)—like the sun
- उददीधयुः (*udadīdhayuḥ*)—made to shine forth
- स्तुवतः (*stuvataḥ*)—who was praising
- वसिष्ठस्य (*vasiṣṭhasya*)—Vasiṣṭha's praise
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अश्रोत् (*aśrot*)—heard
- तृत्सुभ्यः (*tṛtsubhyaḥ*)—for the kings called Tṛtsu
- उरुं (*uruṃ*)—very extensive
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—a kingdom
- अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*)—made and gave

### Printed p. 133

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vasiṣṭha, who was parched with thirst, surrounded by the kings called Tritsus, and begging for rain, made Indra shine like the sun in the battle fought against the ten kings. Indra heard Vasiṣṭha's praise. He fashioned a very spacious kingdom for the kings called Tritsus.

##### English translation
Suffering from thirst, soliciting (rain), supported (by the Tritsus in the war with the ten Rajas, (the Vasishthas) made Indra radiant as the sun: Indra heard (the praises) of Vasishtha glorifying him, and bestowed a spacious region on the Tritsus.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दं॒डा इ॒वेद्गो॒ऽअज॑नास आस॒न्परि॑च्छिन्ना भर॒ता अ॑र्भ॒कासः॑ ।  
> अभ॑वच्च पुरए॒ता वसि॑ष्ठ॒ आदित्तृत्सू॑नां॒ विशो॑ अप्रथंत ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दंडाःऽइव । इत् । गोऽअजनासः । आसन् । परिऽछिन्नाः । भरताः । अर्भकासः ।  
> अभवत् । च । पुरःऽएता । वसिष्ठः । आत् । इत् । तृत्सूनां । विशः । अप्रथंत ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गोऽअजनासो गवां प्रेरका दंडा इव यथा दंडाः परिच्छिन्नपत्रोपशाखा भवंति तद्वद्भरताः । तृत्सूनामेव राज्ञां भरता इति नामांतरेणोपादानं । शत्रुभिः परिच्छिन्ना एवासन् । अर्भकासोऽर्भका अल्पाश्चासन् । आदित्परिच्छिन्नत्वादनंतरमेव तेषां तृत्सूनां वसिष्ठः पुरएता पुरोहितोऽभवच्च । तत्पुरोहित्यसामर्थ्यात्तृत्सूनां विशः प्रजाः अप्रथंत । आवर्धंत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Bharatas are like staves for driving cattle (गोऽअजनासः (*go 'ajanāsaḥ*), those who drive cows). Just as staves have their leaves and twigs stripped off all round, so the Bharatas were stripped all round by their enemies. "Bharatas" is another name used for the very kings who are the Tritsus. They were hemmed in by their enemies and they were few (अर्भकासः (*arbhakāsaḥ*)). Immediately after being thus stripped, Vasiṣṭha became their leader in front (पुरएता (*puraetā*)), their family priest. Through the power of his priesthood the subjects (विशः (*viśaḥ*)) of the Tritsus prospered; अप्रथंत (*aprathaṃta*) means "they grew".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गोअजनासः (*goajanāsaḥ*)—those who prepare to drive cattle
- दंडा इव (*daṃḍā iva*)—to staves: just as they have all leaves and the like stripped off and become bare
- भरताः (*bharatāḥ*)—these Bharatas (the Tritsus)
- परिच्छिन्ना इत् (*paricchinnā it*)—having their wealth completely carried off by enemies
- आसन् (*āsan*)—became; they also became very few
- अर्भकासः (*arbhakāsaḥ*)—very few
- आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately thereafter
- तृत्सूनां (*tṛtsūnāṃ*)—for these Tritsus
- वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*)—Vasiṣṭha
- पुरएता (*puraetā*)—as family priest
- अभवच्च (*abhavacca*)—became
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—(as a result) all their subjects
- अप्रथंत (*aprathaṃta*)—attained growth

### Printed p. 134

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Just as staves prepared for driving cattle have all their leaves and the like stripped off and are made bare, the Tritsus, their wealth completely carried off by enemies, became destitute. They also became very few. Immediately after that, Vasiṣṭha became family priest to these Tritsus. As a result all their subjects prospered.

##### English translation
The Bharatas, inferior (to their foes), were shorn (of their positions), like the staves for driving cattle, (stripped of their leaves and branches): but Vashistha became their family priest, and the people of the Tritsus prospered,

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रयः॑ कृण्वंति॒ भुव॑नेषु॒ रेत॑स्ति॒स्रः प्र॒जा आर्या॒ ज्योति॑रग्राः ।  
> त्रयो॑ घ॒र्मास॑ उ॒षसं॑ सचंते॒ सर्वा॒ इत्ता अनु॑ विदु॒र्वसि॑ष्ठाः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रयः । कृण्वंति । भुवनेषु । रेतः । तिस्रः । प्रजाः । आर्याः । ज्योतिःऽअग्राः ।  
> त्रयः । घर्मासः । उषसं । सचंते । सर्वान् । इत् । तान् । अनु । विदुः । वसिष्ठाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भुवनेषु पृथिव्यंतरिक्षद्युषु त्रयोऽग्निवायुसूर्या यथाक्रमेण रेतो विश्वस्य धारकमुदकं कृण्वंति । कुर्वंति । तेषां त्रयाणां ज्योतिरग्रा आदित्यप्रमुखा आर्याः श्रेष्ठास्तिस्रः प्रजा भवंति । ते च त्रयोऽग्निवायुसूर्या घर्मासो दीप्यमाना उषसं सचंते । समवयंति । दुर्ज्ञानात्सर्वानित्सर्वानेव तान्वसिष्ठा अनु विदुः । अभिजानंति । तेषां रहस्यविज्ञानादियमपि वसिष्ठानामेव स्तुतिः । तथा च शाट्यायनकं । त्रयः कृण्वंति भुवनेषु रेत इत्यग्निः पृथिव्यां रेतः कृणोति वायुरंतरिक्ष आदित्यो दिवि तिस्रः प्रजा आर्या ज्योतिरग्रा इति वसवो रुद्रा आदित्यास्तासां ज्योतिर्यदसावादित्यस्त्रयो घर्मास उषसं सचंत इत्यग्निरुषसं सचते वायुरुषसं सचत आदित्य उषसं सचत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the worlds, that is earth, atmosphere and heaven, the three, Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya respectively, produce रेतः (*retaḥ*), water, which sustains the universe. Of these three, the noble (आर्याः (*āryāḥ*)), excellent three classes of beings (प्रजाः (*prajāḥ*)), headed by the Āditya, who is their light, come into being. And those three, Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, shining (घर्मासः (*gharmāsaḥ*)), attend upon Uṣas. Because this is hard to know, the Vasiṣṭhas know all of them; hence this Ṛk is also a praise of the Vasiṣṭhas, who know their secret. Śāṭyāyanaka accordingly says: त्रयः कृण्वंति भुवनेषु रेतस्तिस्रः प्रजा आर्या ज्योतिरग्राः । त्रयो घर्मास उषसं सचंते सर्वा इत्ता अनु विदुर्वसिष्ठाः ॥ ७ ॥ त्रयः । कृण्वंति । भुवनेषु । रेतः । तिस्रः । प्रजाः । आर्याः । ज्योतिःऽअग्राः । त्रयः । घर्मासः । उषसं । सचंते । सर्वान् । इत् । तान् । अनु । विदुः । वसिष्ठाः ॥ भुवनेषु पृथिव्यंतरिक्षद्युषु त्रयोऽग्निवायुसूर्या यथाक्रमेण रेतो विश्वस्य धारकमुदकं कृण्वंति । कुर्वंति । तेषां त्रयाणां ज्योतिरग्रा आदित्यप्रमुखा आर्याः श्रेष्ठास्तिस्रः प्रजा भवंति । ते च त्रयोऽग्निवायुसूर्या घर्मासो दीप्यमाना उषसं सचंते । समवयंति । दुर्ज्ञानात्सर्वानित्सर्वानेव तान्वसिष्ठा अनु विदुः । अभिजानंति । तेषां रहस्यविज्ञानादियमपि वसिष्ठानामेव स्तुतिः । तथा च शाट्यायनकं । त्रयः कृण्वंति भुवनेषु रेत इत्यग्निः पृथिव्यां रेतः कृणोति वायुरंतरिक्ष आदित्यो दिवि तिस्रः प्रजा आर्या ज्योतिरग्रा इति वसवो रुद्रा आदित्यास्तासां ज्योतिर्यदसावादित्यस्त्रयो घर्मास उषसं सचंत इत्यग्निरुषसं सचते वायुरुषसं सचत आदित्य उषसं सचत इति ॥ (*trayaḥ kṛṇvaṃti bhuvaneṣu retastisraḥ prajā āryā jyotiragrāḥ | trayo gharmāsa uṣasaṃ sacaṃte sarvā ittā anu vidurvasiṣṭhāḥ ‖ 7 ‖ trayaḥ | kṛṇvaṃti | bhuvaneṣu | retaḥ | tisraḥ | prajāḥ | āryāḥ | jyotiḥ 'agrāḥ | trayaḥ | gharmāsaḥ | uṣasaṃ | sacaṃte | sarvān | it | tān | anu | viduḥ | vasiṣṭhāḥ ‖ bhuvaneṣu pṛthivyaṃtarikṣadyuṣu trayo 'gnivāyusūryā yathākrameṇa reto viśvasya dhārakamudakaṃ kṛṇvaṃti | kurvaṃti | teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ jyotiragrā ādityapramukhā āryāḥ śreṣṭhāstisraḥ prajā bhavaṃti | te ca trayo 'gnivāyusūryā gharmāso dīpyamānā uṣasaṃ sacaṃte | samavayaṃti | durjñānātsarvānitsarvāneva tānvasiṣṭhā anu viduḥ | abhijānaṃti | teṣāṃ rahasyavijñānādiyamapi vasiṣṭhānāmeva stutiḥ | tathā ca śāṭyāyanakaṃ | trayaḥ kṛṇvaṃti bhuvaneṣu reta ityagniḥ pṛthivyāṃ retaḥ kṛṇoti vāyuraṃtarikṣa ādityo divi tisraḥ prajā āryā jyotiragrā iti vasavo rudrā ādityāstāsāṃ jyotiryadasāvādityastrayo gharmāsa uṣasaṃ sacaṃta ityagniruṣasaṃ sacate vāyuruṣasaṃ sacata āditya uṣasaṃ sacata iti ‖*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुवनेषु (*bhuvaneṣu*)—in the three worlds, earth and the rest
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—the three, Agni, Vāyu and Āditya
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—water
- कृण्वंति (*kṛṇvaṃti*)—produce. (Among these three also)

### Printed p. 135

- ज्योतिरग्राः (*jyotiragrāḥ*)—those headed by the Āditya
- आर्याः (*āryāḥ*)—and excellent
- तिस्रः प्रजाः (*tisraḥ prajāḥ*)—the three, Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas, become manifest
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—these three
- घर्मासः (*gharmāsaḥ*)—shining
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the goddess Uṣas
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—attend upon
- तान् सर्वान् इत् (*tān sarvān it*)—all those
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—the Vasiṣṭha family
- अनु विदुः (*anu viduḥ*)—have known as they truly are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the three worlds, earth and the rest, the three, Agni, Vāyu and Āditya, produce water. Among these three, the three classes of beings, the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas, headed by the Āditya and excellent, become manifest. These three, shining, attend upon the goddess Uṣas. The Vasiṣṭhas have known all of them as they truly are.

##### English translation
Three shed moisture upon the regions, three are their glorious progeny, of which the chief is night : three communicators of warmth accompany the dawn : verily the Vashisthas understand all these.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सूर्य॑स्येव व॒क्षथो॒ ज्योति॑रेषां समु॒द्रस्ये॑व महि॒मा ग॑भी॒रः ।  
> वात॑स्येव प्रज॒वो नान्येन॒ स्तोमो॑ वसिष्ठा॒ अन्वे॑तवे वः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सूर्यस्यऽइव । वक्षथः । ज्योतिः । एषां । समुद्रस्यऽइव । महिमा । गभीरः ।  
> वातस्यऽइव । प्रजवः । न । अन्येन । स्तोमः । वसिष्ठाः । अनुऽएतवे । वः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसिष्ठाः एषां वो युष्माकं स्तोमो महिमापि वा सूर्यस्य ज्योतिरिव वक्षथः प्रकाशोऽस्ति । हे वसिष्ठाः वो युष्माकं महिमा स्तोमोऽपि वा समुद्रस्येव गभीरो गंभीरोऽस्ति । तथा हे वसिष्ठाः एषां वो युष्माकं स्तोम ऋक्समूहो महिमापि वा वातस्येव प्रजवो यथा वातस्य प्रवेगोऽन्येनान्वेतुं न शक्यस्तद्वदन्येनान्वेतवेऽन्वेतुं न शक्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasiṣṭhas, the praise (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)) of you, or your greatness (महिमा (*mahimā*)), shines like the light of the sun (वक्षथः (*vakṣathaḥ*), brightness). O Vasiṣṭhas, your greatness, or your praise, is deep (गभीरः (*gabhīraḥ*)) like the ocean. And your praise, the collection of Ṛks, or your greatness, has the swiftness (प्रजवः (*prajavaḥ*)) of the wind: as the rush of the wind cannot be followed by another, so this cannot be followed, that is, matched, by any other.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—O Vasiṣṭhas
- एषां वः (*eṣāṃ vaḥ*)—of you, the renowned
- महिमा (*mahimā*)—greatness
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- ज्योतिःइव (*jyotiḥiva*)—like the radiance
- वक्षथः (*vakṣathaḥ*)—shines
- समुद्रस्येव (*samudrasyeva*)—like the ocean
- गभीरः (*gabhīraḥ*)—is profound
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—your praise
- वातस्येव (*vātasyeva*)—

### Printed p. 136

- like the wind
- प्रजवः (*prajavaḥ*)—is swift
- अन्येन (*anyena*)—by any others (by other praises)
- अन्वेतवे (*anvetave*)—to surpass it
- न (*na*)—is not possible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vasiṣṭhas, the greatness of you, the renowned, shines like the radiance of the sun. It is profound like the ocean. Your praise is swift like the wind. It cannot be surpassed by the praises of others.

##### English translation
The glory of these Vashisthas is like the splendour of the sun : their greatness as profound as (the depth of) the ocean : your praise, Vashisthas has the velocity of the wind : by no other can it be surpassed.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska says that in the Ṛgveda mantras not only deities but also Pitṛs and Ṛṣis are praised, and he gives this Ṛk, which describes the praise of the Ṛṣis, as an example (Ni. 11-20). In this Ṛk there is a description of the greatness of the sage Vasiṣṭha and of the Vasiṣṭha family, the sons of Vasiṣṭha and others.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त इन्नि॒ण्यं हृद॑यस्य प्रके॒तैः स॒हस्र॑वल्यम॒भि सं च॑रंति ।  
> य॒मेन॑ त॒तं प॑रि॒धिं वयं॑तोऽप्स॒रस॒ उप॑ सेदु॒र्वसि॑ष्ठाः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । इत् । निण्यं । हृदयस्य । प्रकेतैः । सहस्रऽवल्शं । अभि । सं । चरंति ।  
> यमेन । ततं । परिधिं । वयंतः । अप्सरसः । उप । सेदुः । वसिष्ठाः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त इत्त एव वसिष्ठा निण्यं तिरोहितं दुर्ज्ञानं । निण्यं सस्वरित्यंतर्हितनामसु पाठात् । सहस्रवल्यं सहस्रशाखं संसारं हृदयस्य प्रकेतैः प्रज्ञानैरभि सं चरंति । एवं स्वाच्छंद्येनाभिसंचरंतस्ते वसिष्ठा यमेन कारणात्मना सर्वनियंत्रा ततं विस्तृतं परिधिं वस्त्रं । परिधिरित्यनेन जन्मादिप्रवाहो विवक्षितः । तं वयंतोऽप्सरसो जननीत्वेनोप सेदुः । अत्र वसिष्ठा इति बहुवचनं पूजायां । वसिष्ठः पूर्वं प्रजापतेरुत्पन्नं देहमुत्सृज्याप्सरःसु जायेयेति बुद्धिमकरोदिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those very Vasiṣṭhas move about, with the insights (प्रकेतैः (*praketaiḥ*)) of the heart, in the hidden (निण्यं (*niṇyaṃ*), concealed, hard to know) thousand-branched saṃsāra; he notes that निण्यं (*niṇyaṃ*) is read among the names meaning "hidden". Thus roaming at will, those Vasiṣṭhas, weaving the garment (परिधिं (*paridhiṃ*)) spread out by Yama, who as the causal self controls all, approached the Apsarases as mothers. By "garment" the stream of birth and the rest is meant. The plural *Vasiṣṭhas* is used in honour. The sense is that Vasiṣṭha, formerly born of Prajāpati, gave up that body and conceived the thought "may I be born among the Apsarases".

- निण्यं (*niṇyaṃ*)—the saṃsāra that is secret, beyond the knowledge of others

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those very Vasiṣṭhas, of great glory, with the insights of their heart enter and move about everywhere in the saṃsāra, which is secret, beyond the knowledge of others, and has thousands of branches. They entered the stream of birth and the rest, spread out widely by Yama, the controller of the world, and were born in the womb of an Apsaras.

##### English translation
By the wisdom seated in the heart the Vashisthas traverse the hidden thonsand-branched world, and the Apsaras sit down, wearing the vesture spread out by Yama.

> वि॒द्युतो॒ ज्योतिः॒ परि॑ सं॒जिहा॑नं मि॒त्रावरु॑णा॒ यदप॑श्यतां त्वा  
> तत्ते॒ जन्मो॒तैकं॑ वसिष्ठा॒गस्त्यो॒ यत्त्वा॑वि॒श आ॑ज॒भार॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विद्युतः । ज्योतिः । परि । संजिहानं । मित्रावरुणा । यत् । अपश्यतां । त्वा ।  
> तत् । ते । जन्म । उत । एकं । वसिष्ठ । अगस्त्यः । यत् । त्वा । विशः । आजभार ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एतास्वृक्षु वसिष्ठस्यैव देहपरिग्रहः प्रतिपाद्यते । एताश्चेंद्रस्य वाक्यमित्येके वर्णयंत्यपरे वसिष्ठपुत्राणामिति । हे वसिष्ठ यद्यदा विद्युतो विद्युत इव स्वीयं ज्योतिर्देहांतरपरिग्रहार्थं परि संजिहानं परित्यजंतं त्वा त्वां ॥ छांदसमात्मनेपदं ॥ यद्वा । जिघृक्षितदेहार्थं स्वीयं ज्योतिः परि संजिहानं । परिजिघृक्षंत-मित्यर्थः ॥ अस्मिन्पक्षे जहातेर्गर्त्यर्थत्वादात्मनेपदं छांदसं न भवति ॥ मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणावपश्यतां । आवाभ्यामयं जायेतेति समकल्पयतामित्यर्थः । तत्तदा ते

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In these Ṛks the taking of a body by Vasiṣṭha himself is set forth. Some explain these Ṛks as the words of Indra; others, as of Vasiṣṭha's sons. O Vasiṣṭha, when Mitra and Varuṇa saw you, giving up (परि संजिहानं (*pari saṃjihānaṃ*)) your own light like lightning in order to take another body, the middle voice being Vedic; or alternatively, your own light desiring to take the body, meaning "wishing to take"; on this view the middle voice is not Vedic, since the root *jahāti* has the sense of motion. Mitra and Varuṇa saw you: that is, they resolved "may he be born from us two". Then that was your one birth **NOTE**.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vasiṣṭha, when, for another birth, you gave up your former radiance and Mitra and Varuṇa saw you, and when Agastya brought you from your former dwelling place, to be born of Mitra and Varuṇa along with himself, then one birth of yours came about.

##### English translation
When Mitra and Varuna beheld you, Vasistha, quitting the lustre of the lightning (for the different form), then one of your births (took place), in as much as Agastya bore you from your (former) abode.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in some of the following Ṛks the account of the birth of the sage Vasiṣṭha is told. In this Ṛk there is mention of the question of the births of the sages Vasiṣṭha and Agastya. Some maintain that the words in these Ṛks were spoken by Indra himself, and others that they were spoken by the sons of Vasiṣṭha. The details of the birth of the sage Vasiṣṭha we have explained at length in the Special Topics of the next Ṛk.

### Printed p. 139

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे वसिष्ठ मैत्रावरुणो मित्रावरुणयोः पुत्रोऽसि । हे ब्रह्मन् वसिष्ठ उर्वश्या अप्सरसो मनसो ममायं पुत्रः स्यादितीदृशात्संकल्पाद्द्रप्सं रेतो मित्रावरुणयोरुर्वशीदर्शनात्स्कन्नमासीत् । तस्मादधि जातोऽसि । तथा च वक्ष्यते सत्रे ह जातावित्यृचि । एवं जातं त्वा त्वां दैव्येन देवसंबंधिना ब्रह्मणा वेदराशिनाहंभुवा युक्तं पुष्करे विश्वे देवा आददंत । अधारयंत ॥ तथा चादितेर्मित्रावरुणौ जज्ञाते इति प्रकृत्य पठ्यते । तयोरादित्ययोः सत्रे दृष्ट्वाप्सरसमुर्वशीं । रेतश्चस्कंद तत्कुंभे न्यपतद्वासतीवरे ॥ तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवंतौ तपस्विनौ । अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी संबभूवतुः ॥ बहुधा पतितं रेतः कलशे च जले स्थले । स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूत ऋषिसत्तमः । कुंभे त्वगस्त्यः संभूतो जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः । उदियाय ततोऽगस्त्यः शम्यामात्रो महातपाः ॥ मानेन संमितो यस्मात्तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुंभादृषिर्जातः कुंभेनापि हि मीयते । कुंभ इत्यभिधानं च परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते । ततोऽप्सु गृह्यमाणासु वसिष्ठः पुष्करे स्थितः । सर्वतः पुष्करे तं हि विश्वेदेवा आधारयन् ॥ बृ. ५-२८३ रिंद २८९ ॥ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: "And also, Vasiṣṭha, you are Maitrāvaruṇa, the son of Mitra and Varuṇa. O Brahman Vasiṣṭha, from the thought of Urvaśī the Apsaras, 'May this be my son', and from the sight of Urvaśī, the seed (द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)) of Mitra and Varuṇa was spilled. From that you were born." As will be said in the Ṛk beginning *satre ha jātau*. Thus born, you, endowed with the divine Brahman (the mass of the Veda, self-existent), were held (आददंत (*ādadaṃta*), "supported") by all the gods in the lake (पुष्करे (*puṣkare*)).

He then quotes, with a reference, the verses that state this about Aditi's sons Mitra and Varuṇa. At their sacrificial session they saw the Apsaras Urvaśī, and the seed fell into the jar called Vasatīvara. In that same moment the two powerful ascetic seers, Agastya and Vasiṣṭha, came into being there. The seed fell in many ways: in the jar, in the water and on the ground. On the ground the sage Vasiṣṭha, best of seers, arose; in the jar Agastya arose; in the water a great shining fish. Then Agastya, of great austerity, rose up, measuring a śamyā. Because he was measured by a measure (मानेन (*mānena*)) he is called Mānya here; or else the seer was born of the jar (कुंभ (*kuṃbha*)), and by a jar one measures, for "kumbha" is a name for a measure. Then, as the waters were being taken up, Vasiṣṭha stood on the lotus (पुष्करे (*puṣkare*)), and the Viśvedevas held him there on every side. The reference is given as बृ. ५-२८३ रिंद २८९ (*bṛ. 5-283 riṃda 289*) (Bṛ. 5-283 to 289).**NOTE**

- उत (*uta*)—and
- वसिष्ठ (*vasiṣṭha*)—O Vasiṣṭha
- मैत्रावरुणः (*maitrāvaruṇaḥ*)—you, as son of Mitra and Varuṇa
- असि (*asi*)—are
- ब्रह्मन् (*brahman*)—O Vasiṣṭha, possessed of knowledge of Brahman
- उर्वश्याः (*urvaśyāḥ*)—of Urvaśī, the Apsaras woman
- मनसः (*manasaḥ*)—from the will (thought)
- द्रप्सं (*drapsaṃ*)—the seed of Mitra and Varuṇa
- स्कन्नं (*skannaṃ*)—was spilled
- अधि जातः (*adhi jātaḥ*)—you were born from that
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you, thus born
- दैव्येन (*daivyena*)—divine
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—seeing you endowed with the mass of the Veda
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- पुष्करे (*puṣkare*)—on the lotus leaf
