#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒हेह॑ वः स्वतवसः॒ कव॑यः॒ सूर्य॑त्वचः ।  
> य॒ज्ञं म॑रुत॒ आ वृ॑णे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इहइह । वः । स्वतवसः । कवयः । सूर्यत्वचः ।  
> यज्ञं । मरुतः । आ । वृणे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वैश्वदेवे पर्वणि मारुतस्यानुवाक्या इहेह वः इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च । इहेह वः स्वतवसः प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुराय । आ. २-१९ । इति ॥
> हे स्वतवसः स्वायत्तबलाः स्वयं प्रवृद्धा वा हे कवयः क्रांतदर्शिनः सूर्यत्वचः सूर्यवर्णा एवंभूता हे मरुतः यूयमिहेहेहैवास्मदीये यज्ञमा वृणे । अभजामि । कल्पयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Vaiśvadeva parvan this Ṛk, इहेह वः (*iheha vaḥ*), is the Anuvākyā of the offering to the Maruts. It is laid down in the sūtra इहेह वः स्वतवसः प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुराय (*iheha vaḥ svatavasaḥ pra citramarkaṃ gṛṇate turāya*) (Ā. 2-19). O स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*), whose strength rests on themselves, or who have grown by themselves; O कवयः (*kavayaḥ*), far-seeing; सूर्यत्वचः (*sūryatvacaḥ*), of the colour of the sun; O Maruts, such as you are, इहेह (*iheha*), here and here alone, at our sacrifice, आ वृणे (*ā vṛṇe*): I choose, I arrange (the sacrifice) for you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*)—possessed of strength gained by themselves
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the wise
- सूर्यत्वचः (*sūryatvacaḥ*)—radiant like the sun
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—performed with you in view
- इहेह यज्ञं (*iheha yajñaṃ*)—to this our sacrifice alone
- आ वृणे (*ā vṛṇe*)—I invoke, praying

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, possessed of strength gained by yourselves, wise, and radiant like the sun, I invite you to this sacrifice, performed with you in view.

##### English translation
Maruts of independant strength, who are far-seeing, glorious as the
sun, come hither, come hither, I invoke you to the sacrifice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the Vaiśvadeva parvan, this Ṛk beginning इहेह वः (*iheha vaḥ*) is to be recited as the Anuvākyā mantra in the offering made to the Marut deities. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra sets this out in the sūtra इहेह वः स्वतवसः प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुराय (*iheha vaḥ svatavasaḥ pra citramarkaṃ gṛṇate turāya*) (Ā. 2-19).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्र्यं॑बकं यजामहे सु॒गंधिं॑ पुष्टि॒वर्ध॑नं ।

### Printed p. 394

> उर्वारुकमिव बंधनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रिऽअंबकं । यजामहे । सुगंधिं । पुष्टिवर्धनं ।  
> उर्वारुकम्ऽइव । बंधनात् । मृत्योः । मुक्षीय । मा । अमृतात् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र शौनकः । त्रिरात्रं नियतोऽपोष्य क्षीरेणायसं चरुं । सेचनाहुतिशतं पूर्णं जुहुयाच्छंसितव्रतः ॥ समुद्दिश्य महादेवं त्र्यंबकं त्र्यंबकेत्यृचा । एकपर्वशतं कृत्वा जीवेद्वर्षशतं सुखी ॥ ऋग्वि. २-१२ । (त्रयाणां ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्राणामंबकं पितरं यजामह इति शिष्यसमाहितो वसिष्ठो ब्रवीति । किंविशिष्टमित्यत आह । सुगंधिं प्रसारितपुण्यकीर्तिं । पुनः किं विशिष्टं । पुष्टिवर्धनं । जगद्बीजं उरुशक्तिमित्यर्थः । उपासकस्य वर्धनं । अणिमादिशक्तिवर्धनं । अकस्मत्प्रसादादेव मृत्योर्मरणात्संसाराद्वा मुक्षीय । मोचय । यथा बंधनादुर्वारुकं कर्कटीफलं मुच्यते तद्वन्मरणात्संसाराद्वा मोचय । किं मर्यादीकृत्य । अमृतात् । सायुज्यतामोक्षपर्यंतमित्यर्थः । अथ तैत्तिरीयभाष्ये । तै. सं. १-८-६-२ । शोभनः शरीरगंधः पुण्यगंधो वा यस्यासौ सुगंधिः । यथावृक्षस्य संपुष्पितस्य दूराद्गंधो वात्येवं पुण्यस्य कर्मणो दूराद्गंधो वातीति श्रुतेः । पुष्टिं शरीरधनादिविषयां वर्धयतीति पुष्टिवर्धनः । तादृशं त्र्यंबकं यजामहे । पूजयामः । लोके यथोर्वारुकफलानि बंधनाद्वृंतात्स्वयमेव मुच्यंते तद्वदहं त्र्यंबकप्रसादेन मृत्योर्मुक्षीय । मोचनयुक्तो भूयासं । अमृताच्छरीरजीवितात्स्वर्गादेवा मा मुक्षीय । चतुर्थपादार्थेमंत्रस्य तात्पर्यातिशयं दर्शयति । त्र्यंबकं यजामह इत्याह मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतादिति वावैतदाहेति ॥ )

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Śaunaka says: having fasted for three nights, restrained, one should, observing the vow, offer a full hundred sprinkling-oblations of a caru cooked with milk (क्षीरेणायसं चरुं (*kṣīreṇāyasaṃ caruṃ*)), addressing Mahādeva with the Ṛk त्र्यंबकं (*tryaṃbakaṃ*); having done this at one hundred parvans one lives a hundred years in happiness (Ṛgvi. 2-12). **NOTE**
In the bracketed passage Vasiṣṭha, addressed by his disciple, explains: we worship the father (अंबकं (*aṃbakaṃ*)) of the three, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra. "Of what kind?" Answer: सुगंधिं (*sugaṃdhiṃ*), one whose holy fame is spread abroad. Again, of what kind? पुष्टिवर्धनं (*puṣṭivardhanaṃ*): the seed of the world, of great power; the increaser of the worshipper, the increaser of the powers such as aṇimā. May I be released, by his grace alone, from death, that is, from dying or from saṃsāra; release me as the *urvārukaṃ*, the cucumber (कर्कटीफलं (*karkaṭīphalaṃ*)), is freed from its stalk, so free me from death or saṃsāra. Up to what limit? अमृतात् (*amṛtāt*): up to the liberation of sāyujya.
Then, in the Taittirīya commentary (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-6-2): सुगंधिः (*sugaṃdhiḥ*) is one who has a fine bodily fragrance or the fragrance of merit; as the scent of a flowering tree is borne from afar, so the scent of meritorious action is borne from afar, according to the Śruti. पुष्टिवर्धनः (*puṣṭivardhanaḥ*) is one who increases growth in respect of body, wealth and the like. Such a Tryambaka we worship (यजामहे (*yajāmahe*) = we honour). As in the world cucumbers are freed of themselves from the stalk, so may I, by the grace of Tryambaka, be freed from death, and not be freed from the immortal, that is, from life in the body, from heaven. He shows the special import of the fourth pāda: त्र्यंबकं यजामह इत्याह मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतादिति वावैतदाहेति (*tryaṃbakaṃ yajāmaha ityāha mṛtyormukṣīya māmṛtāditi vāvaitadāheti*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुगंधिं (*sugaṃdhiṃ*)—him who has the fragrance of meritorious deeds
- पुष्टिवर्धनं (*puṣṭivardhanaṃ*)—and who increases the nourishment of the world
- त्र्यंबकं (*tryaṃbakaṃ*)—the Supreme Reality, father even of the three Mūrtis (the Lord of the world)
- यजामहे (*yajāmahe*)—we worship
- बंधनात् (*baṃdhanāt*)—from its stalk
- उर्वारुकमिव (*urvārukamiva*)—as the urvāruka fruit drops off and falls
- मृत्योः (*mṛtyoḥ*)—from saṃsāra, which is subject to death
- मुक्षीय (*mukṣīya*)—may he grant that we obtain release
- मा अमृतात् (*mā amṛtāt*)—may we not be kept far from liberation

### Printed p. 395

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We worship the Supreme Lord, who has the fragrance of meritorious deeds, who increases the nourishment of the world, and who is the father even of the three Mūrtis. As the urvāruka fruit drops off and falls from its stalk, may we obtain release from saṃsāra, which is subject to death. But may we not be far from liberation.

##### English translation
We worship Tryambaka, whose fame is fragrant, the augmenter of
increase : may I be liberated from death, and, like the Urvaruka from its
stalk, but not to immortality : [let us worship Tryambaka, whose fame is
fragrant, the augmrnter of increase : may I be liberated from death like the
Urvaruka from its stalk, but not into immortality.]

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Concerning this Ṛk the great sage Śaunaka says in his work called Ṛgvidhāna:
त्रिरात्रं नियतोऽपोष्य क्षपयेत्पायसं चरुं । (*trirātraṃ niyato 'poṣya kṣapayetpāyasaṃ caruṃ |*)
तेनाहुतिशतं पूर्णं जुहुयाच्छंसितव्रतः ॥ (*tenāhutiśataṃ pūrṇaṃ juhuyācchaṃsitavrataḥ ‖*)
समुद्दिश्य महादेवं त्र्यंबकं त्र्यंबकेत्यृचा । (*samuddiśya mahādevaṃ tryaṃbakaṃ tryaṃbaketyṛcā |*)
एतत्पर्वशतं कृत्वा जीवेद्वर्षशतं सुखी ॥ (*etatparvaśataṃ kṛtvā jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sukhī ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna 3-314, 315)
He says that one should fast completely for three nights, that is, three days, and on the third day cook rice-milk (pāyasa) and caru (cooked rice) and with those substances perform a hundred offerings according to rule. If one makes the offering, as stated above, at a hundred parvan times, addressing the Tryambaka deity, Mahādeva, with this Ṛk त्र्यंबकं यजामहे (*tryaṃbakaṃ yajāmahe*), that man will live happily for a hundred years.
त्र्यंबकं (*tryaṃbakaṃ*)—त्रयाणां ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्राणामंबकं पितरं । (*trayāṇāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudrāṇāmaṃbakaṃ pitaraṃ |*) Tryambaka means the Lord of all, father or protector even of the three Mūrtis, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara.
सुगंधिं (*sugaṃdhiṃ*)—प्रसारितपुण्यकीर्तिं । (*prasāritapuṇyakīrtiṃ |*) The fame of this deity is spread everywhere.
पुष्टिवर्धनं (*puṣṭivardhanaṃ*)—He is the seed-form of the world, and the power of this deity is immeasurable; or he is one who makes his worshipper prosper with wealth, grain and the like; or he is the increaser of the powers such as aṇimā.
उर्वारुकमिव बंधनात् (*urvārukamiva baṃdhanāt*)—As the urvāruka fruit, when ripe, is quickly released from its stalk, that is, drops off, so make us free from the bond of saṃsāra.
Since this mantra is also recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-6-3), the explanation of its meaning there is as follows:

### Printed p. 396
सुगंधिं (*sugaṃdhiṃ*)—शोभनः शरीरगंधः पुण्यगंधो वा यस्यासौ सुगंधिः । यथा वृक्षस्य संपुष्पितस्य दूराद्गंधो वात्येवं पुण्यस्य कर्मणो दूराद्गंधो वाति (*śobhanaḥ śarīragaṃdhaḥ puṇyagaṃdho vā yasyāsau sugaṃdhiḥ | yathā vṛkṣasya saṃpuṣpitasya dūrādgaṃdho vātyevaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇo dūrādgaṃdho vāti*) (Tai. Ā. 10-9) इति श्रुतेः ॥ (*iti śruteḥ ‖*) That is: one with an excellent bodily fragrance, that is, a scent; one filled with a fragrant perfume. Or, as a well-flowered tree spreads the scent of its flowers far through the wind, so the fame of a man who has done good deeds spreads far. Therefore the fame, or the power and capacity, of the Lord of all, ruler of the world and creator, is spread everywhere and renowned; this is the meaning.
पुष्टिवर्धनं (*puṣṭivardhanaṃ*)—पुष्टिं शरीरधनादिविषयां वर्धयतीति पुष्टिवर्धनः । तादृशं त्र्यंबकं यजामहे पूजयामः । (*puṣṭiṃ śarīradhanādiviṣayāṃ vardhayatīti puṣṭivardhanaḥ | tādṛśaṃ tryaṃbakaṃ yajāmahe pūjayāmaḥ |*) Since he increases the nourishment of the body, such as food, and wealth, this deity has the epithet Puṣṭivardhana. Let us worship the Lord of all, named Tryambaka, who has such qualities.
लोके यथोर्वारुकफलानि बंधनाद्वृंतात् स्वयमेव मुच्यंते तद्वदहं त्र्यंबकप्रसादेन मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मोचनयुक्तो भूयासं । अमृताच्छरीर जीवितात् स्वर्गादेवा मा मुक्षीय । (*loke yathorvārukaphalāni baṃdhanādvṛṃtāt svayameva mucyaṃte tadvadahaṃ tryaṃbakaprasādena mṛtyormukṣīya mocanayukto bhūyāsaṃ | amṛtāccharīra jīvitāt svargādevā mā mukṣīya |*) In worldly experience we see that the urvāruka fruit, as soon as it is ripe, drops off from its stalk of itself. Likewise may our bond of saṃsāra be loosed, and may we, escaped from death, remain for a long time in heaven and the like, and may we not leave it. Having said this, he cites in support the Brāhmaṇa sentences त्र्यंबकं यजामह इत्याह । मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतादिति वावैतदाह । (*tryaṃbakaṃ yajāmaha ityāha | mṛtyormukṣīya māmṛtāditi vāvaitadāha |*) (Tai. Brā. 1-6-10-3).
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमोहार्दं निवारयन् । (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamohārdaṃ nivārayan |*)
पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*pumarthāṃścaturo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)
इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपाल साम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये पंचमाष्टके चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpāla sāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye paṃcamāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ‖*)
॥ ओं तत्सत् ॥ (*‖ oṃ tatsat ‖*)
Here ends the fourth chapter in the fifth Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Sāyaṇa's commentary and the Kannada translation.

### Printed p. 397

## Maṇḍala 7

**Introduction (Sūkta 60)**

Sixtieth Sūkta of the seventh Maṇḍala, in the fifth Adhyāya of the fifth Aṣṭaka.

*On the deity Sūrya*

In this Sūkta and in the six Sūktas that follow it, the beginning is a praise of Sūrya and afterwards a praise of Mitra and Varuṇa. Therefore we shall first consider the subject of Sūrya briefly here, and afterwards examine the subject of Mitra and Varuṇa.

In many places in the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda it is said that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. Many Śruti passages can be cited as examples, such as मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः ॥ (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ ‖*) But if one asks what connection Sūrya has with Mitra and Varuṇa, —

### Printed p. 398

it is said that this Sūrya, who is visible to our eyes, is like the eyes of Mitra and Varuṇa. In many Ṛks such as चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः (*cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1), चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य (*cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-63-1), नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे (*namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-1), Sūrya is famed as the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa.

Sūrya is the son of the heaven-world (दिवस्पुत्राय सूर्याय शंसत (*divasputrāya sūryāya śaṃsata*), 10-37-1); in some places Sūrya is also reckoned the son of Aditi (सूर्यमादित्येयं (*sūryamādityeyaṃ*) 10-88-11). Sūrya sits on a chariot. One horse or many horses draw his chariot; ordinarily seven horses bear it (सप्ताश्वा हरितः सूर्यस्य (*saptāśvā haritaḥ sūryasya*) 1-115-3, 4). Sūrya is the Self of the whole world: as the inner self in the bodies of living beings he governs their movements, and Sūrya is also the cause of the movement of inert things (सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) 1-115-1). Impelled by the power of Sūrya, people become able to do their respective tasks (नूनं जनाः सूर्येण प्रसूता अयन्नर्थानि कृणवन्नपांसि (*nūnaṃ janāḥ sūryeṇa prasūtā ayannarthāni kṛṇavannapāṃsi*) 7-63-4). He can see everything to a great distance; he sees all the good and bad deeds that men do (1-50-2, 6; 7-61-1; 7-63-1, 4 etc.).

Explaining the meaning of the word Sūrya, Yāska says:

सूर्यः सर्तेर्वा, सुवतेर्वा, स्वीर्यतेर्वा ॥ (*sūryaḥ sartervā, suvatervā, svīryatervā ‖*) (Ni. 12-14)

That is, he has said that the word Sūrya may be formed from the root सृ (*sṛ*) (to move), or from the root सूज् (*sūj*) (to bring forth), or from सु (*su*) + ईरयति (*īrayati*), meaning to impel. Sūrya rises in the east in the morning, moves in the sky without a break, and by evening reaches the west and sets; thus his movement is unbroken. Again, by the power of Sūrya all the living beings and plants of the world are produced. The air, heated by the rays of Sūrya, through its movements causes manifold changes in the world. By the heat of his rays the waters of seas and other reservoirs turn to vapour, and in the sky, as clouds, pour down rain and become the cause of the production of plants. From plants, living beings and men are produced (अद्भ्य ओषधयः । ओषधीभ्योऽन्नं । अन्नात्पुरुषः ॥ (*adbhya oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadhībhyo 'nnaṃ | annātpuruṣaḥ ‖*) Tai. U. 2-1-1). The movements of inert things also arise from the heat of Sūrya. How? As said in सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*): Sūrya, a mass of radiance, though he stands in the middle of his orb, pervades everything with his heat, and so, as the inner controller of all, impels each to act according to its time. Therefore he is the cause of the production of the whole class of effects, moving (living beings and so on) and unmoving (inert things).

### Printed p. 399

Only Sūrya has the power, once he has risen, to stir up beings who lie motionless like the dead, without knowledge or strength to do any work, and to make them engage in their respective tasks.

योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति । स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेति । ........ असौ योऽस्तमेति । स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायास्तमेति । .... असौ य आपूर्यति । स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणैरापूर्यति । (*yo 'sau tapannudeti | sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyodeti | ........ asau yo 'stameti | sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇānādāyāstameti | .... asau ya āpūryati | sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇairāpūryati |*) (Tai. Ā. 1-14-1)

As said in these Śruti passages: when Sūrya sets he takes with him the Prāṇas of all living beings, that is, the power of movement and the like and the activity of knowing. Therefore at night living beings, unable to do any work, fall under the sway of sleep. Again, in the morning, when Sūrya rises, he comes bringing with him the Prāṇas of all those beings, that is, the powers of doing work and the activity of knowing, and rises. Then he fills those beings with his power in the form of vigour. Since Sūrya gives knowledge and power of action to the whole world and, by his rising and setting, makes it conscious and unconscious in turn, his greatness is here described: he is the Self and the individual soul of all things, moving and unmoving.

Besides this, according to modern science (Sceintific view) too, Sūrya is the cause of the movements of all things in this world. From Sūrya we receive every kind of energy. Sūrya, or his rays, are the cause of the movements going on among living beings; of the movement of the air in the sky, the formation of clouds, the falling of rain and similar events; and of all the work that goes on unceasingly on the earth, such as the growth of plants and the flowing movement of rivers. Without the light of Sūrya, deep darkness would cover this world and not even a blade of grass could move. Therefore it is fitting to give the sentence सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) the meaning: The sun is the source of all the energies so for as this world (earth) is concerned.

In the Purāṇas and elsewhere Sūrya is called by words such as Āditya, Pūṣan, Mitra, Savitṛ. But in the Vedas, and especially in the Ṛgveda, the distinctive character of Sūrya is one thing and that of Āditya another; the distinctive character of the deities Pūṣan, Mitra, Savitṛ and so on is different again. Although the qualities of Sūrya are seen in the twelve Ādityas beginning with Mitra, in sacrifices, where Sūrya is praised, Āditya is not praised. All these are reckoned as separate deities. Not only that: in the Vedas

### Printed p. 400

when one and the same deity has a distinctive personal quality, the deity with that quality is regarded as different. For example, when Indra is called मरुत्वानिंद्रः (*marutvāniṃdraḥ*) and महानिंद्रः (*mahāniṃdraḥ*), Indra is one, Marutvān Indra (Indra accompanied by the Marut deities) another, and Mahān Indra (Indra of great form) another, and each is worshipped according to the occasion. Likewise such distinctions as अग्निः (*agniḥ*) and अग्निःपावकः (*agniḥpāvakaḥ*) are found among other deities. The Ṛks of the Ṛgveda that praise Sūrya are these:

Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50: in Sūkta 1-50, Ṛks 1 to 13: 13 Ṛks
1-115: Ṛks 1 to 6: 6
4-40 **NOTE**: Ṛk 5: 1
5-40 **NOTE**: Ṛk 5: 1
7-60: Ṛk 1: 1
7-62: Ṛks 1 to 3: 3
7-63: Ṛks 1 to 4⅓: 4⅓
7-66 **NOTE**: Ṛks 14 to 16: 3
8-101 **NOTE**: Ṛks 11 to 13: 3
10-37: Ṛks 1 to 12: 12
10-158: Ṛks 1 to 5: 5
10-170: Ṛks 1 to 4: 4
10-189: Ṛks 1 to 3: 3

Only these Ṛks are addressed to Sūrya. There are no other Ṛks in the Ṛgveda addressed to Sūrya.

*What the Ṛks on Sūrya in the Ṛgveda say*

The Sūktas in the Ṛgveda that praise Sūrya are 5 complete Sūktas, together with some Ṛks in other Sūktas, in all 60½ Ṛks. No other deity is perceptible to the senses as Sūrya is. The light of Sūrya in the sky is the face of Agni (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-3). The eye of Sūrya is spoken of in many places (5-40-5 **NOTE** etc.); and he is the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni (1-115-1). Sūrya has a close connection with the organ of sight. It is said that the eye of a dead man merges into Sūrya (10-16-3; 10-90-3; 10-158-3, 4). Sūrya is lord of all the organs of sight (Atha. Ve. 5-24-9). Being the eye of all living beings, he looks upon the sky, the earth and the waters

### Printed p. 401

all of them (Atha. Ve. 13-1-45). He is far-seeing, that is, he can see a great distance (7-35-8; 10-37-1); all-seeing (1-50-2); the spy of the whole world (4-13-3). He sees the world of the moving and unmoving, and the good and bad deeds that men do (1-50-2; 6-51-2; 7-60-2; 7-61-1; 7-63-1, 4). Awakened by the rising of Sūrya, people engage in their tasks (7-63-4). He rises awakening all men (7-63-2, 3). He is the Self of all things moving and unmoving, and he is their protector (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1; 7-60-2). His chariot has one horse (7-63-2), or seven horses (5-45-9), or seven mares (हरितः (*haritaḥ*)) (1-50-8, 9; 7-60-3), or seven swift horses (4-13-3).

Varuṇa prepares for Sūrya the path he must travel (1-24-8; 7-87-1), or Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, all three, prepare it (7-60-4). Pūṣan is his messenger (6-58-3). Sūrya comes forth shining from the lap of the goddess Uṣas (7-63-3). In some places Uṣas is called the wife of Sūrya (7-75-5).

Since Sūrya is the son of Aditi, he has the name Āditya or Āditeya (1-50-12; 1-89-8; 8-90-11; 10-88-11); but he and the Ādityas are distinct (8-35-13, 14). The deity of heaven is his father (10-37-1); he was born of the gods. The gods lifted him up when he lay hidden in the ocean (10-72-7). The gods established him in the sky as a transformation of Agni (10-88-11). He arose from the eye of the Puruṣa of the cosmic form (10-90-13).

Various deities are said severally to be the cause of Sūrya's birth. Indra caused him to be born (3-31-15), established him in the sky and made him shine there (2-14-3; 8-89-2). Indra and Viṣṇu are his parents (8-99-4). Indra and Soma made Sūrya, joined with light, grow (6-72-4). Mitra and Varuṇa established him in the sky (5-63-7). The light in Sūrya was established by Soma (6-44-23; 9-96-5). Sūrya was born from Soma himself (9-96-5; 9-110-3). The deity Soma made Sūrya shine (9-37-2), or made him stay in the sky (9-101-2). It was Agni who established the radiance of Sūrya very high (10-3-2) and made it climb to the sky (10-156-4). Dhātṛ, the creator, fashioned both Sūrya and the moon (10-190-3). By the sacrificial rites of the Aṅgirases Sūrya was able to climb the sky (10-62-3). In all these Ṛks on the birth of Sūrya, the radiant orb of Sūrya is what is indicated.

In many passages Sūrya is conceived as a bird flying in the sky (10-146-3, 4). He is a bird with flowery feet (5-47-3); Sūrya flies (1-50-9). He is compared to a flying hawk (7-63-5); in one place he is called a hawk outright (5-44-11).
51

### Printed p. 402

In another place he is called a bull and a bird (5-47-3), and a bull and a bird with variegated spots (10-189-1; 5-47-3). In one place he is called the white and bright horse brought by the goddess Uṣas (7-77-3). The seven horses of Sūrya are his rays (8-61-16), because these rays carry him along.

Sometimes Sūrya is seen compared to an inanimate object. He is a jewel in the sky (7-63-4; 7-35-1), a many-coloured stone carved in the middle of the sky (5-47-3; Śa. Brā. 6-1-2-3). He is a shining weapon, which Mitra and Varuṇa hide with rain-clouds (5-63-4). He is the weapon called Pavi of Mitra and Varuṇa (5-62-2), a chariot set in the sky by the two (5-63-7). Sūrya himself is a wheel (1-175-4; 4-30-4); the wheel of Sūrya's chariot is mentioned in many places (4-30-2; 5-29-10).

Sūrya shines for the world (7-63-1), for men and gods (1-50-5). With his radiance he drives off the darkness (10-37-4). He rolls up darkness like a skin (7-63-1). Like throwing away a skin, his radiance hurls the darkness into the water (4-13-4). He conquers persons connected with darkness and sorceresses (1-191-8, 9; 7-104-24). The fierce heat of Sūrya is mentioned in two places (7-74-19; 9-107-20). In the Ṛgveda Sūrya is not a cruel deity; this is stated clearly in the Atharvaveda and the Brāhmaṇas.

Sūrya lengthens the span of life (8-48-7). He removes diseases and bad dreams (10-37-4). To see the sunrise means to live long (4-25-4; 7-53-5). All living beings depend on Sūrya (1-164-14), and the sky too depends on him (10-85-1). He is named Viśvakarman (10-170-4). By his greatness he is the priest of the gods (8-90-12). At sunrise men pray to Sūrya to tell the other gods that Mitra and Varuṇa are sinless (7-60-1; 7-62-2). Once Indra defeated Sūrya and carried off the wheel of his chariot (1-175-4; 4-30-4); so it is said.

*Examination of Mitra and Varuṇa*

Although Mitra and Varuṇa are regarded as separate deities, the mantras that praise the two together (collectively) are the more numerous. In some places they are described as deities of the twelfth portion among the twelve Ādityas, the many forms of Sūrya, and elsewhere these deities are described as other forms of Agni.

### Printed p. 403

In the Ṛk त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः । (*tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1) it is said that Agni is named Varuṇa when he is born, and Mitra when he is well kindled and blazing brightly. Moreover, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
मित्रोऽसि वरुणोऽसीत्याह । मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । अहोरात्राभ्यामेवैनमुपावहति । ( (*mitro 'si varuṇo 'sītyāha | maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ | ahorātrābhyāmevainamupāvahati | (*) (Tai. Brā. 1-7 10-1).
Here Mitra is said to be the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. It should therefore be noted that these deities are described in some places as partial deities of the Sun, and in others as different names of Agni.

Mitra—In the Purāṇas and other works Mitra is one of the twelve Ādityas. In the Ṛgveda, although Mitra is another name of the Sun, Mitra has a distinct character, that is, an individual prominence. In the Ṛgveda Mitra and Varuṇa are said to be sons of Aditi, and so they are called Ādityas in many places. That these Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, are six in number is shown by:
इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो घृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥ (*imā gira ādityebhyo ghṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi | śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1)
Here only six names are given: Mitra, Aryamā, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa.
In the Ṛk देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभि रक्ष न इंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ॥ (*devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhi rakṣa na iṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3) the sons of Aditi are said to be seven.
In the Ṛks
अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्व १ स्परि । देवा उप प्रैत्सप्तभिः परा मार्तांडमास्यत् ॥ सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तांडमाभरत् ॥ (*aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanva 1 spari | devā upa praitsaptabhiḥ parā mārtāṃḍamāsyat ‖ saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupa praitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tvatpunarmārtāṃḍamābharat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8,9)
it is said that Aditi first had seven sons and afterwards one more, Mārtāṇḍa, eight sons in all. Further, in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:
अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वः परि । देवाँ उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे तत् । परा मार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते ॥ (*aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥ pari | devām̐ upapraitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tat | parā mārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | aṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgścetyete ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 1-13-3)

### Printed p. 404

Here the names of the eight sons of Aditi are given. Those eight are said to be Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryamā, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān. The same matter is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा चाजायेतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्या अंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चाजायेतां ॥ (*aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā cājāyetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyā aṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgścājāyetāṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1,2,3)
The account of Aditi's obtaining eight sons is clearly set out here. Of these eight, the three Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryamā are the especially famous ones in the Ṛgveda. In Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 3-59 there is an extended description of the heroic deeds, beneficial to the world, of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryamā. Yāska has given the explanation of the word Mitra in his Nirukta thus:
मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा ॥ (*mitraḥ pramītestrāyate saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā ‖*) (Ni. 10-21)
What is the meaning of the word Mitra? —मित्रः कस्मात् । स हि प्रमीतेः त्रायते । प्रमीतिः मरणं । ततः सर्वलोकं त्रायते वर्षद्वारेण ॥ (*mitraḥ kasmāt | sa hi pramīteḥ trāyate | pramītiḥ maraṇaṃ | tataḥ sarvalokaṃ trāyate varṣadvāreṇa ‖*) Pramīti means death. Because he produces rain for people in the world, thereby provides food and other nourishment, and so protects them by averting the fear of death that may arise from hunger, this deity is called Mitra. समंततो मिन्वानः उदकेन द्रवति अंतरिक्षलोके । (*samaṃtato minvānaḥ udakena dravati aṃtarikṣaloke |*) Because this deity, as lord of water, stationed in the atmosphere, through the clouds makes all regions around cling together, that is, join together, he is called Mitra. Having stated this threefold derivation, in support of it the following Ṛk is cited as an example:
मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥ (*mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhota ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1)
In this Ṛk Mitra, as helper in agriculture and other works, pours down rain and the like, provides people with food and other nourishment, and upholds and sustains the people of the earth and the dwellers of heaven. "O men, offer to such a god Mitra oblations mixed with ghee"—thus

### Printed p. 405

Mitra's extraordinary qualities and his service to the world are described very well. The only sūkta in the Ṛgveda addressed to Mitra is the 59th sūkta of the third maṇḍala, of 9 Ṛks. Elsewhere Mitra is praised together with other deities such as Varuṇa.

Because the association of Mitra and Varuṇa is very close, the sūkta with Mitra alone as deity is, as said before, only one in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59). Even there the praise of this deity is obscure. But only in the first Ṛk is Mitra's distinctive character well described. In the 5th Ṛk of the same sūkta:
महा आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः । (*mahā ādityo namasopasadyo yātayajjano gṛṇate suśevaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-5)
This Mitra is called the great Āditya who brings all men together. The word यातयज्जनः (*yātayajjanaḥ*) with this meaning is used of the two, Mitra and Varuṇa, in the Ṛk
व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना । (*vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātayajjanā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2)
and of the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryamā, in the Ṛk
मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्जनोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः । (*mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3)
According to the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59 mentioned above, Mitra is the support of heaven and earth. Men, the five tribes (पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*)), are obedient to him. Thus his qualities are described: he is the sustenance of life for all the other gods. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-4 Savitṛ and Mitra are said to be one and the same person; in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Vā. Saṃ. 4-3) Viṣṇu is said to have taken his three steps following Mitra's ordinances; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1 Agni is Varuṇa when born and Mitra when kindled; and
मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्धो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः । मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिंधूनामुत पर्वतानां ॥ (*mitro agnirbhavati yatsamiddho mitro hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ | mitro adhvaryuriṣiro damūnā mitraḥ siṃdhūnāmuta parvatānāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-5)
here it is said that Agni, when well kindled, is Mitra; that this Mitra is in the sacrifice the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, Varuṇa and the Agni called Jātavedas; and that he is the friend (benefactor) of rivers and mountains. Thus Mitra's qualities are described.

It is Sāyaṇa's view that the word Mitra is a synonym of the Sun. He has explained the parts of the word, showing that the word Mitra is formed of the two roots मि (*mi*) and त्रा (*trā*): *prakarṣeṇa sarvairmiyate jñāyate kathā sarvān vṛṣṭipradānena trāyata iti vā

### Printed p. 406

मित्रः सूर्यः । (*mitraḥ sūryaḥ |*) He is fully known by all and he protects all. Because he has these two qualities, the Sun is denoted by the word Mitra. The word Mitra is found in some places with the meaning friend, benefactor. For example:
मित्रं देवा अब्रुवन् सोममग्ं राजानग्ं हनामेति सोऽब्रवीन्नाहग्ं सर्वस्य वा अहं मित्रमस्मीति । (*mitraṃ devā abruvan somamagṃ rājānagṃ hanāmeti so 'bravīnnāhagṃ sarvasya vā ahaṃ mitramasmīti |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-8-1)
Once, on the occasion of pressing the Soma juice, the gods said to Mitra: "O Mitra, let us destroy King Soma (the Soma plant), crushing it and pressing out the Soma juice." Mitra replied: "Never! It is because I am the friend of all that I have the name Mitra. Therefore I will not join you in this act." These and similar matters describe Mitra's qualities.

Varuṇa—वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (*varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ*) (Ni. 10-3): Yāska's explanation is that this deity is called Varuṇa because he is enveloped by masses of cloud.
Varuṇa is a most exalted deity, equal to Indra in power and the like. The number of mantras addressed to Varuṇa is very small. There are twelve sūktas in the Ṛgveda addressed to Varuṇa, but twenty-four sūktas praise Mitra and Varuṇa together.

Varuṇa has a human body and human activities. But rather than his bodily form and activities, descriptions of his moral activities and deeds are mostly indicated. He has a face, eyes, arms, hands and feet; he drives a chariot, sits, eats, drinks, and so on: such bodily activities of his are described. That the Sun is the eye of Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa is stated plainly in the Ṛks:
चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । (*citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1)
उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धं । (*udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdhaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1)
उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् । (*udvāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-1)
चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक् तमांसि । (*cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasya devaścarmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṃsi |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-3)
नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत । (*namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-1)

### Printed p. 407

in these Ṛks. Since the matter that the Sun is like an eye to him stands in the very first Ṛk of the sūktas addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, it seems that this is the point that first presents itself whenever Mitra and Varuṇa are mentioned. Also in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-10 Aryamā, Mitra and Varuṇa are said to have the Sun as their eye. Varuṇa is said to be far-seeing (उरुचक्षसं (*urucakṣasaṃ*)) in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-5 and 1-25-18.
आ नो बर्हि रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । सीदंतु मनुषो यथा ॥ (*ā no barhi riśādaso varuṇo mitro aryamā | sīdaṃtu manuṣo yathā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-26-4)
व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥ (*vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātayajjanā | ni barhiṣi sadataṃ somapītaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2)
In these and similar Ṛks Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryamā are invoked to come and sit, for the drinking of Soma, on the darbha grass spread on the sacrificial altar.
यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादयैते । (*yadī sakhāyā sakhyāya somaiḥ sutebhiḥ suprayasā mādayaite |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-48-3)
In these and similar Ṛks it is said that Varuṇa drinks Soma together with Indra and the other gods.
बिभ्रद्द्रापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त निर्णिजं । परि स्पशो नि षेदिरे ॥ (*bibhraddrāpiṃ hiraṇyayaṃ varuṇo vasta nirṇijaṃ | pari spaśo ni ṣedire ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-13)
In this Ṛk Varuṇa is described as wearing a golden mantle or coat (armour) and a shining garment. Varuṇa's chariot is golden, bright like the Sun, and has whips that urge the horses. Mitra and Varuṇa mount their chariot in a very high region of the sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-1). Such descriptions occur.
The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is golden and lies in the upper world. Varuṇa, seated in his palace there—
नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्या३ स्वा । साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः ॥ अतो विश्वान्यद्भुता चिकित्वाँ अभि पश्यति । कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥ (*ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastyā3 svā | sāmrājyāya sukratuḥ ‖ ato viśvānyadbhutā cikitvām̐ abhi paśyati | kṛtāni yā ca kartvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-10,11)
sees everything that happens in the world. The abode of Mitra and Varuṇa is very large, very lofty, firm with a thousand pillars, and their house has a thousand doors. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-

### Printed p. 408

5). There are also descriptions that the all-seeing Sun sets out from his own abode and goes to the house of Mitra and Varuṇa to report the doings of men, and enters their dear house. Varuṇa, alone or together with Mitra, like other deities, is called in many places by the word राजा (*rājā*) (king).
अबुध्ने राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः । (*abudhne rājā varuṇo vanasyordhvaṃ stūpaṃ dadate pūtadakṣaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-7)
त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः । (*tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-10)
तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम । (*tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūma |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3)
In these and similar Ṛks Varuṇa is said to be king not only of men but of the gods and of all the worlds. Besides Varuṇa, deities such as Indra, Yama and Soma also have the honorific name of king.

There are many stories about Indra. But in the case of Varuṇa it is quite the opposite: there is not a single story. Varuṇa is much praised as the regulator of physical and moral laws (वरुणस्य व्रतानि (*varuṇasya vratāni*)). The divine power of Mitra and Varuṇa is described by the word माया (*māyā*). When applied to the gods, this also means the hidden power they have to do good. In the good sense this word is fitting for Mitra and Varuṇa; in the bad sense it applies to the Rākṣasas. Like the meaning of the word असुर (*asura*), the word माया (*māyā*) is used in both senses. By this hidden Māyā-power in himself, Varuṇa, standing in the atmosphere, measures out the earth by means of the Sun as with a measuring rod. He makes the Sun cross the sky and makes him veiled by rain clouds. Then honey-mixed (sweet) drops fall (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-4). He makes the sky pour rain. Therefore in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-4, 7-38-4, 10-99-10 and 10-147-5 this word माया (*māyā*) is applied chiefly to Varuṇa among the gods.

Varuṇa is the one who ordains the laws of nature. It was he who established earth and heaven. And
आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि सम्राड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि । (*āsīdadviśvā bhuvanāni samrāḍviśvettāni varuṇasya vratāni |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-42-1)
in this Ṛk it is said that Varuṇa dwells in all the worlds and that his ordinances and the like are observed everywhere there, and
तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिन्तिस्रो भूमीरुपराः षड्विधानाः । (*tisro dyāvo nihitā aṃtarasmintisro bhūmīruparāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-87-5)

### Printed p. 409
Here it is said that the three upper worlds and the three lower (earthly) worlds are under his control. Varuna and Mitra rule the whole universe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-2). They alone are the protectors of the entire world (Ṛ. 2-27-4). Varuna is the support of heaven, earth and sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-1, 4). He has placed Agni in the water, the Sun in the sky, and Soma upon the stone. He has made a broad path for the Sun. Varuna, Mitra and Aryaman clear a path for the Sun (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-60-4). In many such Ṛks Varuna's sovereignty is described.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-8-3) it is said मित्रोऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं (*mitro 'harajanayadvaruṇo rātriṃ*)—that is, Mitra created the day and Varuna the night. Therefore मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ |*)—that is, in many places Mitra is said to be lord of the day and Varuna lord of the night. In one place (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-2-4) it is said that Varuna divided the seasons.

वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ॥ (*veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8): here it is said that Varuna knows the twelve months; and

वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चादृचं । अनास्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशते ॥ (*vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajñamaktuṃ cādṛcaṃ | anāsyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-11): in this Ṛk it is said that Mitra, Varuna and Aryaman divided autumn, the month, the day and the night.

In many places it is said that it is Varuna who regulates the waters. It is he who made the rivers flow; by his command they flow ever on (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4). Though the rivers run swiftly and pour their water into the ocean, they do not fill it—this is through his hidden power (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-6). Varuna and Mitra are lords of the rivers. That Varuna is lord of the oceans is an established point, yet the Ṛgveda rarely states it; perhaps it was left out because it was thought unimportant. In the Purāṇas and the like Varuna is renowned as lord of the waters, and it is said there that he is one of the eight guardians of the quarters, lord of the west. The Ṛgveda has no support for this. Generally everything connected with Varuna concerns the water in the atmosphere. Among the deities prayed to for rain, Varuna and Mitra are the chief. When the mountains are all covered with clouds, Varuna soaks heaven, earth and sky and makes the earth wet with the water that comes from the cloud above, as is said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3, 4.

### Printed p. 410
A whole sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63) praises their power of sending rain. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-4-1) आपो वरुणस्य पत्नय आसन् (*āpo varuṇasya patnaya āsan*)—the waters are said to be Varuna's wives, and (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-2) मित्रावरुणौ वा अपां नेतारौ (*mitrāvaruṇau vā apāṃ netārau*)—Mitra and Varuna are the leaders of the water.

It is said again and again that Varuna's decrees are firmly established. For this reason he is called Dhṛtavrata ("of firm ordinances"). Both Mitra and Varuna bear this epithet.

परि धामानि मर्मृशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वेदेवा अनु व्रतं नभंतामन्यके समे ॥ (*pari dhāmāni marmṛśadvaruṇasya puro gaye viśvedevā anu vrataṃ nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-7)

न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनंति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ॥ (*na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minaṃti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-4)

In these and other Ṛks it is said that even the gods obey the commands of Mitra, Varuna and Aryaman, and that even the primeval gods cannot transgress their firm ordinances. Mitra and Varuna are the regulators of law (ṛta) and of light. By the strength of these decrees they are able to support the laws. This quality is seen especially in these two, sometimes in the Ādityas, or in other common deities too. The epithet that they promote truth (ṛta) and justice, or are their guardians (ऋतस्य गोपाः (*ṛtasya gopāḥ*)), or make others keep the laws, is often applied to Mitra and Varuna.

Varuna's power is immeasurable. Neither flying birds nor flowing rivers can reach the boundary of his realm, nor surpass his power, nor withstand his wrath. Neither the sky nor the rivers have reached the limit of the domain of Mitra and Varuna. Everything is contained in Varuna. The dwellings of all creatures, the three heavens and the three earths, are established in him. Varuna is all-knowing. The flight of birds in the sky, the course of ships on the sea, the path of the far-travelling wind—all this he knows. He sees all that is past or yet to come. He is witness of the true and false deeds of men. The actions, thoughts and devices of every man are known to Varuna. He can grasp all that is in heaven and earth and beyond them. However far beyond the sky one may run, no one can leave Varuna's path of vision.

Being the regulator of right conduct, Varuna becomes very angry at sin, and also at the breach of his ordinances. For both he imposes very cruel punishment. Varuna's noose that binds sinners

### Printed p. 411
is spoken of in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-15; 1-25-21; 6-74-4; 10-85-24 and other Ṛks. That noose binds the speaker of untruth and releases the speaker of truth.

युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभि रज्जुभिः सिनीथः । परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥ (*yuvo rāṣṭraṃ bṛhadinvati dyauryau setṛbhi rajjubhiḥ sinīthaḥ | pari no heḷo varuṇasya vṛjyā uruṃ na iṃdraḥ kṛṇavadu lokaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-84-2)

In this Ṛk it is said that Varuna, together with Indra, binds with bonds that are not ropes. The word pāśa ("noose") occurs in the Ṛgveda in Agni hymns only in one or two places, and that too where Agni is asked to loosen the noose that binds his devotees. Therefore the acts of binding with the noose and of releasing from it may be said to belong to Varuna alone. Varuna with Mitra drives away, hates and punishes untruth. Mitra and Varuna punish even those who do not praise them, and those who are negligent. But Varuna forgives those who repent; he looses them from the noose and removes sin. He frees a man not only from sin committed by himself but also from that committed by his forefathers. He protects those who daily break the very laws he has laid down and afterwards repent, and shows compassion to those who have transgressed his commands through forgetfulness. Varuna has hundreds and thousands of medicines. He drives death far away and removes sin. He can take away life and can also grant life. Thus Varuna's qualities are described in many Ṛks.

The sixtieth sūkta

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्र यदद्य सूर्येति द्वादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । यदद्य मैत्रावरुणं तु वै सौर्याद्येति । मंडलद्रष्टा वसिष्ठ ऋषिः । अनुक्तत्वात् त्रिष्टुप्छंदः । तु वा इत्युक्तत्वादेतदादीनि सप्त सूक्तानि मित्रावरुणदेवत्यानि । आद्या सूर्यदेवत्या ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of these, the fifth sūkta, यदद्य सूर्य (*yadadya sūrya*), has twelve Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says यदद्य मैत्रावरुणं तु वै सौर्याद्या (*yadadya maitrāvaruṇaṃ tu vai sauryādyā*). The seer is Vasiṣṭha, the seer of the Maṇḍala. As nothing else is stated, the metre is Triṣṭubh. Because of the words तु वै (*tu vai*), this and the following seven sūktas are addressed to Mitra and Varuna; the first Ṛk is addressed to Sūrya. The application (viniyoga) is by indication (laiṅgika).

Translation: This sūkta यदद्य सूर्य (*yadadya sūrya*) is the fifth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka of the seventh maṇḍala. It has twelve Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says यदद्य मैत्रावरुणं तु वै सौर्याद्या (*yadadya maitrāvaruṇaṃ tu vai sauryādyā*). The seer of this sūkta is Vasiṣṭha, the seer of this Maṇḍala. In the seven sūktas from here, the first few Ṛks are addressed to Sūrya and the remaining Ṛks to Mitra and Varuna. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The application is by indication.

### Printed p. 412
## Sūkta 60 (Maṇḍala 7)
Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 60. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 5; Varga 1, 2. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: 1. Sūrya; 2-12. Mitra and Varuṇa. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद॒द्य सू॑र्य॒ ब्रवोऽना॑गा उ॒द्यन्मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय स॒त्यं ।  
> व॒यं दे॑व॒त्रादि॑ते स्याम॒ तव॑ प्रि॒यासो॑ अर्यमन्गृ॒णंतः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अद्य । सूर्य । ब्रवः । अनागाः । उत्यन् । मित्राय । वरुणाय । सत्यं ।  
> वयं । देवऽत्रा । अदिते । स्याम । तव । प्रियासः । अर्यमन् । गृणंतः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सूर्य सर्वस्य प्रेरकेत्यन्नामक देव उद्यन्नुदयं कुर्वंस्त्वं यद्यद्याद्यास्मिन्ननुष्ठानकालेऽस्मान्प्रवः ब्रूयाः । किमिति । अनागा अनागस इति । एतेऽपापा इति यदि देवेषु मध्ये ब्रूयास्तर्हि वयं हे अदिते अदीन देव देवत्रा देवेषु देवानां मध्ये मित्राय वरुणाय च सत्यमवितथं स्याम । अनागसो भवेम । किंच हे अर्यमन् दातस्त्वां गृणंतः स्तुवंतस्तव प्रियासः प्रियाः स्याम । त्वत्प्रेमविषया भवेम । यद्वा । उत्तरार्ध एकं वाक्यं । हे अदिते हे अर्यमन्नुक्तलक्षण देव वयं देवेषु मध्ये त्वां गृणंतस्तवैव प्रियाः स्याम । यदि मां देवेष्वपापं ब्रूयास्तर्हि त्वयायमनपराधीत्यनुगृहीतस्त्वां स्तुत्वा तव प्रियो भवेयमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūrya, god, impeller of all, rising today at this time of the rite, if you declare us to be sinless (अनागा (*anāgā*) = अनागस (*anāgasa*))—"these are free of sin"—among the gods, then, O Aditi (the undiminished god), we shall be truthful (सत्यं (*satyaṃ*) = unfalsified) before Mitra and Varuna among the gods; we shall be sinless. Further, O Aryaman, giver, praising you we shall be dear to you, objects of your affection. Or else, the latter half is one sentence: O Aditi, O Aryaman, god of the stated character, praising you among the gods may we be dear to you alone. If you declare me sinless among the gods, then, favoured by you as "this man is without offence", praising you I would become dear to you. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदिते (*adite*)—O Sūrya of complete nature
- सूर्य (*sūrya*)—O Sūrya
- उद्यन् (*udyan*)—you who rise
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)—(these sacrificers are) sinless
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—to Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuna
- ब्रवः (*bravaḥ*)—if you say (then)
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- देवत्र (*devatra*)—in the presence of the gods
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of truthful conduct
- स्याम (*syāma*)—we shall be reckoned
- अर्यमन् (*aryaman*)—O god Aryaman
- गृणंतः (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ*)—we who praise you
- तव (*tava*)—to you
- प्रियासः (*priyāsaḥ*)—may we be dear

### Printed p. 413

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya of complete nature, if you, rising at this time of the sacrifice, tell Mitra and Varuna that "these sacrificers are free of sin", then we shall be reckoned in the presence of the gods as men of truthful conduct. O Aryaman, may we who praise you be dear to you.

##### English translation
Surya, when rising to-day, declare the truth to Mitra and Varuna, that we are void of sin : may we, Aditi, be (approved of) among the gods : praising you, Aryaman, may we be dear to you.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्य मि॑त्रावरुणा नृ॒चक्षा॑ उ॒भे उदे॑ति॒ सूर्यो॑ अ॒भि ज्मन् ।  
> विश्व॑स्य स्था॒तुर्जग॑तश्च गो॒पा ऋ॒जु मर्ते॑षु वृजि॒ना च॒ पश्य॑न् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्यः । मित्रावरुणा । नृचक्षाः । उभे इति । उत् । एति । सूर्यः । अभि । ज्मन् ।  
> विश्वस्य । स्थातुः । जगतः । च । गोपाः । ऋजु । मर्तेषु । वृजिना । च । पश्यन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणा एष पुरतो दृश्यमानः स्यः स सर्वैः स्तुत्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धो नृचक्षा नृणां मनुष्याणां द्रष्टा सूर्य उभे द्यावापृथिव्यावभ्यभिलक्ष्योदेति ज्मन्नंतरिक्षे गच्छन् । स विशेष्यते । विश्वस्य सर्वस्य स्थातुः स्थावरस्य जगतो जंगमस्य च गोपा गोपायिता । किं कुर्वन् । मर्तेषु मनुष्येषु स्थितान्यृजूनि सुकृतानि वृजिनानि पापानि च पश्यन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuna, this Sūrya seen before us, known to all as worthy of praise, beholder of men, rises toward both heaven and earth, moving (ज्मन् (*jman*)) in the atmosphere. He is further described: guardian of all, of the stationary (स्थातुः (*sthātuḥ*)) and of the moving (जगतः (*jagataḥ*)). What does he do? He sees the upright (good) deeds and the sins (वृजिना (*vṛjinā*)) that exist among mortals.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuna
- स्थातुः (*sthātuḥ*)—of the stationary
- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—and of the moving
- विश्वस्य च (*viśvasya ca*)—of the entire world
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—protector
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—he who is visible in front
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the well known
- नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—who beholds all the dealings of men
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya
- मर्तेषु (*marteṣu*)—among men
- ऋजु (*ṛju*)—the truthful life
- वृजिना च (*vṛjinā ca*)—and the untruthful life
- पश्यन् (*paśyan*)—seeing
- ज्मन् (*jman*)—moving in the atmosphere
- उभे अभि (*ubhe abhi*)—facing heaven and earth
- उदेति (*udeti*)—rises

### Printed p. 414

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuna, Sūrya, the protector of the entire world, stationary and moving, visible to all the world, beholder of all the dealings of men, rises facing heaven and earth, seeing the truthful and untruthful life among men and moving in the atmosphere.

##### English translation
This Surya, the beholder of man, rises, Mitra and Varuna, upon both (heaven and earth), moving (in the sky): he who is the preserver of all that is stationary or meveable, witnessing the upright acts or the sins of mortals.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अयु॑क्त स॒प्त ह॒रितः॑ स॒धस्था॒द्या ईं॒ वहं॑ति॒ सूर्यं॑ घृ॒ताचीः॑  
> धामा॑नि मित्रावरुणा यु॒वाकुः॒ सं यो यू॒थेव॒ जनि॑मानि॒ चष्टे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयुक्त । सप्त । हरितः । सधस्थात् । याः । ईं । वहंति । सूर्यं । घृताचीः ।  
> धामानि । मित्रावरुणा । युवाकुः । सं । यः । यूथाऽइव । जनिमानि । चष्टे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ युवयोरागमनाय सधस्थात् सहस्थानादंतरिक्षादंतरिक्षे सप्त सर्पणस्वभावानेतत्संख्याकान्हा हरितो हरिद्वर्णानश्वानयुक्त । युक्तवान्रथे । हरित आदित्यस्येति हि निरुक्तं । या हरित ईमेनं सूर्यं देवं घृताचीर्घृतांचना उदकवत्यः । उदकप्रदा इत्यर्थः । तादृश्यः सत्यो वहंति ता अयुक्त । अथोदितः सन्धामानि स्थानानि लोकांजनिमानि जन्मानि । जन्मभाजः प्राणिन इत्यर्थः । तांश्च युवाकुर्युवां कामयमानो यो देवः संचष्टे सम्यक् पश्यति यूथेव गोयूथानीव यूथपः । स यथा सर्वं यूथं तदवांतरगोव्यक्तिं च सम्यक् पश्यति तद्वल्लोकान्प्राणिनश्च पश्यति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuna, for your coming he yoked to the chariot seven (सप्त (*sapta*)) moving, green-coloured (हरितः (*haritaḥ*)) horses from the common station (सधस्थात् (*sadhasthāt*)), the atmosphere. The Nirukta says हरित आदित्यस्य (*harita ādityasya*). The mares that carry this god Sūrya are घृताचीः (*ghṛtācīḥ*), water-bearing, that is, water-giving; such as they are, he yoked them. Then, having risen, the god who, desiring you both, surveys well (संचष्टे (*saṃcaṣṭe*)) the stations (धामानि (*dhāmāni*)), the worlds, and the births (जनिमानि (*janimāni*))—that is, creatures having birth—sees them as a herd-keeper sees his herds (यूथेव (*yūtheva*)): as he sees the whole herd and each individual cow within it, so he sees the worlds and creatures.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuna
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which horses
- घृताची (*ghṛtācī*)—filled with water
- ईं सूर्यं (*īṃ sūryaṃ*)—this god Sūrya
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—carry, such
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven

### Printed p. 415

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- संख्याकवू (*saṃkhyākavū*)—(continuing) of that number
- हरितः (*haritaḥ*)—the horses of green colour

- अयुक्त (*ayukta*)—Sūrya has yoked to his chariot
- युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*)—desiring your company
- यः (*yaḥ*)—that same Sūrya who
- यूथेव (*yūtheva*)—as a herdsman surveys all his herds of cows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, Sūrya has yoked to his chariot, in the firmament that is the common dwelling-place of all of you, the seven green-coloured horses that, full of water, carry this god Sūrya. That same Sūrya, who desires your company, looks closely at all the worlds and all living beings, as a herdsman surveys all his herds of cows.

##### English translation
He has harnessed his seven bay steeds Mitra and Varuna, (to come from your common dwelling-place, (the firmament): the horses that, shedding water convcy that Surya who, friendly to you both, (contemplates all) regions, and looks carefully upon living creatures as (a herdsman) upon the herd.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Mitra and Varuṇa: for you the foods (पृक्षासः (*pṛkṣāsaḥ*)), the caru, puroḍāśa and the like, sweet and with their means, the plants and so on, have been prepared. ()

> न्यासन् । सूर्यश्च शुक्रं दीप्तपुर्णोर्णवमंतरिक्षमारुहत् । आरोहति ।
> यस्मै सूर्याय तद्गमनार्थमादित्या अदितेः पुत्रा देवा अध्वनो मार्गान्रदंति
> विलिखंति साधयंति । के ते । मित्रोऽर्यमा वरुणश्चैते त्रयोऽपि देवाः सजोषसः समानप्रीतयः संतः । स देव आरुहदिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sentence is completed: they have been prepared. Sūrya has mounted the shining, bright-bodied firmament. For his going the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, cut and make ready the paths. Who are they? Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, these three gods, of one accord; by them that god has ascended.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पृक्षासः (*pṛkṣāsaḥ*)—foods such as caru and puroḍāśa
- मधुमंतः (*madhumaṃtaḥ*)—endowed with sweetness
- उपस्थाः (*upasthāḥ*)—have been prepared
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—for which Sūrya
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—of equal affection
- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—sons of Aditi
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- अध्वनः (*adhvanaḥ*)—the paths
- रदंति (*radaṃti*)—open up and make ready
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—that Sūrya
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—shining
- अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—the firmament
- आरुहत् (*āruhat*)—has ascended

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, foods such as caru and puroḍāśa, endowed with sweetness, have been prepared for you. Sūrya, for whom Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, sons of Aditi and of equal affection, open up and make ready the paths, has ascended the shining firmament.

##### English translation
For you (Mitra and Varuna), the sweet-flavoured viands have been prepared: the sun has ascended the shining firmament, for whom the Adityas and the consentient Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman make ready the paths.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमे मित्रोऽर्यमा वरुणश्च त्रयोऽप्यनृतस्य पापस्य भूरेः प्रभूतस्य चेतारो हंतारः संति । भवंति हि । इमे मित्रादय ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य दुरोणे गृहे ववृधुः । वर्धंते हविषा स्तुत्या च । कीदृशास्ते । शग्मासः सुखकरा अदितेः पुत्रा अदब्धाः अहिंसिताः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These three, Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, are destroyers of abundant अनृत (*anṛta*), that is, sin. These, Mitra and the others, grow in the house (दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)) of the sacrifice (ऋत (*ṛta*)), through oblation and praise. Of what kind are they? Bringers of happiness, sons of Aditi, unconquered, that is, unharmed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- इमे (*ime*)—these three deities
- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—of abundant
- अनृतस्य (*anṛtasya*)—sin
- चेतारः (*cetāraḥ*)—as destroyers
- संति हि (*saṃti hi*)—they become
- शग्मासः (*śagmāsaḥ*)—givers of happiness
- अदितेः पुत्राः (*aditeḥ putrāḥ*)—sons of Aditi
- अदब्धाः (*adabdhāḥ*)—unharmed
- इमे (*ime*)—these deities
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—in the house
- ववृधुः (*vavṛdhuḥ*)—are nourished (by the oblation)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, these three deities, are destroyers of abundant sin. These deities, givers of happiness, sons of Aditi, unharmed, are nourished by the oblation in the house of sacrifice.

##### English translation
These (deities), Mitra, Aryaman, Varuna are the detecters of much untruth : these unconquered sons of Aditi, dispensers of happiness, are magnified in the hall of sacrifice.

> इम आदित्या मित्रो वरुणश्च ।       ।  दूळभासो दुर्धभा अनभिभाव्या अचेतसं चिदप्रज्ञातमनुष्यानपि  ज्ञानरहितम
> 53

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Ādityas, Mitra and Varuṇa, are दूळभासः (*dūḷabhāsaḥ*), unassailable, unconquerable. (The Sanskrit is damaged here.) Even men without understanding and devoid of knowledge … **NOTE**

### Printed p. 418

> दक्षैः सामर्थ्यैश्चितयंति । अपि सुचेतसं प्रकृष्टज्ञानवंतं पुरुषं क्रतुं कर्तारं कर्मानुष्ठानवंतं वतंतो गच्छंतोऽंहो दुष्कृतं तिरश्चित्तिरो नयंतोऽस्मान्सुपथा शोभनेन मार्गेण नयंति । प्रापयंत्यभिमतं यज्ञं स्वर्गादिकं वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They awaken with their powers. Moreover, going to the man of excellent understanding, the doer, who performs rites, and carrying off his sin, they lead us by a good path, they bring us to the desired sacrifice or to heaven and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa (and Aryaman)
- इमे (*ime*)—these three deities
- दूळभासः (*dūḷabhāsaḥ*)—possessed of unobstructed power
- अचेतसं चित् (*acetasaṃ cit*)—even one devoid of knowledge of performing rites
- दक्षैः (*dakṣaiḥ*)—by their powers
- चितयंति (*citayaṃti*)—awaken
- अपि (*api*)—and
- सुचेतसं (*sucetasaṃ*)—one of excellent knowledge of rites
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—to the man who performs rites
- वतंतः (*vataṃtaḥ*)—going
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—his sin
- तिरश्चित् (*tiraścit*)—destroying
- सुपथा (*supathā*)—(him) by an excellent path
- नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—they lead

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These three deities, Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, sons of Aditi, possessed of unobstructed power, awaken by their powers even the ignorant who do not know how to perform rites. And approaching the man of excellent knowledge of rites who performs them, they destroy his sin and lead him by an excellent path.

##### English translation
These, the unsubdued Mitra, Varuna, and Aryaman, animate with energies the unconseious (sleepers) : repairing to the intelligent performer (of pious acts), they lead (him), by safe paths (to heaven), removing all iniquity.

### Printed p. 419

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमे मित्रादयो दिवो द्युलोकस्य पृथिव्याश्च संबंधिनोऽनिमिषानिमिषेण सर्वदा चिकित्वांसो जानंतः । कं । अचेतसमज्ञानं । नयंति । प्रापयंति कर्माणि । प्रव्राजे चित् प्रवणेऽप्यत्यंतनिन्नेऽपि देशे नद्यो नद्या गाधमस्ति । भवति युष्मत्सामर्थ्यात् । ते महांतो नोऽस्माकमस्य विष्पितस्य व्याप्तस्य कर्मणः पारं पर्षन् । पारयंतु । नयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These, Mitra and the others, belonging to heaven and earth, always knowing with unwinking eye, lead the अचेतसं (*acetasaṃ*), the ignorant, to rites. Even in a stream's steep, deeply sunk place there is a ford, a bottom, through your power. May those great ones carry us across to the far shore of this extended rite.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमे (*ime*)—the deities Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—belonging to the heavenly world
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—belonging to the earth
- अचेतसं (*acetasaṃ*)—ignorance
- अनिमिषा (*animiṣā*)—with an unwinking gaze
- चिकित्वांसः (*cikitvāṃsaḥ*)—knowing
- नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—lead to the path of rites
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—of the river
- प्रव्राजे चित् (*pravrāje cit*)—even in the deepest place
- गाधं अस्ति (*gādhaṃ asti*)—a bottom is found (through the greatness of these deities)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- विष्पितस्य (*viṣpitasya*)—extensive
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this rite
- पारं (*pāraṃ*)—to the shore
- पर्षन् (*parṣan*)—may they carry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, knowing with unwinking gaze the ignorance that belongs to heaven and to earth, lead all to the path of rites. Through the greatness of these deities a bottom is found even in the deepest place of a river. May these great deities cause this extended rite to be accomplished without hindrance. (May they carry across this river that is exceedingly extensive and of the nature of rites.)

##### English translation
(Beholding) with unclosing eyes, and cognizant (of the things) of heaven and earth, they conduct the ignorant man (to duty): in the lowest depth of the river, (through them), there is a bottom : may they lead us to the opposite shore of the vast expanse.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्गो॒पाव॒ददि॑तिः॒ शर्म॑ भ॒द्रं मि॒त्रो यच्छं॑ति॒ वरु॑णः सु॒दासे॑ ।  
> तस्मि॒न्ना तो॒कं तन॑यं॒ दधा॑ना॒ मा क॑र्म देव॒हेळ॑नं तुरासः ॥

### Printed p. 420

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । गोपावत् । अदितिः । शर्म । भद्रं । मित्रः । यच्छंति । वरुणः । सुदासे ।  
> तस्मिन् । आ । तोकं । तनयं । दधानाः । मा । कर्म । देवहेळनं । तुरासः ॥८॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यच्छर्म सुखं गृहं वा गोपावद्रक्षणोपेतं भद्रं स्तुत्यमदितिरदीनोऽर्यमादितिर्वा मित्रो वरुणश्चैते त्रयो देवाः सुदासे सुदानाय मह्यं यच्छंति प्रयच्छंति तस्मिन् शर्मणि तोकं पुत्रं तनयं तत्पुत्रादिकं । अथवा तनयशब्दोऽपत्यसामान्यवचनः । तोकं बलवंतं पुत्रमा सर्वतो दधाना धारयंतो
> वयं हे तुरासो गमनाय त्वरमाणाः देवहेळनं देवानां मित्रादीनां कोपनं मा कर्म । माकार्ष्म ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The शर्म (*śarma*), happiness or house, protected, भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), praiseworthy, which Aditi (the undiminished Aryaman, or Aditi) and Mitra and Varuṇa, these three gods, give to me, the good giver (सुदासे (*sudāse*)): in that शर्म (*śarma*), holding on all sides sons (तोकं (*tokaṃ*)) and तनयं (*tanayaṃ*), their sons and so on (or तनय (*tanaya*) is a general word for offspring, and तोकं (*tokaṃ*) a strong son), may we, hastening to go (तुरासः (*turāsaḥ*)), not commit देवहेळनं (*devaheḷanaṃ*), the provoking of the gods, Mitra and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aryaman, of perfect form
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa (these three deities)
- सुदासे (*sudāse*)—to me, who offer an excellent oblation
- गोपावत् (*gopāvat*)—endowed with protection
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- यत् शर्म (*yat śarma*)—which house
- यच्छंति (*yacchaṃti*)—they give
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in that house
- तोकं (*tokaṃ*)—sons
- तनयं (*tanayaṃ*)—grandsons
- आ दधानाः (*ā dadhānāḥ*)—I (and our people) having them everywhere
- तुरासः (*turāsaḥ*)—being hasty
- देवहेळनं (*devaheḷanaṃ*)—an act that provokes the anger of the gods
- मा कर्म (*mā karma*)—may we not do

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the house, protective and auspicious, that Aryaman, of perfect form, and Mitra and Varuṇa, these three deities, give to me who offer an excellent oblation, having sons and grandsons everywhere, may I and our people, hasty by nature, not perform any rites that provoke the anger of the gods.

##### English translation
Including our sons and grandsons in that preserving and auspicious felicity which Aditi, Mitra and Varuna confer upon the liberal donor (of the oblation), may we never, acting precipitately, incur the displeasure of the deities.
