#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अव॒ वेदिं॒ होत्रा॑भिर्यजेत॒ रिपः॒ काश्चि॑द्वरुण॒ध्रुतः॒ सः ।  
> परि॒ द्वेषो॑भिरर्य॒मा वृ॑णक्तू॒रुं सु॒दासे॑ वृषणा उ लो॒कं

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । वेदिं । होत्राभिः । यजेत । रिपः । काः । चित् । वरुणध्रुतः । सः ।  
> परि । द्वेषोभिः । अर्यमा । वृणक्तु । उरुं । सुदासे । वृषणा । ऊं इति । लोकं

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रादयः सोऽस्मद्द्वेषी वेदिं यागसाधनं होत्राभिः । वाङ्नामैतत् । वाग्रूपाभिः स्तुतिभिः सार्धमव यजेत । वेद्यां कर्माणि कुर्वन्देवान्स्तयादित्यर्थः । अवपूर्वो यजतिस्त्यागार्थः । स किं प्राप्नुयादिति तत्राह । वरुणधृतो वरुणेन क्रुद्धेन हिंसितः स काश्चिद्रिपो हिंसाः प्राप्नुयादिति शेषः । अस्मांस्त्वर्यमा देवो द्वेषोभिर्द्वेष्टृभी रक्षःप्रभृतिभिः परि वृणक्तु । वर्जयतु ।
> उरुं विस्तीर्णं लोकं स्थानं सुदासे शोभनदानाय मह्यं प्रयच्छतं हे वृषणा वर्षकौ कामानां मित्रावरुणौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing Mitra and the other deities: let that enemy of ours "sacrifice away" the altar, the means of the sacrifice, together with his होत्राभिः (*hotrābhiḥ*) (a name for speech), that is, with praises in the form of speech. The meaning is that, performing his rites at the altar, he gives up the gods. The verb यजति (*yajati*) with अव (*ava*) has the sense of giving up. What may he then obtain? Sāyaṇa answers: struck by an angry Varuna, may that enemy meet with some injuries. May Aryaman, the god, keep us away from those who hate us, the Rakṣases and the like. O showerers of desires, Mitra and Varuna, grant a wide region, a place, to me, the one who gives well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः (*saḥ*)—our enemy
- होत्राभिः (*hotrābhiḥ*)—with his (unrecited) praises
- वेदिं (*vediṃ*)—the sacrificial altar
- अव यजेत (*ava yajeta*)—let him lose
- वरुणध्रुतः (*varuṇadhrutaḥ*)—he who is afflicted by Varuna
- काश्चित् (*kāścit*)—some
- रिपः (*ripaḥ*)—injuries, let him obtain
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman
- द्वेषोभिः (*dveṣobhiḥ*)—from our enemies
- परि वृणक्तु (*pari vṛṇaktu*)—let him separate us
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuna, showerers of desires
- सुदासे (*sudāse*)—to me, the giver of oblations
- उरुं (*uruṃ*)—wide
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—a place; grant it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and the other deities, let our enemy lose his sacrificial altar by not reciting praises. Afflicted by Varuna, may he also become the object of many injuries. May the god Aryaman separate us from our enemies. O Mitra and Varuna, showerers of desires, provide a wide place for me, the giver of oblations.

### Printed p. 422

##### English translation
Let my adversary desecrate the altar by (ill-expressed) praises: repelled by Varuna, may he (undergo) various sufferings: may Aryaman defend us from those who hate us: confer, showerers (of benefits), a vast region upon the liberal donor (of oblations).
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒स्वश्चि॒द्धि समृ॑तिस्त्वे॒ष्ये॑षामपी॒च्ये॑न॒ सह॑सा॒ सहं॑ते ।  
> यु॒ष्मद्भि॒या वृ॑षणो॒ रेज॑माना॒ दक्ष॑स्य चिन्महि॒ना मृ॒ळता॑ नः ॥१०॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सस्वः । चित् । हि । संऋतिः । त्वेषी । एषां । अपीच्येन । सहसा । सहंते ।  
> युष्मत् । भिया । वृषणः । रेजमानाः । दक्षस्य । चित् । महिना । मृळत । नः ॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषां मित्रादीनां समृतिः संगतिः संहतिर्वा सस्वरंतर्हिता निगूढा त्वेषी
> दीप्ता च भवति । तादृशा सती अपीच्येन । एतद्गुह्यांतर्हितनाम । निगूढेन सहसा बलेन सहंते । अभिभवंत्यस्मद्द्वेष्टॄन् । किं च हे वृषणोऽभिमतवर्षका मित्रादयः युष्मद्युष्मत्तो भिया भीत्या रेजमानाः कंपमाना भवंति विरोधिनः । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्दक्षस्य युष्माकं बलस्य महिना महिम्ना महत्त्वेन नोऽस्मभ्यं मृळत । उपदयां कुरुत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The समृतिः (*samṛtiḥ*) of these, Mitra and the others, that is their union or combination, is सस्व (*sasva*) (hidden, concealed) and also lustrous. Being such, it overcomes our haters with अपीच्येन (*apīcyena*) (a name for "secret, hidden") power. Further: O Mitra and the others, showerers of what is desired, the opponents tremble with fear of you. Since this is so, show us mercy through the greatness of your युष्माकं बलस्य (*yuṣmākaṃ balasya*) strength (दक्ष (*dakṣa*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these three deities, Mitra and the others
- समृतिः (*samṛtiḥ*)—companionship
- सस्वः (*sasvaḥ*)—inexpressible
- त्वेषी (*tveṣī*)—is radiant
- अपीच्येन (*apīcyena*)—secret
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—with strength
- सहंते (*sahaṃte*)—they defeat our enemies
- वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*)—O Mitra and the others, showerers of desires
- युष्मत् (*yuṣmat*)—of you
- भिया (*bhiyā*)—through fear
- रेजमानाः (*rejamānāḥ*)—our enemies tremble
- दक्षस्य (*dakṣasya*)—of your power
- महिना (*mahinā*)—through the greatness
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- मृळत (*mṛḷata*)—bring happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The companionship of the three deities, Mitra and the others, is inexpressibly radiant. By their secret power they defeat all our enemies. O Mitra and the others, showerers of desires, our enemies tremble through fear of you. Through the greatness of your power, bring us happiness.

### Printed p. 423

##### English translation
The association of these (three deities) is of mysterious lustre: by their secret strength they overcome (all enemies): showerers (of benefits), through fear (of you our opponents) are trembling: have mercy upon us in the mightiness of your strength.
#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो ब्रह्म॑णे सुम॒तिमा॒यजा॑ते॒ वाज॑स्य सा॒तौ प॑र॒मस्य॑ रा॒यः ।  
> सीक्षं॑त म॒न्युं म॒घवा॑नो अ॒र्य उ॒रु क्षया॑य चक्रिरे सु॒धातु॑ ॥११॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ब्रह्मणे । सुमतिं । आयजाते । वाजस्य । सातौ । परमस्य । रायः ।  
> सीक्षंत । मन्युं । मघवानः । अर्यः । उरु । क्षयाय । चक्रिरे । सुधातु ॥११॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो यजमानो ब्रह्मणे परिवृढस्वकर्मणे युष्मत्स्तोत्ररूपाय सुमतिं शोभनां बुद्धिमायजाते आयजते । यजतिरत्र दाने । ददाति करोति । किमर्थं । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातौ दाने निमित्ते परमस्योत्कृष्टस्य रायो धनस्य च सातौ ।
> तस्यार्थः । ईरयति स्तुतीः प्रेरयतीत्यरिः स्तोता । मन्युं स्तोत्रं मघवानो
> दानवंतोऽर्यमादयः सीक्षंत । सचंते । सेवित्वा च तस्मै उरुक्षयाय विस्तीर्णनिवासाय सुधातु सुधाम शोभनस्थानं चक्रिरे । कुर्वते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer who offers a good mind, सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*), to ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*), that is to the praise-making of the Parivṛḍha (your hymn-form), for the sake of वाजस्य (*vājasya*) food, to obtain it by gift, and of supreme wealth: here यजति (*yajati*) is in the sense of giving; he gives, he makes. The *ariḥ* is the praiser, one who sends forth praises. The munificent ones, Aryaman and the rest, together enjoy his मन्युं (*manyuṃ*), his hymn; having enjoyed it, they make for him a wide dwelling, a सुधातु (*sudhātu*), a good place.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food
- सातौ (*sātau*)—for the gaining
- परमस्य (*paramasya*)—of excellent
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth, for the sake of
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—for the praise addressed to Mitra and the others
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—his excellent mind
- आ यजाते (*ā yajāte*)—offers
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—of such a praiser
- मन्युं (*manyuṃ*)—the hymn
- मघवानः (*maghavānaḥ*)—Aryaman and the others, the wealthy
- सीक्षंत (*sīkṣaṃta*)—enjoy together
- उरु क्षयाय (*uru kṣayāya*)—for him to dwell, wide
- सुधातु (*sudhātu*)—an excellent place
- चक्रिरे (*cakrire*)—they make

### Printed p. 424

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealthy Aryaman and the others together enjoy the hymn of the praiser who, for the gaining of food and for excellent wealth, offers his excellent mind for the making of praise addressed to Aryaman and the others. They make for him an excellent place in which to dwell widely.

##### English translation
These munificent (deities) conjointly accept the praise of the worshipper, and bestow a spacious mansion for a dwelling upon him who, for the sake of food and excellent riches, devotes his mind to your glorification.
#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यं दे॑व पु॒रोहि॑तिर्यु॒वभ्यां॑ य॒ज्ञेषु॑ मित्रावरुणावकारि ।  
> विश्वा॑नि दु॒र्गा पि॑पृतं ति॒रो नो॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑  
> नः ॥१२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । देवा । पुरोहितिः । युवभ्यां । यज्ञेषु । मित्रावरुणौ । अकारि ।  
> विश्वानि । दुर्गा । पिपृतं । तिरः । नः । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥१२॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया स्तुतिमुपसंहरति । हे देवा देवौ मित्रावरुणौ युवभ्यां युवाभ्यां यज्ञेष्वियं पुरोहितिः पुरस्क्रिया पूजा स्तुतिलक्षणाकारि । कृताभूत् ।
> तां सेवित्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि दुर्गा दुःखेन गंतव्यान्यापदस्तिरः । तिरस्कुरुतं । तथा
> कृत्वा नोऽस्मान् पिपृतं पारयतं । शिष्टो गतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk he concludes the praise. O divine Mitra and Varuna, this पुरोहितिः (*purohitiḥ*), a fore-placing, a worship in the form of praise, has been made for you two at the sacrifices. Having enjoyed it, put aside तिरः (*tiraḥ*) all difficulties, दुर्गा (*durgā*), the calamities hard to pass through; having done so, carry us across.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवा (*devā*)—O Mitra and Varuna, the foremost of the deities
- मित्रावरुणौ (*mitrāvaruṇau*)—O Mitra and Varuna
- युवभ्यां (*yuvabhyāṃ*)—addressed to you
- इयं पुरोहितिः (*iyaṃ purohitiḥ*)—this worship in the form of praise, offered before you
- यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—at the sacrifices
- अकारि (*akāri*)—has been procured (enjoying it)
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- दुर्गा (*durgā*)—calamities

### Printed p. 425
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—destroy
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*)—carry across from hardship
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuna, foremost of the deities, this worship in the form of praise, offered before you and addressed to you, has been procured at the sacrifices. Enjoying it, destroy all calamities. Carry us across hardship. Protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
Excellent Mitra and Varuna, to you this adoration at sacrifices is addressed: remove from us all difficulties, and ever cherish us with blessings
## Sūkta 61 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उद्वां चक्षुरिति सप्तर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं मैत्रावरुणं ।
> उद्वां सप्तेत्यनुक्रमणिका । विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sixth sūkta, उद्वां चक्षुः (*udvāṃ cakṣuḥ*), of seven Ṛks, has Vasiṣṭha as seer, Mitra and Varuna as deity, and Triṣṭubh as metre. The Anukramaṇikā says उद्वां सप्त (*udvāṃ sapta*). The use in ritual is लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*), by the indication of the text itself.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, उद्वां चक्षुः (*udvāṃ cakṣuḥ*), is the sixth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is its seer; Mitra and Varuna are the deity; Triṣṭubh is the metre. The Anukramaṇikā says उद्वां सप्त (*udvāṃ sapta*). The use in ritual is Laiṅgika.

Sūkta 61. Maṇḍala 7. Anuvāka 4. Aṣṭaka 5. Adhyāya 5. Varga 3. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: Mitra and Varuna. Metre: Triṣṭubh.
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद्वां॒ चक्षु॑र्वरुण सु॒प्रती॑कं दे॒वयो॑रेति॒ सूर्य॑स्तत॒न्वान् ।  
> अ॒भि यो विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि॒ चष्टे॒ स म॒न्युं मर्त्ये॒ष्वा चि॑केत ॥  
> ५४

### Printed p. 426

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । वां । चक्षुः । वरुणा । सु-प्रतीकं । देवयोः । एति । सूर्यः । ततन्वान् ।  
> अभि । यः । विश्वा । भुवनानि । चष्टे । सः । मन्युं । मर्त्येषु । आ । चिकेत ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुणा मित्रावरुणौ देवयोर्द्योतमानयोर्वां युवयोश्चक्षुः
> प्रकाशकं तेजः सुप्रतीकं शोभनरूपमेवं रूपः सूर्यस्ततन्वान्तेजो विस्तारयन्नुदेति । उद्गच्छति । अथोदितो यो देवो विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातान्यभि चष्टे अभिपश्यति स देवो मर्त्येषु प्रवृत्तं मन्युं स्तोत्रं कर्म वा
> चिकेत । आजानाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuna, that is, Mitra and Varuna: of you two, the shining divinities, the चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*), the illuminating radiance, of beautiful form (सुप्रतीकं (*supratīkaṃ*)), such is Sūrya, who rises spreading his radiance. The god thus risen, who looks upon विश्वा (*viśvā*) all beings, भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*), that god चिकेत (*ciketa*) perceives the मन्युं (*manyuṃ*), the hymn or the rite, current among mortals.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणा (*varuṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuna
- देवयोः (*devayoḥ*)—of the shining ones
- वां (*vāṃ*)—of you
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—the one of radiant form
- सुप्रतीकं (*supratīkaṃ*)—and of attractive form
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya
- ततन्वान् (*tatanvān*)—rises, spreading his radiance
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Sūrya god who
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—beings
- अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)—beholds directly
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same god
- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among men
- मन्युं (*manyuṃ*)—the hymn that is current
- आ चिकेत (*ā ciketa*)—knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuna, Sūrya, the radiant and attractive form of you who are divine, rises spreading his radiance. The god Sūrya who beholds directly all beings knows the praise current among men.

##### English translation
Spreading around the beautiful light, Mitra and Varuna, of you two divinities, Surya rises: he who beholds all existing beings apprehends the acts of mortals.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वां॒ स मि॑त्रावरुणावृ॒तावा॒ विप्रो॒ मन्मा॑नि दीर्घ॒श्रुदि॑यर्ति ।

### Printed p. 427

> यस्य ब्रह्माणि सुक्रतू अवाथ आ यत्क्रत्वा न शरदः पृणैथे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वां । सः । मित्रावरुणौ । ऋत-वा । विप्रः । मन्मानि । दीर्घ-श्रुत् । इयर्ति ।  
> यस्य । ब्रह्माणि । सुक्रतू इति सु-क्रतू । अवाथः । आ । यत् । क्रत्वा । न । शरदः ।  
> पृणैथे इति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवयोर्मन्मानि मननीयानि स्तोत्राणि स प्रसिद्धो
> विप्रो मेधाव्यृतावा यज्ञवान् दीर्घश्रुत् चिरकालं श्रोता एवमुक्तलक्षणो वसिष्ठ इयर्ति । प्रेरयति ॥ यस्य ऋषेर्ब्रह्माणि परिवृढानि स्तोत्राणि हे सुक्रतू शोभनकर्माणौ अवाथः रक्षथः ॥ यत्क्रत्वा कर्मणा शरदो बहून् संवत्सराना पृणैथे अपूरयेथे स उदियर्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, that well-known sage Vasiṣṭha — wise (मेधावि (*medhāvi*)), possessed of sacrifice (ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)), a hearer for a long time (दीर्घश्रुत् (*dīrghaśrut*)), so described — sends forth (इयर्ति (*iyarti*)) to you the praises worthy of meditation (मन्मानि (*manmāni*)). He is the seer whose prayers (ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)), that is, extensive hymns, you, O doers of good deeds (सुक्रतू (*sukratū*)), protect (अवाथः (*avāthaḥ*)). By the rite (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) you fill up (पृणैथे (*pṛṇaithe*)) for many years (शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)); that one sends forth the praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुक्रतू (*sukratū*)—possessed of excellent action
- मित्रावरुणौ (*mitrāvaruṇau*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Vasiṣṭha
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—the hymns
- अवाथः (*avāthaḥ*)—you protect
- यत् क्रत्वा (*yat kratvā*)—which rite
- शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—for many years
- आ पृणैथे (*ā pṛṇaithe*)—you fill with the reward
- सः (*saḥ*)—the well-known
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise
- ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—the performer of sacrifice
- दीर्घश्रुत् (*dīrghaśrut*)—one who has perceived praise for many ages; Vasiṣṭha
- वां (*vāṃ*)—directed to you
- मन्मानि (*manmāni*)—the hymns
- प्र इयर्ति (*pra iyarti*)—recites, sending forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, of excellent deeds, the hymns of Vasiṣṭha you protect, whose rites you honour and for many years fill with their rewards — that well-known, wise Vasiṣṭha, performer of sacrifice, who has perceived praise for many ages, composes and recites the praises directed to you.

##### English translation
The sage, the solemnizer of sacrifice, the ancient hearer (of holy prayer), earnestly repeats, Mitra and Varuna, your praises: he whose prayers, doers of good deeds, you favour, whose acts (of worship) you recompense not for years.

### Printed p. 428

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In न शरदः (*na śaradaḥ*) the bhāṣya does not state what the use of न (*na*) is meant to be. In the translation it is given a negative sense. But the same translator (Wilson) gives a fuller explanation in his Notes: Sayana passes by न (*na*) which may be conjunction 'and' as well as the negative 'not'. In either case the sense is obscure ; it may mean that the merit of the worship is so great that it cannot be adequately rewarded except after a long time.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रोरोर्मि॑त्रावरुणा पृथि॒व्याः प्र दि॒व ऋ॒ष्वाद्बृ॑ह॒तः सु॑दानू ।  
> स्पशो॑ दधाथे॒ ओष॑धीषु वि॒श्वन्ध॑ृग्य॒तो अनि॑मिषं॒ रक्ष॑माणा ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । उरोः । मित्रावरुणा । पृथिव्याः । प्र । दिवः । ऋष्वात् । बृहतः । सुदानू इति  
> सु-दानू ।  
> स्पशः । दधाथे इति । ओषधीषु । विश्व-धृक् । यतः । अनिमिषं । रक्षमाणा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ युवामुरोर्विस्तीर्णायाः पृथिव्या अपि प्र ।
> प्ररिरिचाथे । अस्येव प्र रिरिचे । ऋ. १-६१-९ । इत्यादिषु प्रशब्दस्य रिरिच इत्यनेन
> सह संबंधदर्शनादत्राप्युचितक्रियाध्याहारेण रिरिचाथे इति योज्यं । तथा ऋष्वात् महतो बृहतः स्वरूपतोऽतिमहतो दिवो द्युलोकादपि प्र रिरिचाथे हे सुदानू शोभनदानौ । किंच ओषधीषु विश्वासु प्रजासु निमित्तभूतासु प्रजासु चेति वा
> स्पशो रूपं दधाथे । धारयेथे । किं कुर्वंतौ । यतो यथाक्रमेण यतो
> विवेकात् सत्येन गच्छतो जनाननिमिषमव्यवधानेन सर्वदा रक्षमाणा पालयंतौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you surpass even the vast earth. Because प्र (*pra*) is seen elsewhere connected with रिरिच (*ririca*) (as in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-9 अस्येव प्र रिरिचे (*asyeva pra ririce*)), here too the verb रिरिचाथे (*riricāthe*) is to be supplied. Likewise you surpass the great (ऋष्वात् (*ṛṣvāt*)), by nature exceedingly vast heaven, O good givers. Moreover you bear (दधाथे (*dadhāthe*)) beauty/form (स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*)) in the plants and in all creatures — or, as causes, in creatures. Doing what? Since, in due order, with discrimination, you protect without interval, always guarding, the people who proceed by truth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, you
- उरोः (*uroḥ*)—of the vast
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—than the earth, more
- प्र (*pra*)—you have grown beyond
- सुदानू (*sudānū*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa of excellent giving
- ऋष्वात् (*ṛṣvāt*)—of surpassing qualities
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of great nature
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—than heaven, more

### Printed p. 429
- प्र (*pra*)—you have grown beyond it
- ऋधक् यतः (*ṛdhak yataḥ*)—the people who conduct themselves on the path of truth
- अनिमिषं (*animiṣaṃ*)—always
- रक्षमाणा (*rakṣamāṇā*)—protecting
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the plants
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—in the people
- स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*)—beautiful form
- दधाथे (*dadhāthe*)—you have placed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you have grown beyond the vast earth. O Mitra and Varuṇa of excellent giving, you have grown beyond heaven, which is full of surpassing qualities and of great nature. Always protecting the people who conduct themselves on the path of truth, you have placed beautiful form in the plants and in the people.

##### English translation
You are vaster, Mitra and Varuna, than the ample earth, vaster, bounteous donors, than the glorious and expansive heaven : you maintain beauty in plants and in people, deligent observers of truth, and vigilantly protecting (us).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्र (*pra*)—प्र रिरिचाथे (*pra riricāthe*). In this Ṛk there is no verb with the preposition प्र (*pra*), so the verb रिरिचाथे (*riricāthe*) is to be supplied and joined. The bhāṣyakāra explains that, since in the earlier Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-9, with the same context, अस्येदेव प्र रिरिचे (*asyedeva pra ririce*) the verb रिरिचे (*ririce*) is used with the preposition प्र (*pra*), and since generally रिरिचे (*ririce*) is seen used with the word प्र (*pra*), it is proper to supply that verb here too, and he has construed the meaning accordingly.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शंसा॑ मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॒ शुष्मो॒ रोद॑सी बद्बधे महि॒त्वा  
> अय॒न्मासा॒ अय॑ज्ञनाम॒वीराः॒ प्र य॒ज्ञम॑न्मा वृ॒जनं॑ तिराते ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शंस । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धाम । शुष्मः । रोदसी इति । बद्बधे । महित्वा ।  
> अयन् । मासाः । अयज्ञनां । अवीराः । प्र । यज्ञ-मन्मा । वृजनं । तिराते ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 430

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च धाम तेजःस्थानं शंस । स्तुहि । ययोर्देवयोः शुष्मो बलं रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ सह वर्तमाने महित्वा स्वमहत्त्वेन
> बद्बधे बध्नाति पृथक्कारयति इयं पृथिवीयं द्यौरिति पृथक्करोति । द्यावापृथिवी
> सहास्तामिति श्रुतेः ॥ अयज्ञनामननुष्ठातृणां मासाः कालावयवा अवीरा अपुत्रा
> एवायन् । यंतु । गच्छंतु । तद्विपरीतो यज्ञमन्मा यज्ञार्थं मतिमान्यजमानो
> वृजनं बलं प्र तिराते । प्रवर्धयतु । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, praise the abode (धाम (*dhāma*)), the place of radiance, of Mitra and Varuṇa, whose strength (शुष्मः (*śuṣmaḥ*)) by its own greatness (महित्वा (*mahitvā*)) binds (बद्बधे (*badbadhe*)) heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), which were together, and separates them: "this is earth, this is heaven", as the śruti says द्यावापृथिवी सहास्तामिति (*dyāvāpṛthivī sahāstāmiti*). For those who do not sacrifice, may the months, the parts of time, go by childless (अवीरा (*avīrā*)). Contrary to them, may the sacrificer, whose mind is on sacrifice (यज्ञमन्मा (*yajñamanmā*)), increase his strength (वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)); तिरति (*tirati*) with प्र (*pra*) has the sense of increase.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुष्मः (*śuṣmaḥ*)—whose strength, of Mitra and Varuṇa
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth that were together
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by its greatness
- बद्बधे (*badbadhe*)—set apart
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- धाम (*dhāma*)—the radiant abode
- शंस (*śaṃsa*)—praise
- अयज्ञनां (*ayajñanāṃ*)—of those without performance of sacrifice
- मासाः (*māsāḥ*)—the times
- अवीराः (*avīrāḥ*)—without sons and the like
- अयन् (*ayan*)—let them pass
- यज्ञमन्मा (*yajñamanmā*)—one whose mind is on performing sacrifice
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—his own strength
- प्र तिराते (*pra tirāte*)—let him increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise the radiant abode of those Mitra and Varuṇa whose strength by its greatness set apart heaven and earth, which were at first together. For those who do not perform sacrifice, let their life pass without wealth such as sons. Let the sacrificer, whose mind is on action, increase his own strength.

##### English translation
Praise the splendour of Mitra and Varuna, whose strength, by its mightiness, keeps heaven and earth asunder : may the days of those who offer not worship pass without male descendants : may he who delights in sacrifice increase in prosperity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रोदसी (*rodasī*)—In the beginning, heaven and earth, that is, the earth and the sky, were joined together. There is an ancient story that Mitra and Varuṇa by their greatness separated them and established the atmosphere in the middle. It is said that the śruti sentence द्यावापृथिवी सहास्तां (*dyāvāpṛthivī sahāstāṃ*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-3-2) supports this.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अमू॑रा॒ विश्वा॑ वृषणावि॒मा वां॒ न यासु॑ चि॒त्रं ददृ॑शे॒ न य॒क्षं

### Printed p. 431

> द्रुहः सचंते अनृता जनानां न वां निण्यान्यचिते अभूवन् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अमूरा । विश्वा । वृषणौ । इमाः । वां । न । यासु । चित्रं । ददृशे । न । यक्षं ।  
> द्रुहः । सचंते । अनृता । जनानां । न । वां । निण्यानि । अचिते । अभूवन् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अमूरामूढौ हे विश्वा व्याप्तौ हे वृषणौ वर्षितारौ वां युवाभ्यामिवा इमानि स्तुतिवचांसि क्रियंते । यासु स्तुतिषु चित्रमाश्चर्यं न ददृशे न दृश्यते न यक्षं न पूजा दृश्यते । युवाभ्यां महिम्नोऽपि महत्त्वात् प्रयत्नेन क्रियमाणमपि स्तोत्रं न चमत्करोतीत्यर्थः । जनानामनृतास्तुत्यविषयाणि स्तोत्राणि द्रुहो द्रोग्धारः सचंते । सेवंते । न महांतः वां युवाभ्यां क्रियुमाणानि निण्यान्यंतर्हितानि रहस्यान्यपि स्तोत्राण्यचितेऽज्ञानाय नाभूवन् । न भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O undeluded (अमूरा (*amūrā*)), all-pervading (विश्वा (*viśvā*)), showering (वृषणौ (*vṛṣaṇau*)) ones, these praise-words are made for you; in them no wonder is seen (न ददृशे (*na dadṛśe*)), no worship (न यक्षं (*na yakṣaṃ*)) is seen. Since your greatness is greater still, a hymn made even with effort does not astonish. The untruthful hymns of men, directed to unpraiseworthy ends, are attended by injurers (द्रुहः (*druhaḥ*)). But the hymns made by us for you, though hidden and secret, do not come to be unknown (अचिते (*acite*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमूरा (*amūrā*)—discriminating
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all-pervading
- वृषणौ (*vṛṣaṇau*)—givers of desired ends, O Mitra and Varuṇa
- यासु (*yāsu*)—in which praises
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—what marvels
- न ददृशे (*na dadṛśe*)—are not seen
- न यक्षं (*na yakṣaṃ*)—no materials of worship exist
- इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these praise-words
- वां (*vāṃ*)—are offered to you
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of dishonest people
- अनृता (*anṛtā*)—false words
- द्रुहः (*druhaḥ*)—being injurious
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—are attended
- वां (*vāṃ*)—directed to you
- निण्यानि (*niṇyāni*)—even though the praise-words are secret
- अचिते (*acite*)—without being attended by you
- न अभूवन् (*na abhūvan*)—they are not

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O discriminating, all-pervading givers of desired ends, Mitra and Varuṇa, the evil words of wicked people, in whose praises there are neither marvels nor materials of worship, are offered to you. Such dishonest and injurious words make you angry. But the praises offered by us, who are honest, even though secret, do fall under your notice. You certainly attend to them.

##### English translation
Unperplexed, all-pervading showerers (of benefits), these (praises) are for you, in which nothing surprising, no adoration (worthy of you), is

### Printed p. 432
beheld : the insincere commendations of men serve as offences : eulogies of you, although offered in secret, are not unappreciated.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समु॑ वां य॒ज्ञं म॑हयं॒ नमो॑भिर्हु॒वे वां॑ मित्रावरुणा स॒बाधः॑ ।  
> प्र वां॒ मन्मा॑न्यृ॒चसे॒ नवा॑नि कृ॒तानि॒ ब्रह्म॑ जुजुषन्नि॒मानि॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सम् । ऊं इति । वां । यज्ञं । महयं । नमः-भिः । हुवे । वां । मित्रावरुणा । स-बाधः ।  
> प्र । वां । मन्मानि । ऋचसे । नवानि । कृतानि । ब्रह्म । जुजुषन् । इमानि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवयोर्यज्ञं नमोभिर्नमस्कारैः स्तुतिभिः समु
> महयं । संपूजयाम्यहं । तदर्थं हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ वां सबाधो बाधायुक्तोऽहं हुवे ॥ आह्वयामि बाधापरिहाराय । वां युवामृचसे
> सेवितुं नवानि नूतनानि स्तुत्यानि वा मन्मानि स्तोत्राणि प्र भवंत्वित्यध्याहारः । कृतानि मया समूहीकृतानीदानीं क्रियमाणानि ब्रह्म परिवृढानि स्तोत्राणि
> इमानि वां जुजुषन् । प्रीणयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, I honour (महयं (*mahayaṃ*)) your sacrifice with salutations (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)), that is, with praises. For that purpose I, afflicted (सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)), call (हुवे (*huve*)) you, for the removal of affliction. "May new, praiseworthy hymns come forth to serve you" — this is the supplied clause. The hymns made (कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)) by me, gathered together and now being made, these extensive praises (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)), may they please (जुजुषन् (*jujuṣan*)) you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Mitra and Varuṇa) वां (*vāṃ*)—directed to you
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—accompanied by salutations

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa

- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- हुवे (*huve*)—I call
- वां (*vāṃ*)—to serve you
- ऋचसे (*ṛcase*)—to serve
- नवानि (*navāni*)—new
- मन्मानि (*manmāni*)—hymns
- प्र (भवंति) (*pra (bhavaṃti)*)—are composed
- कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)—made by me
- इमानि ब्रह्म (*imāni brahma*)—these hymns
- जुजुषन् (*jujuṣan*)—may they gladden you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, I offer to you the sacrifice accompanied by salutations in the form of worship. O Mitra and Varuṇa, I, beset by injury, call you. You

Rest of the Bhāvārtha, continuing: the new hymns are composed to serve you; may these hymns composed by me gratify you.

#### Ṛk 7

> विश्वा॑नि दु॒र्गा पि॑पृतं ति॒रो नो॑ यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । देवा । पुरः-हितिः । युव-भ्यां । यज्ञेषु । मित्रावरुणौ । अकारि ।  
> विश्वानि । दुः-गा । पिपृतं । तिरः । नः । यूयं । पात । स्वस्ति-भिः । सदा । नः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया स्तुतिमुपसंहरति । हे देवा देवौ मित्रावरुणौ युवभ्यां युवाभ्यां यज्ञेष्वियं पुरोहितिः पुरस्क्रिया पूजा स्तुतिलक्षणाकारि । कृताभूत् ॥ तां
> सेवित्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि दुर्गा दुःखेन गंतव्यान्यापदस्तिरः । तिरस्कुरुतं । तथा कृत्वा
> नोऽस्मान् पिपृतं पारयतं । शिष्टो गतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk he concludes the praise. O divine Mitra and Varuṇa, in the sacrifices this पुरोहितिः (*purohitiḥ*) has been made for you two; it means the foremost rite, worship in the form of praise. Having accepted it, set aside all difficulties, the calamities hard to pass through, and having done so carry us across. शिष्टो गतः (*śiṣṭo gataḥ*).

### Printed p. 434

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, divine ones, the worship in the form of praise offered before you has been accomplished in the sacrifices. Accepting it, destroy all calamities. Carry us across difficulty. Always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
To you, divine Mitra and Varna, to you this adoration at sacrifice is addressed : remove from us all difficulties, and ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 62 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत्सूर्य इति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका ॥ उत्सूर्यः
> षळाद्यास्तिस्रः सौर्य इति । वसिष्ठ ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । आद्यास्तिस्रः सूर्यदेवत्याः शिष्टा मित्रावरुणदेवत्याः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

उत्सूर्य (*utsūrya*) is a hymn of six Ṛks, the seventh hymn. The Anukramaṇikā says: उत्सूर्यः षळाद्यास्तिस्रः सौर्य (*utsūryaḥ ṣaḷādyāstisraḥ saurya*). The seer is Vasiṣṭha; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The first three Ṛks have Sūrya as deity, the rest Mitra and Varuṇa. The hymn's application is as indicated by the characteristic mark (लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*)).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning उत्सूर्यः (*utsūryaḥ*) is the seventh hymn in the fourth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says उत्सूर्यः षळाद्यास्तिस्रः सौर्यः (*utsūryaḥ ṣaḷādyāstisraḥ sauryaḥ*). Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this hymn; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the first three Ṛks have Sūrya as deity; the remaining Ṛks have Mitra and Varuṇa. The hymn's application is Laiṅgika.

Sūkta 62. Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 62. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 5; Varga 4. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 6.
Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: 1–3 Sūrya; 4–6 Mitra and Varuṇa. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्सूर्यो॑ बृ॒हद॒र्चिंष्य॑श्रेत् पु॒रु विश्वा॒ जनि॑म॒ मानु॑षाणां ।  
> स॒मो दि॒वा द॑दृशे॒ रोच॑मानः॒ क्रत्वा॑ कृ॒तः सुकृ॑तः क॒र्तृभि॑र्भूत् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 435

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । सूर्यः । बृहत् । अर्चींषि । अश्रेत् । पुरु । विश्वा । जनिम । मानुषाणां ।  
> समः । दिवा । ददृशे । रोचमानः । क्रत्वा । कृतः । सुऽकृतः । कर्तृऽभिः । भूत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रेरको देवो बृहदत्यधिकं पुरु पुरूणि बहून्यर्चिंषि तेजांस्युदश्रेत् । ऊर्ध्वं श्रयति । किं प्रति । मानुषाणां मनुष्याणां विश्वा सर्वाणि जनिम जनिमानि जनान् । जनशब्दः संघवचनः । तान्प्रत्युदश्रेत् । स देवो दिवाहनि रोचमानः सन् समो ददृशे । एकरूपः प्रतिनियतः सन्दृश्यते । तस्मात्पुरुषं पुरुषं प्रत्यादित्यो भवतीति हि श्रुतिः । स देवः क्रत्वा सर्वस्य कर्ता कृतः संपादितः प्रजापतिना कर्तृभिः स्तुतिकर्तृभिः सुकृतः स्तुत्या तीक्ष्णीकृतो भूत् । भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sūrya, the god who impels all, raises up his abundant and manifold rays, his splendours, upward. Towards what? Towards all the races (जनिम (*janima*)) of men, the people; the word जन (*jana*) denotes a multitude. He, shining by day, is seen as the same, of one form, firmly fixed for each. Hence the Śruti: पुरुषं पुरुषं प्रत्यादित्यो भवतीति (*puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyādityo bhavatīti*). That god, the maker of all through his power (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)), is made by Prajāpati; he is well made, sharpened by the praise of the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya, the impeller of all
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- पुरु (*puru*)—and manifold
- अर्चींषि (*arcīṃṣi*)—his rays
- उदश्रेत् (*udaśret*)—spreads upward
- मानुषाणां (*mānuṣāṇāṃ*)—of men
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- जनिम (*janima*)—over the crowds he spreads his rays
- दिवा (*divā*)—in the days
- रोचमानः (*rocamānaḥ*)—shining
- समः (*samaḥ*)—in one manner by all
- ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)—is seen
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—the maker of all
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—himself made by Prajāpati, Sūrya
- कर्तृभिः (*kartṛbhiḥ*)—by the praisers
- सुकृतः (*sukṛtaḥ*)—well refined
- भूत् (*bhūt*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sūrya, the impeller of all, spreads upward his abundant and manifold rays. He spreads his rays over all the crowds of men. Shining in those days he is seen by all in one manner. Sūrya, the maker of all and himself made by Prajāpati, becomes one well refined by the praisers.

##### English translation
Sury aspreads his vast and numerous rays over all the crowds of men; shining bright by day, he is beheld (by all) the same, the creator, the created, he is glorified by his worshippers.

> प्र नो॑ मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय वो॒चोऽना॑गसो अर्य॒म्णे  
> अ॒ग्नये॑ च ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । सूर्य । प्रति । पुरः । नः । उत् । गाः । एभिः । स्तोमेभिः । एतशेभिः । एवैः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सूर्य स प्रसिद्धस्त्वं नोऽस्मान्प्रति पुरः पुरस्तादुद्गाः । उद्गच्छ । कैः साधनैः । एभिः स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैः स्तुत्यैरेतशेभिरेतवर्णैः ॥ स्वार्थिकः शकारः यो जरंता युवशा ता । ऋ- १-१६१-६ । पुरुषः कृष्णशवास्येत्तरतः । ऐ. ब्रा. ५-१४. इत्यादिवत् ॥ तादृशैरेवैर्गमनशीलैरश्वैरुद्गाः । अथ तथा कृत्वास्माभिः स्तुतः सन्नोऽस्माननागसोऽपापान् प्र वोचः । केभ्यः । मित्राय वरुणायार्यम्णेऽग्नये च । अत्र सौर्य इतरेषां मित्रादीनां संकीर्तनं तेषामपि निपातभाक्त्वादविरुद्धं । एवं पूर्वत्रोत्तरत्र च मैत्रावरुणेऽर्यमादीनां संकीर्तनमपि न विरुध्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūrya, you, the renowned one, rise before us. By what means? With these praises, with एतशेभिः (*etaśebhiḥ*), horses of variegated colour (the श (*śa*) is pleonastic), as in यो जरंता युवशा ता (*yo jaraṃtā yuvaśā tā*) (Ṛ. 1-161-6) and पुरुषः कृष्णशवास्येत्तरतः (*puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśavāsyettarataḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 5-14). Rise with such swift-moving horses. Then, praised by us, declare us sinless to Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman and Agni. Here, in a hymn to Sūrya, the mention of the other deities, Mitra and the rest, is not inconsistent, since they too share in the particle; likewise, before and after, in a hymn to Mitra and Varuṇa the mention of Aryaman and others is not inconsistent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्य (*sūrya*)—O Sūrya
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the renowned
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—with praiseworthy
- एतशेभिः (*etaśebhiḥ*)—and radiant
- एभिः एवैः (*ebhiḥ evaiḥ*)—together with these horses
- नः प्रति (*naḥ prati*)—facing us
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front of us
- उद्गाः (*udgāḥ*)—rise and come
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—to Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuṇa
- अर्यम्णे (*aryamṇe*)—to Aryaman
- अग्नये च (*agnaye ca*)—and before Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*)—as sinless
- प्र वोचः (*pra vocaḥ*)—declare openly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Sūrya, you, the renowned, together with your praiseworthy and radiant horses, rise and come facing us, in front of us. Before Mitra, and before Aryaman and Agni, declare us sinless and make it known.

> स्तवानाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्मभ्यं शुरुधः शुचेर्दुःखस्य प्रतिरोद्धार ऋतावानः सत्यवंतो वरुणादयः सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याकं धनं विरदंतु वितरंतु । अथवा शुरुध उक्तलक्षणाः सहस्रसंख्याका ओषधी रदंतु । किं च ते चंद्रा आह्लादकारिणोऽस्मभ्यमुपमं स्तुत्यमर्कमर्चनीयं यच्छंतु । किंच स्तवाना अस्माभिः स्तूयमाना नोऽस्माकं काममपेक्षितं पूपुरंतु । पूरयंतु । हे सूर्य त्वयानुज्ञाता इति सूर्यस्य स्तुतिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Varuṇa and the others, the शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*) (warders-off of *śuci*, sorrow) and ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*) (possessed of truth), distribute to us a thousandfold wealth. Or else, the शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*) so defined are the thousand herbs; let them eat... [as given: ओषधी रदंतु (*oṣadhī radaṃtu*)]. Moreover, may those delightful ones grant us the उपमं (*upamaṃ*), the praiseworthy अर्कं (*arkaṃ*), the worshipful. And praised by us, may they fulfil our desire, what is wished for. O Sūrya, "permitted by you": thus it is praise of Sūrya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*)—destroyers of sorrow
- ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*)—guardians of truth
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—a thousandfold wealth
- विरदंतु (*viradaṃtu*)—let them give us
- चंद्राः (*caṃdrāḥ*)—these delighting gods
- उपमं (*upamaṃ*)—extraordinary
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—and worshipful food
- नः यच्छंतु (*naḥ yacchaṃtu*)—let them give us
- स्तवानाः (*stavānāḥ*)—these gods praised by us
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—desire
- आ पूपुरंतु (*ā pūpuraṃtu*)—let them fill and give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni, destroyers of sorrow and guardians of truth, give us a thousandfold wealth. May these delighting gods give us extraordinary and worshipful food. May these gods, praised by us, fulfil our desires.

### Printed p. 438

##### English translation
May Varuna, Mitra, and Agni, the alleviators of pain, the observers of truth, bestow upon us thousands (of riches) : may they, the givers of delight, grant us excellent (food) : glorified by us, may they fulfil our desires

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्यावा॑भूमी अदिते॒ त्रासी॑थां नो॒ ये वां॑ ज॒ज्ञुः सु॒जनि॑मान ऋष्वे ।  
> मा हेळे॑ भूम॒ वरु॑णस्य वा॒योर्मा मि॒त्रस्य॑ प्रि॒यत॑मस्य नृ॒णां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्यावाभूमी इति । अदिते । त्रासीथां । नः । ये । वां । जज्ञुः । सुऽजनिमानः । ऋष्वे इति ।  
> मा । हेळे । भूम । वरुणस्य । वायोः । मा । मित्रस्य । प्रियऽतमस्य । नृणां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे द्यावाभूमी द्यावापृथिव्यौ हे अदितेऽखंडनीये । एतद्द्यावाभूम्योरेवैकवचनेन संबोधनं । हे ऋष्वे । महन्नामैतत् । हे महत्यौ नोऽस्मांस्त्रासीथां । रक्षतं । ये वयं सुजनिमानः शोभनजन्मानो वां युवां जज्ञुः । ज्ञातवंतः स्म । किं च वयं वरुणस्य हेळे क्रोधे मा भूम । तथा वायोर्मा भूम । तथा नृणां स्तुतिनेतृणां मनुष्याणां प्रियतमस्य मित्रस्य हेळे मा भूम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, the unbreakable: this is a single-number address to Heaven and Earth alone. O ऋष्वे (*ṛṣve*)—this is a name meaning "great"—O great ones, protect us, who, well born, have known you. And may we not come under the anger (हेळे (*heḷe*)) of Varuṇa, nor of Vāyu, nor under the anger of Mitra, the dearest of men (नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*), the leaders in praise).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदिते (*adite*)—O ones of perfect nature
- ऋष्वे (*ṛṣve*)—and of greatness
- द्यावाभूमी (*dyāvābhūmī*)—O Heaven and Earth
- ये (*ye*)—we who
- सुजनिमानः (*sujanimānaḥ*)—of excellent births
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your greatness
- जज्ञुः (*jajñuḥ*)—have known; such
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- त्रासीथां (*trāsīthāṃ*)—protect
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- हेळे (*heḷe*)—to the anger
- मा भूम (*mā bhūma*)—cause us not to fall subject (we)
- वायोः (*vāyoḥ*)—do not make us objects of Vāyu's wrath either
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—to men
- प्रियतमस्य (*priyatamasya*)—who does exceeding good
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra's wrath also
- मा (*mā*)—may we not become subject

### Printed p. 439

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, whose nature is whole and undivided and who are possessed of majesty: protect us who, being of good birth, have come to know your greatness. Let us not fall under the wrath of Varuna. Let us not become objects of the anger of Vayu, nor of the anger of Mitra, who is beneficial to men.

##### English translation
Indivisible and mighty heaven and earth protect us who, of fortunate birth, have knowledge of you both : let us not incur the displeasure of Varuna, or of Vayu, or of Mitra, the best beloved of men.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र बा॒हवा॑ सिसृतं जी॒वसे॑ न॒ आ नो॒ गव्यू॑तिमुक्षतं घृ॒तेन॑ ।  
> आ नो॒ जने॑ श्रवयतं युवाना श्रु॒तं मे॑ मित्रावरुणा॒ हवे॒मा ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । बाहवा । सिसृतं । जीवसे । नः । आ । नः । गव्यूतिं । उक्षतं । घृतेन ।  
> आ । नः । जने । श्रवयतं । युवाना । श्रुतं । मे । मित्रावरुणा । हवा । इमा ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र बाहवेति पंचमी मैत्रावरुणे पशौ पशुपुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे नो यद्वंहिष्ठं नातिविधे सुदानू । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ देवौ बाहवा युवाभ्यां बाहू प्र सिसृतं ।
> प्रसारयतं हविःस्वीकाराय धनप्रदानाय वा । किमर्थमिति । नो जीवसेऽस्माकं
> जीवनाय । किंच नोऽस्माकं गव्यूतिं गावो यंति गच्छंत्यत्रेति गव्यूतिर्गोमार्गभूमिः । तां तृणादिप्ररोहाय घृतेनोदकेन समंतादुक्षतं । सिंचतं ।
> किंच नोऽस्माकं जनेऽस्मत्समाने मनुष्यसमूहे वा नोऽस्मान् श्रवयतं । विश्रुतं
> कुरुतं । हे युवाना नित्ययौवनौ सर्वत्र व्याप्तौ वा युवां मे ममेमानि
> हवाह्वानानि श्रुतं । शृणुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fifth Ṛk, प्र बाहवेति (*pra bāhaveti*), is the yājyā for the animal's cake-offering (paśupuroḍāśa) in the animal sacrifice to Mitra and Varuna. It is stated in the sūtra: प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे न आ नो गव्यूतिमुक्षतं घृतेन । आ नो जने श्रवयतं युवाना श्रुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमा ॥ ५ ॥ प्र । बाहवा । सिसृतं । जीवसे । नः । आ । नः । गव्यूतिं । उक्षतं । घृतेन । आ । नः । जने । श्रवयतं । युवाना । श्रुतं । मे । मित्रावरुणा । हवा । इमा ॥ ५ ॥ प्र बाहवेति पंचमी मैत्रावरुणे पशौ पशुपुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे नो यद्वंहिष्ठं नातिविधे सुदानू । (*pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase na ā no gavyūtimukṣataṃ ghṛtena | ā no jane śravayataṃ yuvānā śrutaṃ me mitrāvaruṇā havemā ‖ 5 ‖ pra | bāhavā | sisṛtaṃ | jīvase | naḥ | ā | naḥ | gavyūtiṃ | ukṣataṃ | ghṛtena | ā | naḥ | jane | śravayataṃ | yuvānā | śrutaṃ | me | mitrāvaruṇā | havā | imā ‖ 5 ‖ pra bāhaveti paṃcamī maitrāvaruṇe paśau paśupuroḍāśasya yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase no yadvaṃhiṣṭhaṃ nātividhe sudānū |*) (Ā. 3-8). O Mitra and Varuna, stretch forth your arms to accept the oblation or to bestow wealth. Why? For our life. Further, the गव्यूति (*gavyūti*) is the land where cows walk (गावो यंति (*gāvo yaṃti*)); sprinkle it all round with घृत (*ghṛta*), meaning water, so that grass and the like may grow. Further, make us heard of, famous, among our own people or among the multitude of men. O ever-youthful, or all-pervading, ones, hear these my invocations.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuna, stretch out both your arms at length for our good life. Drench with water, everywhere, the land where our cows roam. Make us renowned before good people. You who are ever young, hear this invocation of mine.

##### English translation

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal offering made to Mitra and Varuna, at the offering of the cake (puroḍāśa), this Ṛk प्र बाहवा (*pra bāhavā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे नो यद्वंहिष्ठं नातिविधे सुदानू (*pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase no yadvaṃhiṣṭhaṃ nātividhe sudānū*) (Ā. 3-8).

> मित्रो वरुणोऽर्यमा चैते त्रयो देवा न्नद्य नोऽस्माकं त्मन आत्मन आत्महिताय तोकाय पुत्राय च वरिवो धनं दधंतु । प्रयच्छंतु । नोऽस्माकं विश्वा सर्वाणि गंतव्यानि सुगा सुगमनानि सुपथानि च संतु । भवंतु । शिष्पं गतं ॥

## Sūkta 63 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उद्वेतीति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । आद्याश्चतस्रः पंचम्याः पूर्वार्धश्च सूर्यदेवत्या अवशिष्टास्त्रयोऽर्धर्चा मित्रावरुणदेवत्याः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । उद्वेतीति चार्धपंचम्या इति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta उद्वेतीति (*udvetīti*) has six Ṛks and is the eighth sūkta. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The first four Ṛks and the first half of the fifth have Sūrya as deity; the remaining three half-verses (one and a half Ṛks) have Mitra and Varuna. So the Anukramaṇī: उद्वेतीति चार्धपंचम्या इति (*udvetīti cārdhapaṃcamyā iti*). The application (viniyoga) is by indication (लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*)).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta उद्वेति (*udveti*) is the eighth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; its metre is Triṣṭubh. In this sūkta the first four Ṛks and the first half of the fifth have Sūrya as deity. The remaining three half-Ṛks, that is, one and a half Ṛks, have Mitra and Varuna as deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: उद्वेतीति चार्धपंचम्याः (*udvetīti cārdhapaṃcamyāḥ*). The application is by indication.

- Metre: Triṣṭubh

> चक्षु॑र्मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य दे॒वश्चर्मे॑व॒ यः स॒मुवि॑व्य॒क्तमां॑सि ‖१‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ऊं इति । एति । सुभगः । विश्वचक्षाः । साधारणः । सूर्यः । मानुषाणां ।  
> चक्षुः । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । देवः । चर्मऽइव । यः । सम्ऽअविव्यक् । तमांसि

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उद्वेति उद्गच्छत्ययं सूर्यः सुभगः शोभनभाग्यः सुषु भजनीयो वा विश्वचक्षाः सर्वस्य द्रष्टा मानुषाणां सर्वेषां मनुष्याणां साधारणः । साधारणत्वप्रतिपादकश्रुतिः पूर्वमुदाहृता । मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च चक्षुः प्रकाशको देवो द्योतमानः । यो देवश्चर्मेव चर्मणेव तमांसि समुविव्यक् सह विचति संवेष्टयति स महानुभावो देव उद्वेति ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Sūrya rises: auspicious (सुभगः (*subhagaḥ*)), of good fortune or well worth worshipping; विश्वचक्षाः (*viśvacakṣāḥ*), the seer of all; साधारणः (*sādhāraṇaḥ*), common to all men. The Śruti that teaches his commonness has been cited earlier. He is the eye, the illuminator, of Mitra and Varuna, a shining god. The god who envelops (संवेष्टयति (*saṃveṣṭayati*)) the darknesses as a skin does (चर्मेव (*carmeva*); समुविव्यक् (*samuvivyak*) means "he covers all round"), that god of great power rises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- चर्मेव (*carmeva*)—spread like a skin
- तमांसि (*tamāṃsi*)—the black darkness
- समुविव्यक् (*samuvivyak*)—who completely disperses, such a one
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—for Mitra
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—for Varuna
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—who is like an eye
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—divine in nature
- मानुषाणां (*mānuṣāṇāṃ*)—for all men
- साधारणः (*sādhāraṇaḥ*)—who appears alike to all
- विश्वचक्षाः (*viśvacakṣāḥ*)—who can see everything
- सुभगः (*subhagaḥ*)—auspicious
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya
- उद्वेति (*udveti*)—rises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sūrya rises: he who completely disperses the black darkness spread like a skin, who is like an eye to Mitra and Varuna, divine in nature, appearing alike to all men, able to see everything, and auspicious.

### Printed p. 443

##### English translation
The auspicious Surya rises, the eye of all, the common (parent) of men : the divine eye of Mitra and of Varuna, who breaks through the glooms as through (investing) skin.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद्वे॑ति प्रसवी॒ता जना॑नां म॒हान्के॒तुर॑र्ण॒वः सूर्य॑स्य ।  
> स॒मा॒नं च॒क्रं प॑र्या॒विवृ॑त्स॒न्यदे॑त॒शो वह॑ति धू॒र्षु यु॒क्तः ‖२‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ऊं इति । एति । प्रसविता । जनानां । महान् । केतुः । अर्णवः । सूर्यस्य ।  
> समानं । चक्रं । परिऽआविवृत्सन् । यत् । एतशः । वहति । धूःसु । युक्तः

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सूर्यस्य सूर्यः ‖ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ‖ उद्वेति । उद्गच्छति । कीदृशोऽयं । जनानां सर्वेषां प्रसविता सर्वेषु कर्मस्वनुज्ञाता महान् पूज्यः केतुः सर्वस्य प्रज्ञापकोऽर्णव उदकप्रदः । किं कुर्वन्नुदेतीति उच्यते । समानं सर्वेषामेकरूपमेकमेव चक्रं रथांगं चरणशीलं रथं वा पर्याविवृत्सन् पर्यावर्तयितुमिच्छन् । यद्रथचक्रं धूर्षु रथस्य युक्तः एतश एतशवर्णो हरितवर्णोऽश्वो वहति । एको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा । ऋ. १-१६४-२ । इत्युक्तं ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*) here stands for सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*) (a change of case ending). He rises. What is he like? प्रसविता (*prasavitā*) of all people, the one who gives permission in all rites; great, worthy of worship; केतुः (*ketuḥ*), the one who makes everything known; अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*), the giver of water. What does he do as he rises? He wishes to turn round the one wheel (the chariot's wheel, or the moving chariot itself), alike for all, which the एतशः (*etaśaḥ*) (a horse of हरित (*harita*), green-tawny, colour), yoked at the chariot's poles, draws. It is said: एको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा (*eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-2).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—which chariot wheel
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—at the yoke of the chariot
- युक्तः (*yuktaḥ*)—that which is yoked
- एतशः (*etaśaḥ*)—the green-coloured horse
- वहति (*vahati*)—draws; such a one
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—the one common to the whole universe
- चक्रं (*cakraṃ*)—chariot wheel
- पर्याविवृत्सन् (*paryāvivṛtsan*)—wishing to turn
- महान् (*mahān*)—the worshipful
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—the one who makes known
- अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*)—the giver of water
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of all men
- प्रसविता (*prasavitā*)—the impeller of rites
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—Sūrya
- उद्वेति (*udveti*)—rises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sūrya rises, turning that chariot wheel, one for the whole universe, which the green-coloured horse yoked at the yoke of the chariot draws; he is worshipful, the one who makes known, the giver of water, and the impeller of rites for all men.

### Printed p. 444

##### English translation
The animator of men arises, the great rain-shedding banner of Surya rolling on the universal wheel, which the white steeds yoked to his car drag along.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒भ्राज॑मान उ॒षसा॑मु॒पस्था॑द्रे॒भैरुदे॑त्यनुम॒द्यमा॑न�ः ।  
> ए॒ष मे॑ दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता च॑च्छंद॒ यः स॑मा॒नं न प्र॑मि॒नाति॒ धाम॑ ‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विभ्राजमानः । उषसां । उपस्थात् । रेभैः । उत् । एति । अनुमद्यमानः ।  
> एषः । मे । देवः । सविता । चच्छंद । यः । समानं । न । प्रमिनाति । धाम

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सूर्यो विभ्राजमानो विशेषेण दीप्यमान उषसामुपस्थादुपस्थे मध्ये रेभैः स्तोत्रैरनुमद्यमानः सन्नुदेति । किंचैष देवो द्योतमानः सविता मे मह्यं चच्छंद । उपच्छंदयति कामान् । एष इत्युक्तं क इति । यो देवः समानं सर्वेषां प्राणिनामेकरूपं धाम स्वीयं तेजःस्थानं न प्रमिनाति न हिनस्ति न संकोचयति स देव उदेतीति ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Sūrya, shining brilliantly, rises being gladdened with praises (रेभैः (*rebhaiḥ*) means *stotraiḥ*) from the lap, the midst, of the dawns. Further, this shining god Savitṛ has fulfilled (चच्छंद (*cacchaṃda*), "he gratifies desires") my wishes. "This one" is said: who? The god who does not impair, harm or contract his own place of radiance (धाम (*dhāma*)), one in form for all beings, that god rises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which god
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—of one kind for the whole world
- धाम (*dhāma*)—his own radiance
- न प्रमिनाति (*na pramināti*)—does not diminish; such a one
- विभ्राजमानः (*vibhrājamānaḥ*)—who shines in a special manner
- रेभैः (*rebhaiḥ*)—by the praisers
- अनुमद्यमानः (*anumadyamānaḥ*)—who is gratified
- उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)—of the dawns
- उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)—from the midst
- उदेति (*udeti*)—comes rising
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—divine in nature
- एषः सविता (*eṣaḥ savitā*)—this Savitṛ
- मे (*me*)—to me
- चच्छंद (*cacchaṃda*)—fills with desired objects

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sūrya, who does not diminish his radiance, one in kind for the whole world, who shines in a special manner and is gratified by the praisers, comes rising from the midst of the dawns. This Savitṛ, divine in nature, fills my desired objects.

### Printed p. 445
Delighted by the praises (of his worshippers), the radiant sun rises from the lap of the dawns: that divine sun gratifies my desires, who limits not the lustre that is common (to all).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वो रु॒क्म उ॑रु॒चक्षा॒ उदे॑ति दू॒रेअ॑र्थस्त॒रणि॒र्भ्राज॑मानः ।  
> नू॒नं जनाः॒ सूर्ये॑ण॒ प्रसू॑ता॒ अय॒न्नर्था॑नि कृ॒णव॒न्नपां॑सि ‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः । रुक्मः । उरुचक्षाः । उत् । एति । दूरेअर्थः । तरणिः । भ्राजमानः ।  
> नूनं । जनाः । सूर्येण । प्रसूताः । अयन् । अर्थानि । कृणवन् । अपांसि

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सूर्यो रुक्मो रोचमान उरुचक्षाः प्रभूततेजाश्च सन्दिवोऽंतरिक्षादुदेति । यद्वा । दिवोऽंतरिक्षस्य रुक्म आभरणस्थानीयः । कीदृशोऽयं । दूरेअर्थो दूरेगंता ‖ अर्थोऽर्तेः ‖ दूरे प्रार्थ्यमानो वा । तरणिस्तारको भ्राजमानो दीप्यमानः सन्नुदेति । नूनं निश्चयं जनाः सर्वे प्राणिनः सूर्येण प्रेरकेण देवेन प्रसूता अनुज्ञाताः प्रेरिताः संतोऽर्थानि गंतव्यान्यनुष्ठेयान्यपांसि कर्माणि कृणवन् । कुर्वंति ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sun, shining (रुक्मो (*rukmo*)) and of abundant lustre (उरुचक्षाः (*urucakṣāḥ*)), rises from the sky, the atmosphere. Or else: he is the ornament (रुक्म (*rukma*)) of the sky. What is he like? दूरेअर्थः (*dūrearthaḥ*) means one who travels far, or one who is sought from afar. He is तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*), the one who carries across, and rises blazing. Surely all living beings, impelled and permitted by Sūrya, the impelling god, go to and perform the works that are to be gone to and carried out.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दूरे अर्थः (*dūre arthaḥ*)—one who travels very far
- तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*)—one who crosses the atmosphere
- भ्राजमानः (*bhrājamānaḥ*)—the shining one
- रुक्मः (*rukmaḥ*)—the golden-hued one
- उरुचक्षाः (*urucakṣāḥ*)—the one of exceeding lustre; the sun
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- उदेति (*udeti*)—rises
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—certainly
- जनाः (*janāḥ*)—all living beings
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—by the sun
- प्रसूताः (*prasūtāḥ*)—impelled
- आयन् (*āyan*)—turned toward their duties
- अर्थानि (*arthāni*)—their works to be performed
- अपांसि (*apāṃsi*)—works
- कृणवन् (*kṛṇavan*)—do

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sun, who travels very far, crosses the atmosphere, shines, is golden-hued and of exceeding lustre, rises from the atmosphere. All living beings

### Printed p. 446
impelled by the sun and turned toward their duties, perform their works to be performed; that is, all, impelled by the sun, turn to their duties and do their works.

##### English translation
The bright and glorious sun rises from the firmament far-going, traversing (the heavens), diffusing light: verily all brings animated by Surya proceed and execute their assigned labours.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्रा॑ च॒क्रुर॒मृता॑ गा॒तुम॑स्मै श्ये॒नो न दीय॒न्नन्वे॑ति॒ पाथः॑ ।  
> प्रति॑ वां॒ सूर॒ उदि॑ते विधेम॒ नमो॑भिर्मित्रावरुणो॒त ह॒व्यैः ‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । चक्रुः । अमृताः । गातुं । अस्मै । श्येनः । न । दीयन् । अनु । एति । पाथः ।  
> प्रति । वां । सूरे । उत्ऽइते । विधेम । नमःभिः । मित्रावरुणा । उत । हव्यैः

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिन्नंतरिक्षेऽमृता अमरणधर्माणः पूर्वे देवाः अस्मै सूर्याय गातुं मार्गं चक्रुः अकुर्वन् तत्पाथोऽंतरिक्षमन्वेति । अनुगच्छति । क इव । दीयन् गच्छन् श्येनो न शंसनीयगमनो गृध्र इव । अयमर्थर्चः सौर्य इत्युक्तं । हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ वां युवां सूरे सूर्य उदिते सति प्रातःसवने नमोभिर्नमस्कारैः स्तुतिभिरुतापि च हव्यैर्हविर्भिश्च प्रति विधेम । परिचरेम ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the atmosphere where the immortal, deathless ancient gods made a path for this Sūrya, along that path, the atmosphere, he goes, like a hawk (श्येनो (*śyeno*)) of praised flight, a vulture, darting along. This half-Ṛk, it is said, is addressed to Sūrya. "O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the sun has risen, at the morning libation, we serve you with salutations, that is, praises, and with oblations."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which atmosphere
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—the gods free from the nature of death
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this sun
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—the path of travel
- चक्रुः (*cakruḥ*)—made
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—in that same atmospheric path
- दीयन् (*dīyan*)—moving swiftly
- श्येनो न (*śyeno na*)—like a hawk
- अन्वेति (*anveti*)—the sun travels
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- सूरे उदिते (*sūre udite*)—when the sun has risen (at the time of the morning libation)
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with salutations
- उत (*uta*)—and
- हव्यैः (*havyaiḥ*)—with oblations
- प्रति विधेम (*prati vidhema*)—we serve

### Printed p. 447

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the atmosphere where the immortal gods made a path for this sun, in that same atmosphere the sun travels like a swiftly moving hawk. O Mitra and Varuṇa, as soon as the sun has risen (at the time of the morning libation), we serve you with salutations and with oblations.

##### English translation
He travels the path which the immortals have prepared for his course darting along like a hawk: we worship you, Mitra and Varuna, when the sun has risen, with praises and oblations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—For the word पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska gives the explanation पाथोऽन्तरिक्षं पथा व्याख्यातं । श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*pātho 'ntarikṣaṃ pathā vyākhyātaṃ | śyeno na dīyannanveti pāthaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*) (Ni. 6-7). That is, although the word पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) means a path, here he has explained it as the atmosphere, the path on which the sun travels. And of the word पंथाः (*paṃthāḥ*) he says: पंथाः पतेर्वा पद्यतेर्वा पंथतेर्वा (*paṃthāḥ patervā padyatervā paṃthatervā*) (Ni. 2-25). That is, he indicates that the word पंथाः (*paṃthāḥ*) may be formed from the root पत् (*pat*) meaning "fall down," or from the root पद् (*pad*) meaning "go," or from the root पंथ् (*paṃth*) meaning "move." These three roots all convey the sense of motion.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू मि॒त्रो वरु॑णो अर्य॒मा न॒स्त्मने॑ तो॒काय॒ वरि॑वो  
> दधंतु ।  
> सु॒गा नो॒ विश्वा॑ सु॒पथा॑नि संतु यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । मित्रः । वरुणः । अर्यमा । नः । त्मने । तोकाय । वरिवः । दधंतु ।  
> सुगा । नः । विश्वा । सुपथानि । संतु । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मित्रो वरुणोऽर्यमा चैते त्रयो देवा  नोऽस्माकं त्मन आत्मन आत्महिताय तोकाय पुत्राय च वरिवो धनं दधंतु । प्रयच्छंतु । नोऽस्माकं विश्वा सर्वाणि गंतव्यानि सुगा सुगमनानि सुपथानि च संतु । भवंतु । शिष्टं गतं ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, these three gods, are to bestow wealth (वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)) on us, for ourselves (त्मने (*tmane*), that is, for our own good) and for our son. May all our paths to be travelled be easy to go and good roads. The rest is already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- नु (*nu*)—now
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- त्मने (*tmane*)—for ourselves
- तोकाय (*tokāya*)—for our sons
- वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)—wealth
- दधंतु (*dadhaṃtu*)—let them give
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us

- सुगा (*sugā*)—paths of travel
- सुपथानि (*supathāni*)—fit for excellent travel
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be
- (O gods) यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman now give wealth to us ourselves and to our sons. May they make all our paths fit for excellent travel. O gods, always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
May Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman grant affluence to us and to our posterity: may all paths be easy of access to us, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 64 (Maṇḍala 7)
The Kannada Anuvāda: The sūkta beginning दिवि क्षयंता (*divi kṣayaṃtā*) is the ninth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Mitra and Varuṇa; its metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says दिवि पंच (*divi paṃca*). In the third chandoma, when the Praüga śastra mantras are recited, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited addressed to the deities Mitra and Varuṇa, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: दिवि क्षयंता रजसः पृथिव्यामा विश्ववाराश्विना गतं नः (*divi kṣayaṃtā rajasaḥ pṛthivyāmā viśvavārāśvinā gataṃ naḥ*) (Ā. 8-11).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वि क्षयं॑ता॒ रज॑सः पृथि॒व्यां प्र वां॑ घृ॒तस्य॑ नि॒र्णिजो॑ ददीरन् ।  
> ह॒व्यं नो॑ मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा सुजा॑तो॒ राजा॑ सुक्ष॒त्रो वरु॑णो जुषंत ‖ १ ‖

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवि । क्षयंता । रजसः । पृथिव्यां । प्र । वां । घृतस्य । निःनिजः । ददीरन्  
> हव्यं । नः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । सुजातः । राजा । सुक्षत्रः । वरुणः । जुषंत

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवि द्युलोकेऽंतरिक्षे पृथिव्यां च वर्तमानस्य रजस उदकस्य क्षयंता । क्षयतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । स्वामिनौ भवथः । हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवाभ्यां प्रेरिता मेघा घृतस्य निर्णिज उदकस्य रूपाणि ददीरन् । ददते । प्रयच्छंति । अथवा वां युवाभ्यां घृतस्य निर्णिजो रूपाणि । घृतानीत्यर्थः । तानि ददीरन् । दीयंते । नोऽस्माकं संबंधि हव्यं मित्रः सुजातः सुष्ठु प्रादुर्भूतोऽर्यमा राजा सर्वस्य स्वामी सुक्षत्रः शोभनबलो वरुणश्चैते जुषंत । सेवंतां ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you are lords (क्षयंता (*kṣayaṃtā*); the root क्षयति (*kṣayati*) has the sense of lordship) of the water (रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)) that is in the sky, the atmosphere, and on the earth. The clouds impelled by you give the forms of water, the घृतस्य निर्णिजः (*ghṛtasya nirṇijaḥ*). Or else: the forms of ghee, that is, ghee itself, are given to you. May Mitra, well born (सुजातः (*sujātaḥ*), excellently manifested), Aryaman, the king, lord of all, and Varuṇa, of good strength (सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*)), accept our oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवि (*divi*)—in the atmosphere
- पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—and on the earth
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the water
- क्षयंता (*kṣayaṃtā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, the lords
- वां (*vāṃ*)—the clouds impelled by you
- घृतस्य निर्णिजः (*ghṛtasya nirṇijaḥ*)—streams of water, or rain
- ददीरन् (*dadīran*)—give (pour down)
- [or वां (*vāṃ*)—for you; घृतस्य निर्णिजः (*ghṛtasya nirṇijaḥ*)—oblations in the form of ghee; ददीरन् (*dadīran*)—are offered]
- नः (*naḥ*)—our, that is, offered by us
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—this oblation
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- सुजातः (*sujātaḥ*)—excellently born

### Printed p. 450
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- राजा (*rājā*)—the lord of all
- सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*)—the one of excellent favour
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa, these three
- जुषंत (*juṣaṃta*)—let them accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of all the waters in earth and atmosphere, the clouds, impelled by you, pour rain on the earth. (Or: ghee in the form of oblation is offered to you.) May Mitra, Aryaman of excellent people, and Varuṇa, lord of all and of excellent strength, these three, accept the oblation we now offer.

##### English translation
Ruling over the waters that are in heaven and earth, impelled by you (the clouds) assume the form of rain: may the auspiciously manifested Mitra, the royal Aryaman, the powerful Varuna accept our oblation.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ रा॑जाना मह ऋतस्य गोपा॒ सिंधु॑पती क्षत्रिया यातम॒र्वाक् ।  
> इळां॑ नो मित्रावरुणो॒त वृ॒ष्टिमव॑ दि॒व इ॑न्वतं जीरदानू ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । राजाना । महः । ऋतस्य । गोपा । सिंधुपती इति सिंधु-पती । क्षत्रिया । यातं ।  
> अर्वाक् ।  
> इळां । नः । मित्रावरुणा । उत । वृष्टिं । अव । दिवः । इन्वतं । जीरदानू इति जीरदानू ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजाना सर्वस्य स्वामिनौ हे महो महत ऋतस्योदकस्य यज्ञस्य वा
> गोपा गोपायितारौ ॥ सुबामंत्रिते परांगवत्स्वर इति परांगवद्भावात् षष्ठ्यामंत्रितसमुदायस्य निघातत्वं । हे सिंधुपती नद्याः पालयितारौ हे क्षत्रिया बलवंतौ युवामर्वागस्मदभिमुखमा यातं । आगच्छतं । किं च हे मित्रावरुणा
> मित्रावरुणौ हे जीरदानू क्षिप्रदानौ युवां नोऽस्मभ्यमिळामन्नमुतापि च
> पुष्टिं च तत्साधिकां वृष्टिं च दिवोऽंतरिक्षादवावस्तादिन्वतं । प्रेरयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O kings, lords of all, O guardians (गोपा (*gopā*)) of the great (महः (*mahaḥ*)) water or sacrifice (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)): the vocative group takes the lowered accent in the genitive because of the rule सुबामंत्रिते परांगवत्स्वर (*subāmaṃtrite parāṃgavatsvara*). O lords of the river (सिंधुपती (*siṃdhupatī*)), protectors of the stream, O mighty ones (क्षत्रिया (*kṣatriyā*)), come hither, toward us. Further, O Mitra and Varuṇa, swift givers (जीरदानू (*jīradānū*)), send down to us from the sky, the atmosphere, food (इळां (*iḷāṃ*)), nourishment, and the rain that produces it.

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water or of the sacrifice
- गोपा (*gopā*)—you who are protectors
- सिंधुपती (*siṃdhupatī*)—guardians of the rivers

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- जीरदानू (*jīradānū*)—you who quickly give what is desired

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of all, exalted, protectors of water or of the sacrifice, guardians of the rivers, and powerful: come facing us. O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who quickly fulfil our wishes, impel food for us, and nourishing rain, to fall downward from the firmament.

##### English translation
Sovereigns, mighty preservers of water, powerful lords of rivers, come to our presence : send down to us, munificent Mitra and Varuna, from the firmament, sustenance and rain.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitra, Varuṇa and the divine Aryaman, these three, are asked to lead us at the time of our need, whenever we require it, by the most effective paths, that is, to bring us to our goal.

### Printed p. 452

> यंतु । किंच नोऽस्मान् सुदासे शोभनदानाय जनायारिरर्यमा यथा ब्रवत्
> असावनुकंप्य इति ब्रूयात् तथा कुर्वंतु । आर्यम्णः पुनरभिधानमादरार्थं ।
> देवगोपा देवा यूयं गोपायितारो येषामस्माकं ते वयमिषा
> युष्माभिर्दातव्येनान्नेन सह पुत्रादिसहिता मदेम । हृष्येम ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, may they act so that Aryaman speaks of us to the generous giver (सुदासे (*sudāse*)), saying "this one deserves compassion"; Aryaman is named again for the sake of respect. O gods, you who are our protectors, may we, with the food to be given by you, together with sons and the rest, rejoice (मदेम (*madema*), "be glad").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman, these three
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- यत् (*yat*)—when we desire
- साधिष्ठेभिः (*sādhiṣṭhebhiḥ*)—that are effective means
- पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—by paths
- नयंतु (*nayaṃtu*)—let them lead to the appointed place; and
- नः (*naḥ*)—us, that is, our concern
- सुदासे (*sudāse*)—to good people, excellent givers
- अरिः (*ariḥ*)—Aryaman
- यथा ब्रवत् (*yathā bravat*)—let him declare
- देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*)—we who are protected by you, the gods
- इषा (*iṣā*)—with the food you give us
- सह (*saha*)—together with sons and the rest
- मदेम (*madema*)—may we be happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these three gods, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, together lead us by suitable paths to the appointed place when we desire it. May Aryaman inform good people that we are worthy of excellent favour. Protected by you, the gods, may we be happy with sons and the rest, through the food and other provisions you give.

##### English translation
May Mitra, Varuna, the divine Aryaman, conduct us by the most practicable paths, then, (when we desire their guidance), accordingly as Aryaman promises to the liberal donor (of oblations), may we, enjoying the protection of the gods, rejoice in abundance, together with posterity.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒क्षेथां॑ मित्रावरुणा घृ॒तेन॒ ता रा॑जाना सुक्षि॒तीस्त॑र्पयेथां ॥ ४ ॥

> च ।  
> उक्षेथां । मित्रावरुणा । घृतेन । ता । राजाना । सु-क्षितीः । तर्पयेथां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ यो वां युवयोरेतं गर्तं रथं मनसा तक्षत् स्तोमेन संकल्पयेत् तथा कृत्वोर्ध्वामुन्नतां धीतिं कर्म स्तुतिरूपं कृणवत्
> कुर्यात् उच्चैः स्तुयात् एवं कृत्वा धारयच्च यागे धारयेत् हे राजाना
> स्वामिनौ मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ ता तौ युवां जनं घृतेनोदकेनोक्षेथां
> सिंचतं । तस्मै सुक्षितीः शोभननिवासाः प्रजाः तर्पयेथां । यथा सुक्षितयो
> भवंति तथा तर्पयेथामिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, whoever fashions this chariot (गर्तं (*gartaṃ*)) of yours in his mind, that is, conceives it through praise, and so makes a lofty (ऊर्ध्वां (*ūrdhvāṃ*)) धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*), a rite in the form of praise, praising aloud, and upholds it in the sacrifice: O sovereign lords Mitra and Varuṇa, you two sprinkle that man with घृतेन (*ghṛtena*), that is, water. For him satisfy the subjects who have good dwellings (सुक्षितीः (*sukṣitīḥ*)); satisfy them so that they have good dwellings.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever man
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- एतं गर्तं (*etaṃ gartaṃ*)—this chariot
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the mind, that is, with praise
- तक्षत् (*takṣat*)—praises and extols; and
- ऊर्ध्वां (*ūrdhvāṃ*)—exalted, that is, excellent
- धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)—the rite in the form of praise
- कृणवत् (*kṛṇavat*)—makes with a loud voice (praises)
- धारयत् च (*dhārayat ca*)—and offers in the sacrifice; that man
- राजाना (*rājānā*)—you who are lords of all
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- ता (*tā*)—you
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with water in the form of rain
- उक्षेथां (*ukṣethāṃ*)—sprinkle (him)
- सुक्षितीः (*sukṣitīḥ*)—giving excellent dwelling-places
- तर्पयेथां (*tarpayethāṃ*)—bring satisfaction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, whichever man praises and extols your chariot in his own mind, and in the sacrifice recites that praise aloud and offers it: him, O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of all, sprinkle with rain-water, that is, pour rain for him, and give him excellent dwelling-places and make him happy.

##### English translation
Mitra and Varuna, bedew with water him who fabricates your chariot in his mind, offering high praise, and confirming it (by sacrifice) : render, sovereign (deities), the people well affected towards him.
