#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्तोमो॑ वरुण मित्र॒ तुभ्यं॒ सोमः॑ शु॒क्रो न वा॒यवे॑यामि ।  
> अ॒वि॒ष्टं धियो॑ जिगृ॒तं पुरं॑धीर्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्तोमः । वरुण । मित्र । तुभ्यं । सोमः । शुक्रः । न । वायवे । अयामि ।  
> अविष्टं । धियः । जिगृतं । पुरं-धीः । यूयं । पात । स्वस्ति-भिः । सदा । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया स्तुतिमुपसंहरति । हे वरुण हे मित्र तुभ्यं युवयोर्वायवे
> वायुर्गंतादित्यः । स एवार्यमा । कस्मै चैष स्तोम आयामि । अकारि ।
> किमिव । शुक्रो दीप्तः सोमो न युष्मभ्यं प्रीतिकरः सोमो यथा दीयते
> तद्वत् । धियः कर्माण्यस्मदीयान्यविष्टं । रक्षतं । पुरंधीः स्तुतीर्जिगृतं । प्रबुद्धृतं । अन्यदृतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse he concludes the praise. O Varuṇa, O Mitra, this स्तोम (*stoma*) has been made (आयामि (*āyāmi*), "has been done") for you, and for वायवे (*vāyave*): वायुर्गंतादित्यः (*vāyurgaṃtādityaḥ*), the going Āditya, who is Aryaman himself. It is like bright (शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)) Soma, as Soma is offered to you, pleasing. Protect (अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)) our rites (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)). Wake up (जिगृतं (*jigṛtaṃ*)) to our praises (पुरंधीः (*puraṃdhīḥ*)), that is, attend to them. The rest is clear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you, that is, addressed to you
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—and addressed to Aryaman, who moves about
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—pure
- सोमः न (*somaḥ na*)—like Soma-juice, pleasing to you
- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise
- अयामि (*ayāmi*)—has been made
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the sacrifices and other rites we are performing
- अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)—protect (so that they are free of obstacles)
- पुरंधीः (*puraṃdhīḥ*)—our praises
- जिगृतं (*jigṛtaṃ*)—(hear and) understand; O Mitra, Varuṇa and the other gods
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, O Aryaman, this praise, pure like Soma-juice and pleasing to you, has been made for you. Make the sacrifices and other rites we are now performing free of obstacles, and protect them. Hear and understand our praise. O gods, protect us always with blessings.

### Printed p. 455

##### English translation
Varuna and Mitra, this praise, pure as the Soma libation, has been offered to you, and also Aryaman, (to you) : protect our rites : be awake to our praises : and do you ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 65 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रति वां सूर इति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं मैत्रावरुणं ।
> प्रति वामित्यनुक्रांतं । द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रेऽप्येषस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> प्रति वां सूर उदिते सूक्तैर्धेनुः प्रश्नस्य । आ. ८-१० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ten-verse… rather, the five-verse sūkta प्रति वां सूर (*prati vāṃ sūra*) is the tenth sūkta; its seer is Vasiṣṭha and its deity Mitra and Varuṇa. The Anukramaṇī says प्रति वां (*prati vāṃ*). In the second Chandoma, in the Praüga-śastra, the first three verses are used as well. It is prescribed in the sūtra: प्रति वां सूर उदिते सूक्तैर्धेनुः प्रश्नस्य । आ. ८-१० । इति (*prati vāṃ sūra udite sūktairdhenuḥ praśnasya | ā. 8-10 | iti*).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning प्रति वां सूरे (*prati vāṃ sūre*) is the tenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Mitra and Varuṇa. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as प्रति वां (*prati vāṃ*). It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 8-10), प्रति वां सूर उदिते सूक्तैर्धेनुः प्रश्नस्य (*prati vāṃ sūra udite sūktairdhenuḥ praśnasya*), that the first three Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning प्रति वां (*prati vāṃ*), are used for the Praüga-śastra mantras in the second Chandoma.

Sūkta 65. Maṇḍala 7. Anuvāka 4. Sūkta 65. Aṣṭaka 5. Adhyāya 5. Varga 7. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: Mitra and Varuṇa. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रति॑ वां॒ सूर॒ उदि॑ते सू॒क्तैर्मि॒त्रं हु॑वे॒ वरु॑णं पू॒तद॑क्षं ।  
> ययो॑रसु॒र्य१॒॑मक्षि॑तं॒ ज्येष्ठं॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ याम॑न्ना॒चिता॑ जिग॒त्नु

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । वां । सूरे । उत्-इते । सु-उक्तैः । मित्रं । हुवे । वरुणं । पूत-दक्षं ।  
> ययोः । असुर्यं । अक्षितं । ज्येष्ठं । विश्वस्य । यामन् । आ-चिता । जिगत्नु ।

### Printed p. 456

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूरे सूर्ये उदिते प्रातःसवने मित्रं पूतदक्षं शुद्धबलं वरुणं वां
> सूक्तैर्हुवे । आह्वये । ययोर्मित्रावरुणयोरक्षितमक्षीणमत एव ज्येष्ठमसुर्यं बलमाचिता चिते उपचिते शूरसंघैरुपेते यामन् यामनि संग्रामे
> विश्वस्य शत्रुसंघस्य जिगत्नु जेतृ भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At sunrise, at the morning libation, I invoke with praises (सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)) Mitra, and Varuṇa of pure strength (पूतदक्षं (*pūtadakṣaṃ*)), you two. The strength (असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)) of these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, is imperishable (अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)) and therefore supreme; in battle (यामन् (*yāman*)), crowded (आचिता (*ācitā*)) with throngs of heroes, it is the conqueror (जिगत्नु (*jigatnu*)) of the whole host of enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरे (*sūre*)—when the sun
- उदिते (*udite*)—has risen, at the morning libation
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—Mitra
- पूतदक्षं (*pūtadakṣaṃ*)—of pure strength
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you both
- सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)—with words of praise
- हुवे (*huve*)—I pray and call
- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—of whichever Mitra and Varuṇa
- अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)—the imperishable
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—and supreme
- असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)—strength
- आचिता (*ācitā*)—gathered together, enemy heroes assembled for battle
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in battle
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—the whole host of enemies
- जिगत्नु (*jigatnu*)—is conquering

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra and Varuṇa, whose imperishable and supreme strength is able to conquer the host of enemies gathered together in battle: you two, Mitra and Varuṇa of pure strength, I pray and call with words of praise at the morning libation, as soon as the sun has risen.

##### English translation
When the sun has risen, I invoke Mitra and you, Varuna, of pure vigour, whose imperishable and superior might is triumphant in the crowded conflict over all enemies.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता हि दे॒वाना॒मसु॑रा॒ ताव॒र्या ता नः॑ क्षि॒तीः क॑रतमू॒र्जयं॑तीः ।  
> अ॒श्याम॑ मित्रावरुणा व॒यं वां॒ द्यावा॑ च॒ यत्र॑ पी॒पय॒न्नहा॑ च ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । हि । देवानां । असुरा । ता । अर्या । ता । नः । क्षितीः । करतं । ऊर्जयंतीः ।  
> अश्याम । मित्रावरुणा । वयं । वां । द्यावा । च । यत्र । पीपयन् । अहा । च ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 457

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता हि तौ खलु देवौ देवानां मध्येऽसुरा बलवंतौ । अर्या अर्यौ
> सर्वस्येश्वरौ । ता तौ नोऽस्माकं क्षितीः पुत्रादिरूपाः प्रजा ऊर्जयंतीः प्रवृद्धाः
> करतं । कुरुतं । हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ वयं वां युवामश्याम । व्याप्नुयाम । यत्र यस्यां युवयोर्व्याप्तौ द्यावा द्यावापृथिव्यौ । सर्वदा
> तयोः सहभावादयमर्थो लभ्यते । अहा च । एतद्रात्रेरुपलक्षणं । अहोरात्राणि च पीपयन् अस्मान् प्याययेयुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those two gods, among the gods, are असुरा (*asurā*), that is, mighty; they are अर्या (*aryā*), lords of all. May they make our offspring, sons and the rest, grow strong. O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we reach you, in whose pervasion the heaven and earth stand; since the two are always together this sense is obtained. अहा च (*ahā ca*) ("and the days") also implies the night: may days and nights nourish us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता हि (*tā hi*)—those Mitra and Varuṇa
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—among the gods
- असुरा (*asurā*)—they are powerful
- अर्या ता (*aryā tā*)—who are lords of all
- ता (*tā*)—those Mitra and Varuṇa
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- क्षितीः (*kṣitīḥ*)—offspring, sons and the rest
- ऊर्जयंतीः (*ūrjayaṃtīḥ*)—so that they grow strong
- करतं (*karataṃ*)—may they make
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- वां (*vāṃ*)—both of you
- अश्याम (*aśyāma*)—may we attain
- यत्र द्यावा (*yatra dyāvā*)—(which) heaven and earth that you pervade
- अहा च (*ahā ca*)—day and night also
- पीपयन् (*pīpayan*)—may they satisfy us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those gods Mitra and Varuṇa are endowed with power and strength even among all the gods. May those two, lords of all, make our offspring, sons and the rest, prosper. O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we be near you both. May this heaven and earth that you pervade, and day and night as well, bring us satisfaction.

##### English translation
They verily are mighty among the gods : they are rulers : they bestow upon us a numerous posterity : may we obtain you, Mitra and Varuna, whether on earth or in heaven, and wherever the (passing) days may preserve us.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता भूरि॑पाशा॒वनृ॑तस्य॒ सेतू॑ दुर॒त्येतू॑ रि॒पवे॒ मर्त्या॑य ।  
> ऋ॒तस्य॑ मित्रावरुणा प॒था वा॑म॒पो न ना॒वा दु॑रि॒ता त॑रेम ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 458

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । भूरिपाशौ । अनृतस्य । सेतू इति । दुरत्येतू इति दुःअत्येतू । रिपवे । मर्त्याय ।  
> ऋतस्य । मित्रावरुणा । पथा । वां । अपः । न । नावा । दुःइता । तरेम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तौ मित्रावरुणौ भूरिपाशौ प्रभूतबंधनसाधनपाशोपेतौ अनृतस्य यागरहितस्य सेतू सेतुवद्बंधकौ रिपवे मर्त्याय वैरिजनाय दुरत्येतू दुरतिक्रमौ भवतः । हे मित्रावरुणा तादृशौ मित्रावरुणौ वां युवयोर्यज्ञस्य युवयोरर्थायानुष्ठीयमानस्य यागस्य पथा मार्गेण दुरिता दुःखानि तरेम नावापो न प्रभूतान्युदकानीव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Mitra and Varuṇa have many fetters, instruments of binding; they are bridges, binders, for the man without sacrifice, and are hard to overcome for the hostile mortal, the enemy. O Mitra and Varuṇa, such as you are, by the path of your sacrifice, the rite performed for you, may we cross over sorrows as one crosses abundant waters by a boat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तौ (*tau*)—those Mitra and Varuṇa
- भूरिपाशौ (*bhūripāśau*)—having fetters as instruments of binding
- अनृतस्य (*anṛtasya*)—for those who do not perform sacrifices
- सेतू (*setū*)—who bind like a bridge
- रिपवे (*ripave*)—the enemy
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—by the man
- दुरत्येतू (*duratyetū*)—who cannot be brought to an end
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, possessed of such qualities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice we perform desiring wealth
- पथा (*pathā*)—by the path
- नावा (*nāvā*)—by a boat
- अपो न (*apo na*)—as one crosses (deep) water
- दुरिता (*duritā*)—sorrows
- तरेम (*tarema*)—may we cross

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The fetters of those Mitra and Varuṇa are able to bind, like a bridge, those who do not perform sacrifices and the like. No enemy can withstand you. O Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with such qualities, by this guidance of yours in the sacrifice we perform desiring wealth, may we cross sorrows as one crosses deep water by a boat.

##### English translation
Holders are you of many fetters, barriers against the irreligious, invincible by hostile mortals: may we cross over all the danger, Mitra and Varuna, by the path of sacrifice, to you, as (we cross over) water by a boat.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मैत्रावरुणे पशावा नो मित्रावरुणेत्येषा चतुर्थ्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> आ नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे । आ. ३-८ । इति ।
> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ नोऽस्माकं हव्यजुष्टिं हविःसेवनवंतं यज्ञमा गच्छतमिति शेषः । आगत्य इळाभिरन्नैः सह घृतैरुदकैर्गव्यूतिमस्मदीयां भूमिमुक्षतं सिंचतं । वां युवां प्रत्यत्रास्मिल्लोके वरमुत्कृष्टं हविः स्तोत्रं वा क आ यच्छेदिति शेषः । अतः केवलं कृपयैव दिव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य चारोश्चरणीयस्योद्न उदकस्य । कर्मणि षष्ठी । उक्तलक्षणमुदकं प्रणीतं प्रयच्छतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Maitrāvaruṇa animal offering, the verse आ नो मित्रावरुणा (*ā no mitrāvaruṇā*) is the fourth anuvākyā. It is so stated in the sūtra: आ नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे (*ā no mitrāvaruṇā havyajuṣṭiṃ yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe*) (Ā. 3-8). O Mitra and Varuṇa, come to our sacrifice, the partaking of the oblation (the verb "come" is supplied). Having come, sprinkle our land with waters together with food. Who in this world could offer you an excellent oblation or hymn? Therefore, out of mere kindness, grant the celestial, desirable water; the genitive is in the sense of the object.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हव्यजुष्टिं (*havyajuṣṭiṃ*)—to the sacrifice of partaking of the oblation
- आ (गच्छतं) (*ā (gacchataṃ)*)—be pleased to come (then)
- इळाभिः (*iḷābhiḥ*)—with foods
- घृतैः (*ghṛtaiḥ*)—with waters
- गव्यूतिं (*gavyūtiṃ*)—this region where we dwell
- उक्षतं (*ukṣataṃ*)—sprinkle
- वां प्रति (*vāṃ prati*)—towards you
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this world
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—excellent oblation or hymn
- आ (*ā*)—who indeed could offer? (therefore)
- दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—that is in the sky in the form of cloud
- चारोः (*cāroḥ*)—excellent
- उद्नः (*udnaḥ*)—the rain water
- जनाय (*janāya*)—for the people
- प्रणीतं (*praṇītaṃ*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, come to this sacrifice in which the oblation is offered to you. Then, with food and rain waters, sprinkle and satisfy this region where we dwell. Which man is capable of offering you an excellent oblation or hymn? (Therefore, with a gracious mind) provide the excellent water in the sky to the people in the form of rain.

##### English translation
Come, Mitra and Varuna, to our offered oblation: sprinkle our place of sacrifice with water and viands: (who) in this world (may) present to you

### Printed p. 460
such) excellant (donations) that you may (thereby be induced to) gratify mankind with celestial and beautiful water.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal offering made to Mitra and Varuṇa, the verse आ नो मित्रावरुणा (*ā no mitrāvaruṇā*) is to be recited as the fourth anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे (*ā no mitrāvaruṇā havyajuṣṭiṃ yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe*) (Ā. 3-8).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्तोमो॑ वरुण मित्र॒ तुभ्यं॒ सोमः॑ शु॒क्रो न वा॒यु-वे॑यामि ।  
> अ॒वि॒ष्टं धियो॑ जिगृ॒तं पुरं॑धीर्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्तोमः । वरुण । मित्र । तुभ्यं । सोमः । शुक्रः । न । वायवे । अयामि ।  
> अविष्टं । धियः । जिगृतं । पुरंधीः । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया स्तुतिमुपसंहरति । हे वरुण हे मित्र तुभ्यं युवयोर्वायवे । वायुर्गंतादित्यः । स एवार्यमा । तस्मै चैष स्तोमोऽयामि । अकारि । किमिव । शुक्रो दीप्तः सोमो न युष्मभ्यं प्रीतिकरः सोमो यथा दीयते तद्वत् । धियः कर्माण्यस्मदीयान्यविष्टं । रक्षतं । पुरंधीः स्तुतीर्जिगृतं । प्रबुद्ध्येशं । अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse he concludes the praise. O Varuṇa, O Mitra, this hymn has been made for you; वायवे (*vāyave*): Vāyu is the "goer", the Āditya, who is Aryaman, and for him too. How? As the bright, shining Soma is given, pleasing to you, so is this praise. Protect our rites; awaken to our praises. The rest is already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you, that is, addressed to you
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—addressed also to Aryaman, the ever-moving
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—pure
- सोमः न (*somaḥ na*)—like Soma juice, pleasing to you
- एषः स्तोमः (*eṣaḥ stomaḥ*)—this praise
- अयामि (*ayāmi*)—has been fashioned
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the sacrifices and the like that we perform
- अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)—protect (so that there are no obstacles)
- पुरंधीः (*puraṃdhīḥ*)—our praises
- जिगृतं (*jigṛtaṃ*)—hear and understand; O gods Mitra, Varuṇa and the rest
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

### Printed p. 461

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, O Aryaman, this praise, pleasing to you like pure Soma juice, has been fashioned for you. Protect the sacrifices and rites we are now performing, making them free of obstacles; and hear and understand our praise. O gods, always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
Varuna and Mitra, this praise, pure as the Soma libation, has been offered to you, and also Aryaman, (to you): protect our rites: be awake to our praises: and do you ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 66 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र मित्रयोरित्येकोनविंशत्यृचमेकादशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं । आत्रेय-मनुक्रमणिका । प्र मित्रयोरेकोना गायत्रं दशम्याद्यास्त्रयः प्रगाथाः पुरउष्णिक् चतुर्थ्याद्या दशादित्यास्तिस्रः सौर्य इति । दशमी बृहती एकादशी सतोबृहती द्वादशी बृहती त्रयोदशी सतोबृहती चतुर्दशी बृहती पंचदशी सतोबृहती षोडशी पुरउष्णिक् शिष्टा गायत्र्यः । चतुर्थ्याद्यास्त्रयोदशांता आदित्यदेवताश्चतुर्दश्यास्तिस्रः सूर्यदेवत्याः । आद्यौ तृचौ पूर्ववन्मैत्रावरुणौ ॥ अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रे आनिष्टो नवर्चः शस्याः । प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति नव । आ. ५-१० । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवषडहयोः स्तोमवृद्धिनिमित्तमाद्या षडृचः । सूत्रितं च । प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति षट् । आ. ७-५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र मित्रयोः (*pra mitrayoḥ*), of nineteen verses, is the eleventh sūkta; its seer is Vasiṣṭha. The Ātreya Anukramaṇikā says: प्र मित्रयोरेकोना गायत्रं दशम्याद्यास्त्रयः प्रगाथाः पुरउष्णिक् चतुर्थ्याद्या दशादित्यास्तिस्रः सौर्यः (*pra mitrayorekonā gāyatraṃ daśamyādyāstrayaḥ pragāthāḥ purauṣṇik caturthyādyā daśādityāstisraḥ sauryaḥ*). Verse 10 is Bṛhatī, 11 Satobṛhatī, 12 Bṛhatī, 13 Satobṛhatī, 14 Bṛhatī, 15 Satobṛhatī, 16 Puraūṣṇih; the rest are Gāyatrī. Verses 4 to 13 have the Ādityas as deity, the three from 14 Sūrya; the first and last triads are, as before, Maitrāvaruṇa. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, nine verses are to be recited, since the sūtra says प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति नव (*pra mitrayorvaruṇayoriti nava*) (Ā. 5-10). In the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas the first six verses are used to increase the stoma; the sūtra says प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति षट् (*pra mitrayorvaruṇayoriti ṣaṭ*) (Ā. 7-5).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta प्र मित्रयोः (*pra mitrayoḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has nineteen ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is its seer; the Anukramaṇikā says प्र मित्रयोरेकोना गायत्रं दशम्याद्यास्त्रयः प्रगाथाः पुरउष्णिक् चतुर्थ्याद्या दशादित्यास्तिस्रः सौर्यः (*pra mitrayorekonā gāyatraṃ daśamyādyāstrayaḥ pragāthāḥ purauṣṇik caturthyādyā daśādityāstisraḥ sauryaḥ*). The tenth ṛk of this sūkta is in the Bṛhatī metre, the eleventh Satobṛhatī, the twelfth Bṛhatī, the thirteenth Satobṛhatī, the fourteenth Bṛhatī, the fifteenth Satobṛhatī, the sixteenth Puraūṣṇih; the remaining ṛks are Gāyatrī. For the ṛks from the fourth to the thirteenth (4-13) the Ādityas are the deity; for the three following from the fourteenth (14-16)

### Printed p. 462
Sūrya is the deity; for the first and last ṛks of this sūkta Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities, as before. The first nine ṛks of this sūkta are used for the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa at the midday pressing of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति नव (*pra mitrayorvaruṇayoriti nava*) (Ā. 5-10). In the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha sacrifices, the first six ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited for the mantras recited as āvāpa to increase the stoma, as explained by the sūtra प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोरिति षट् (*pra mitrayorvaruṇayoriti ṣaṭ*) (Ā. 7-5).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र मि॒त्रयो॒र्वरु॑णयोः॒ स्तोमो॑ न एतु शू॒ष्यः॑ ।  
> नम॑स्वान्तुविजा॒तयोः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । मित्रयोः । वरुणयोः । स्तोमः । नः । एतु । शूष्यः ।  
> नमस्वान् । तुविजातयोः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मित्रयोर्वरुणयोः । मित्रावरुणयोरित्यर्थः । उभयत्र प्रतियोगापेक्षया द्विवचनत्वं । तुविजातयोर्बहुषु प्रादुर्भावयोर्देवयोर्योऽस्मदीयः शूष्यः सुखकरो नमस्वानन्नवान् हविर्भिर्युक्तः स्तोमः स्तोत्रं प्रैतु । गच्छतु । अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणाविति श्रुतिः । अनयोरहोरात्रापेक्षया पुनःपुनरागमनादनयोस्तुविजातत्वं । अथवा बहूनामुपकारायानयोः प्रादुर्भावात्तुविजातत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मित्रयोर्वरुणयोः (*mitrayorvaruṇayoḥ*) means of Mitra and Varuṇa; the dual is used in both words with regard to their mutual relation. Of the two gods तुविजातयोः (*tuvijātayoḥ*), who have manifestations in many places, may our praise, which is शूष्यः (*śūṣyaḥ*) (pleasant), नमस्वान् (*namasvān*) (endowed with food and oblations), go forth. The śruti says *ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇau*. Since they come again and again in relation to day and night, they are तुविजात (*tuvijāta*); or else, because they appeared for the benefit of many.

### Printed p. 463

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुविजातयोः (*tuvijātayoḥ*)—having many births
- मित्रयोः वरुणयोः (*mitrayoḥ varuṇayoḥ*)—offered to Mitra and Varuṇa
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- शूष्यः (*śūṣyaḥ*)—that which brings happiness
- नमस्वान् (*namasvān*)—that which is accompanied by oblation
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—this hymn of praise
- प्र एतु (*pra etu*)—may it go to them and reach them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this hymn of praise of ours, which brings happiness and is accompanied by oblation, and which we offer to Mitra and Varuṇa, who have many births, go to them and reach them.

##### English translation
May this our propitiatory praise, accompanied by oblations, proceed to you, Mitra and Varuna, of reiterated manifestations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तुविजातयोः (*tuvijātayoḥ*)—tuvi means many, jāta means birth. What is meant by many births? In Śruti passages such as अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणौ (*ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇau*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-10-1) and मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ*), Mitra is said to be the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. Since day and night come round every day, one after the other in a changing order, the seer has hinted in another way at his meaning, that Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of these, have many births.
मित्रयोः वरुणयोः (*mitrayoḥ varuṇayoḥ*)—मित्रावरुणयोरित्यर्थः । उभयत्र प्रतियोगापेक्षया द्विवचनत्वं (*mitrāvaruṇayorityarthaḥ | ubhayatra pratiyogāpekṣayā dvivacanatvaṃ*). Here there are two separate words, Mitra and Varuṇa, and both deities are indicated; because of this, and for the convenience of the metre, the dual has been used for each word. The same kind of usage is seen in the Ṛk
उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धं (*udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdhaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1).
Here too the separate dual words मित्रयोः वरुणयोः (*mitrayoḥ varuṇayoḥ*) are used in place of the word मित्रावरुणयोः (*mitrāvaruṇayoḥ*). Besides, in many contexts it is the custom to use the dual of one word alone, Mitra or Varuṇa, to indicate both.
In the Ṛk आ यद्वामीयचक्षसा मित्र वयं च सूरयः (*ā yadvāmīyacakṣasā mitra vayaṃ ca sūrayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-6) the dual word मित्रा (*mitrā*) (in the Saṃhitā text it is short, मित्र (*mitra*)) is used to indicate both Mitra and Varuṇa.

### Printed p. 464
In the Ṛk अधारयतं पृथिवीमुत द्यां मित्रराजाना वरुणा नमोभिः (*adhārayataṃ pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ mitrarājānā varuṇā namobhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-62-3) the dual word वरुणा (*varuṇā*) is used to indicate both Mitra and Varuṇa. There are many more examples like this.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या धा॒रयं॑त दे॒वाः सु॒दक्षा॒ दक्ष॑पितरा ।  
> अ॒सु॒र्या॑य॒ प्रम॑हसा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । धारयंत । देवाः । सुदक्षा । दक्षपितरा ।  
> असुर्याय । प्रमहसा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या यौ युवां धारयंत । के । देवा आदिकर्तारोऽसुर्याय बलकराय । कीदृशौ युवां । सुदक्षा शोभनबलौ दक्षपितरा बलस्य पालकौ स्वामिनौ वा । बलप्रदावित्यर्थः । प्रमहसा प्रकृष्टतेजस्कौ । तौ साधयतमित्युत्तरत्रान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"या (*yā*)": you two whom the gods, the first makers, uphold for strength-giving vigour (*asuryāya balakarāya*). What kind are you? सुदक्षा (*sudakṣā*): of excellent strength; दक्षपितरा (*dakṣapitarā*): protectors, or lords, of strength, that is, givers of strength; प्रमहसा (*pramahasā*): of surpassing splendour. The connection is with the next verse: "Accomplish those (rites)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Mitra and Varuṇa)
- सुदक्षा (*sudakṣā*)—you of excellent strength
- दक्षपितरा (*dakṣapitarā*)—lords of power and capacity, that is, givers of strength to men
- प्रमहसा (*pramahasā*)—you who are exceedingly radiant
- या (*yā*)—whom you
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- असुर्याय (*asuryāya*)—in order to produce strength in all
- धारयंत (*dhārayaṃta*)—established [such as you, make our sacrifices and other rites fruitful]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who have excellent strength, are lords of power and capacity, and are exceedingly radiant: the earlier gods established you to produce strength in all. Such as you, make our sacrifices and other rites fruitful.

##### English translation
You whom the gods uphold for their invigoration, both mighty, masters of strength and of diffusive radiance.

### Printed p. 465

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

What is said in this Ṛk must be construed together with the meaning of the next Ṛk. In this Ṛk there is only a description of the qualities of Mitra and Varuṇa; the main verb is in the next Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता नः॑ स्ति॒पा त॑नू॒पा वरु॑ण जरितॄ॒णां ।  
> मित्र॑ सा॒धय॑तं॒ धियः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । नः । स्तिपा । तनूपा । वरुण । जरितॄणां ।  
> मित्र । साधयतं । धियः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता तौ स्तिपा । स्त्यायंत इति स्त्रियो गृहाः । तान्पात इति स्तिपौ । तनूपा तन्वः पातारौ हे वरुण हे मित्र उक्तलक्षणौ युवां जरितॄणां नोऽस्माकं धियः कर्माणि स्तुतिरूपाणि साधयतं । सफलवंति कुरुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"ता (*tā*)": those two. स्तिपा (*stipā*): स्त्यायंत इति स्त्रियो गृहाः । तान्पात इति स्तिपौ (*styāyaṃta iti striyo gṛhāḥ | tānpāta iti stipau*), that is, protectors of houses. तनूपा (*tanūpā*): protectors of bodies. O Varuṇa, O Mitra, you two of the stated character: make the acts of us, the praisers, our praise-acts, successful (साधयतं (*sādhayataṃ*) = make them fruitful).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता (*tā*)—such, that is, those endowed with the qualities spoken of in the previous Ṛk
- स्तिपा (*stipā*)—protectors of houses
- तनूपा (*tanūpā*)—you who protect our bodies and the like (from harm)
- वरुण मित्र (*varuṇa mitra*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, you
- जरितॄणां (*jaritṝṇāṃ*)—who praise you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—sacrificial rites or hymns
- साधयतं (*sādhayataṃ*)—make fruitful

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra, O Varuṇa, endowed with the qualities spoken of before, protectors of houses and of bodies and the like: make this sacrificial rite of ours, which takes the form of praise of you, fruitful.

##### English translation
Protectors of our dwellings, protectors of our persons, Mitra and Varuna, perfect the rites of your adorers.

### Printed p. 466

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्तिपा (*stipā*)—स्त्यायंत इति स्त्रियो गृहाः । तान् पात इति स्तिपौ (*styāyaṃta iti striyo gṛhāḥ | tān pāta iti stipau*). Because they are spread out so as to be suitable to dwell in, स्त्रियः (*striyaḥ*) means houses. Because they protect these, Mitra and Varuṇa are described by the epithet स्तिपा (*stipā*).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद॒द्य सूर॒ उदि॒तेऽना॑गा मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> सु॒वाति॑ सवि॒ता भगः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अद्य । सूरे । उत्इते । अनागाः । मित्रः । अर्यमा ।  
> सुवाति । सविता । भगः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्धनमस्माकमपेक्षितं तदद्यास्मिन्काले सूर उदिते सति प्रातःसवनेऽनागाः पापहंता मित्रोऽर्यमा सविता भगश्चैते प्रत्येकं सुवाति । प्रेरयेत् । अथवा । अनागा मित्रोर्यमा दाता भवतु । तदीप्सितं धनं भगो भजनीयः सविता सुवाति । प्रेरयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wealth we desire: today, at this time, when the sun has risen, at the morning pressing, may Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Bhaga, each of them, the sinless (अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*) = destroyers of sin), impel (सुवाति (*suvāti*) = send) it. Or else: let Mitra and Aryaman, sinless, be givers; and Savitṛ, Bhaga, the one to be worshipped, impels (sends) that desired wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—whatever wealth we desire, that
- अद्य (*adya*)—now, that is, this day
- सूरे (*sūre*)—the sun
- उदिते (*udite*)—while rising, at the time of the morning pressing
- अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)—who remove sins
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the god called Bhaga too
- सुवाति (*suvāti*)—may he impel it to reach us, that is, may he give it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealth we desire, this day while the sun is rising, at the time of the morning pressing, may the gods Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Bhaga, who remove sins, impel to reach us; that is, may those gods give us the wealth we desire.

##### English translation
May Mitra, the distroyer of sin, Aryaman, Savitri, Bhaga, bestow (upon us), to-day at sunrice (what we pray for).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒प्रा॒वीर॑स्तु॒ स क्षयः॒ प्र नु याम॑न्सुदानवः ।  
> ये नो॒ अंहो॑ऽति॒पिप्र॑ति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुप्रअवीः । अस्तु । सः । क्षयः । प्र । नु । यामन् । सुदानवः ।  
> ये । नः । अंहः । अतिपिप्रति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सः क्षयः स निवासः सुप्रावीरस्तु । सुष्ठु प्रकर्षेण रक्षितास्तु । प्रशब्द आदरार्थः । प्रकर्षेण नु क्षिप्रं भवत्विति शेषः ।  । हे सुदानवः सुदानाः युष्माकं यामन् यामनि गमने सति  गमने । ये यूयमागत्य नोऽस्माकमंहः पापमतिपिप्रति अतिपारयथ  गमन इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"That dwelling": may that abode be well protected (सुप्रावीः (*suprāvīḥ*) = well and excellently guarded). The word प्र (*pra*) has the sense of regard; the supplied remainder is "may it be quickly, with excellence". O liberal ones (सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)), when you go (यामन् (*yāman*)), you who, having come, carry us across (अतिपिप्रति (*atipiprati*) = अतिपारयथ (*atipārayatha*)) our sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)).**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—you who (having come)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin
- अतिपिप्रति (*atipiprati*)—remove it and bring us across; such
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—O Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, who give desired objects abundantly, (your)
- यामन् (*yāman*)—after the going
- सः क्षयः (*saḥ kṣayaḥ*)—that well-known dwelling-place of ours
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सुप्रावीः अस्तु (*suprāvīḥ astu*)—will become well protected

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, you who remove our sins and carry us across: after you have come to us and gone, the house where we dwell will become well protected, without any fear.

##### English translation
May this our dwelling be well protected, liberal deities, on your departure, you who purify us from sin.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त स्व॒राजो॒ अदि॑ति॒रद॑ब्धस्य व्र॒तस्य॒ ये ।  
> म॒हो राजा॑न ईशते ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 468

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । स्वराजः । अदितिः । अदब्धस्य । व्रतस्य । ये ।  
> महः । राजानः । ईशते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च ये मित्रादयस्त्रयः स्वराजः सर्वस्य स्वामिनोऽदितिस्तेषां माता च संति अदब्धस्याहिंसितस्य महो महतो व्रतस्यास्य कर्मणो राजानः स्वामिनः ते ईशते समर्था भवंति । अभिमतं दातुमिति शेषः । अथवैवं योज्यं । ये मित्रादयोऽदितिश्चादब्धस्य व्रतस्य स्वराज ईश्वराः ते महो महतोऽस्मदभिमतधनस्य राजानः स्वामिनः संत ईशतेऽस्मभ्यं तद्दातुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Moreover": those three, Mitra and the others, who are self-sovereign (स्वराजः (*svarājaḥ*) = lords of all), and Aditi their mother, are the lords (राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)) of this great (महः (*mahaḥ*)) and unharmed (अदब्धस्य (*adabdhasya*)) rite (व्रतस्य (*vratasya*)); they are able (ईशते (*īśate*)) to give what is desired (this is the supplied remainder). Or else construe thus: those, Mitra and the others and Aditi, who are lords of the unharmed rite, are, as lords of the great wealth we desire, able to give it to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- ये (*ye*)—those Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman who
- स्वराजः (*svarājaḥ*)—are lords of all, they
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—and their mother, the goddess Aditi too
- अदब्धस्य (*adabdhasya*)—of the unharmed (unobstructed)
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—and great
- व्रतस्य (*vratasya*)—of this sacrificial rite
- राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)—as masters
- ईशते (*īśate*)—are givers of what we desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, lords of all, and their mother the goddess Aditi too, as owners of this great sacrifice of ours, which is performed without obstruction, give us what we desire.

##### English translation
And who are sovereign over all, and, with Aditi, preside over this unobstructed and great ceremony.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रति॑ वां॒ सूर॒ उदि॑ते मि॒त्रं गृ॑णीषे॒ वरु॑णं ।  
> अ॒र्य॒मणं॑ रि॒शाद॑सं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । वां । सूरे । उत्इते । मित्रं । गृणीषे । वरुणं ।  
> अर्यमणं । रिशादसं ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 469

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रति वामित्येष तृचश्चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणस्य पर्यासार्थः । सूत्रितं च । प्रति वां सूर उदिते व्यंतरिक्षमतिरत् । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥
> हे मित्रावरुणौ मित्रं त्वां वरुणं च युवां रिशादसं शत्रूणामत्तारमर्यमणं च प्रति प्रत्येकं गृणीषे । स्तुवे । कदेति उच्यते । सूरे सूर्ये देव उदिते सति । प्रातःकाल इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This triplet beginning प्रति वां (*prati vāṃ*) is the paryāsa recitation of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest at the morning pressing on the Cāturviṃśika day. He cites the sūtra प्रति वां सूर उदिते व्यंतरिक्षमतिरत् (*prati vāṃ sūra udite vyaṃtarikṣamatirat*) (Ā. 7-2). Addressing Mitra and Varuna, the poet says: "I praise each of you, Mitra and Varuna, and Aryaman, the devourer of enemies." When? When the sun, the god, has risen, that is, in the morning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरे (*sūre*)—the sun
- उदिते (*udite*)—when he rises, that is, in the morning
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—Mitra
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuna
- वां (*vāṃ*)—both of you
- रिशादसं (*riśādasaṃ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*)—the god Aryaman
- प्रति (*prati*)—addressing
- गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuna, as the sun rises, this morning I praise you separately, addressing Mitra, Varuna, and Aryaman, the destroyer of enemies.

##### English translation
I glorify you, Mitra and Varuna, and Aryaman, the consumer of enemies when the sun has risen.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the morning pressing on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, this triplet (three Ṛks) beginning प्रति वां (*prati vāṃ*) is to be recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa as a paryāsa. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra प्रति वां सूर उदिते व्यंतरिक्षमतिरत् (*prati vāṃ sūra udite vyaṃtarikṣamatirat*) (Ā. 7-2).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रा॒या हि॑रण्य॒या म॒तिरि॒यम॑वृ॒काय॒ शव॑से ।  
> इ॒यं विप्रा॑ मे॒धसा॑तये ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> राया । हिरण्यया । मतिः । इयं । अवृकाय । शवसे ।  
> इयं । विप्रा । मेधसातये ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 470

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हिरण्यया हितरमणीयेन राया धनेन सहितायावृकायाहिंस्याय शवसेऽस्माकं बलायेयमिदानीं क्रियमाणा मतिः स्तुतिर्भवत्विति शेषः ॥ हिरण्ययेत्यत्र सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयैकवचनस्य याचादेशः ॥ किंच हे विप्राः प्राज्ञाः इयं मे च स्तुतिर्मेधसातये यज्ञलाभाय च भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"May this praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)) now being made be for our strength (शवसे (*śavase*)), unharmed (अवृकाय (*avṛkāya*)), together with golden, that is, most delightful, wealth (राया (*rāyā*))." "May be" is to be supplied. Further: "O wise ones (विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)), may this praise of mine also be for the gaining of the sacrifice (मेधसातये (*medhasātaye*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)—beneficial and delightful
- राया (*rāyā*)—with wealth
- अवृकाय (*avṛkāya*)—free from harm
- शवसे (*śavase*)—for the increase of our strength
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this which we now recite
- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—may the praise be the means
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—O wise gods
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this praise of ours
- मेधसातये (*medhasātaye*)—may it also be for the gaining of the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise gods, may the praise we now recite to you be the means of obtaining wealth, strength and the gain of the sacrifice for us.

##### English translation
May this praise (be effective) for unimpeached strength, along with golden treasure: may it (be effective), sages, for the fulfilment of (the objects of) the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते स्या॑म देव वरुण॒ ते मि॑त्र सू॒रिभिः॑ स॒ह ।  
> इषं॒ स्व॑श्च धीमहि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । स्याम । देव । वरुण । ते । मित्र । सूरिभिः । सह ।  
> इषं । स्वरिति स्वः । च । धीमहि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव वरुण ते वयं तव स्तोतारः स्याम । समृद्धा भवेम । न केवलं वयमेव यजमानाः किंतु सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः सह । तथा हे मित्र देव ते वयं सूरिभिः सह स्याम । भवेम । किंचेषमन्नं स्वरुदकं च धीमहि । धारयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O divine Varuna, may we be yours, your praisers; may we prosper. Not we alone, the sacrificers, but together with the wise (सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)), the praising priests. Likewise, O divine Mitra, may we be yours together with the wise. Further, may we obtain (धीमहि (*dhīmahi*), we hold) food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)) and water (स्वः (*svaḥ*))."

### Printed p. 471

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—O shining one
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuna
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- ते (*te*)—we who praise you
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—with the praising priests
- सह (*saha*)—together
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be prosperous
- ते (*te*)—we
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—water
- धीमहि (*dhīmahi*)—we ask and pray for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Varuna, O Mitra, together with the praising priests may we be prosperous. We who praise you ask and pray that you give us food and other nourishment, and water in the form of rain.

##### English translation
May we be yours, divine Varuna: may we, along with pious worshippers, be, Mitra, yours: may we obtain food and water.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब॒हवः॒ सूर॑चक्षसोऽग्निजि॒ह्वा ऋ॑ता॒वृधः॑ ।  
> त्रीणि॒ ये ये॒मुर्वि॒दथा॑नि धी॒तिभि॒र्विश्वा॑नि॒ परि॑भूतिभिः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बहवः । सूरचक्षसः । अग्निजिह्वाः । ऋतावृधः ।  
> त्रीणि । ये । येमुः । विदथानि । धीतिभिः । विश्वानि । परिभूतिभिः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आश्विनशस्त्रे बहवः सूरचक्षस इति प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च । बहवः सूरचक्षस इति प्रगाथाः । आ. ६-५ । इति ॥ दशरात्रे पंचमेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे स्त्रिहैयं प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च । बहवः सूरचक्षस इमा उ वां दिदिष्टयः । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥
> बहवो महांतः सूरचक्षसः सूर्यसदृशप्रकाशाः । सूरः प्रकाशको येषामिति वा । अग्निजिह्वाः । अग्निरेव जिह्वादानसाधनो येषां तादृशाः । ऋतावृधो यज्ञस्य वर्धयितारो मित्रादयः । किंच ये त्रीणि विश्वानि व्याप्तानि विदथानि त्रित्वादिस्थानानि त्रित्वादीनि परिभूतिभिः परिभावुकैर्धीतिभिः कर्मभिर्येमुः प्रयच्छंति ते

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Āśvina śastra, बहवः सूरचक्षसः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ*) is a pragātha; the sūtra is बहवः सूरचक्षस इति प्रगाथाः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasa iti pragāthāḥ*) (Ā. 6-5). On the fifth day of the Daśarātra, in the Praüga śastra, it is a pragātha of three verses; the sūtra is बहवः सूरचक्षस इमा उ वां दिदिष्टयः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasa imā u vāṃ didiṣṭayaḥ*) (Ā. 7-12).
बहवः (*bahavaḥ*) are the many, the great; सूरचक्षसः (*sūracakṣasaḥ*) are those of radiance like the sun's, or those whose illuminator is the sun. अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*) are those whose tongue, the means of receiving offerings, is Agni himself. ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*) are Mitra and the others, who augment the sacrifice. Further, those who with comprehensive (परिभूतिभिः (*paribhūtibhiḥ*)) rites (धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)) have given (येमुः (*yemuḥ*)) the three all-pervading places (विदथानि (*vidathāni*)), the triple stations and so on, they have attained (आशत (*āśata*)) the ruling power (क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)); this is to be connected in the next verse.

### Printed p. 472

> क्षत्रमाशतेत्येतत्तत्र संबंधनीयं । अथवात्रैव ये त्रीणि स्थानानि प्रयच्छंति ते बहुत्वादिगुणोपेता आगच्छंत्वित्यध्याहार्यं ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Alternatively, here itself, those who give the three stations, endowed with the qualities of multitude and the rest, are to be asked to come; "may they come" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बहवः (*bahavaḥ*)—those of great nature
- सूरचक्षसः (*sūracakṣasaḥ*)—those shining with radiance equal to the sun, or those illumined by the sun
- अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*)—those who, in sacrifices, take Agni as their tongue, that is, their means of receiving oblations
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—those who cause the sacrifice to prosper without obstruction
- ये (*ye*)—those Mitra, Varuna and others who
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all-pervading
- त्रीणि विदथानि (*trīṇi vidathāni*)—the three stations, earth and the rest
- परिभूतिभिः (*paribhūtibhiḥ*)—with your powerful
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—with rites
- येमुः (*yemuḥ*)—those who give, may those Mitra, Varuna and others come here

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those deities, Mitra, Varuna and the rest, come to this sacrificial ground: the venerable ones, shining with sun-like radiance or making the sun shine, who receive the oblations through the tongue of Agni, that is, the flame, who augment the sacrifice, and who by their powerful rites give the three all-pervading stations, earth and the rest.

##### English translation
Manifold, radiant as the sun, Agni-tongued augmenters of sacrifice, you who have limited the three universal sacrifices with comprehensive rites.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Āśvina śastra mantras this Ṛk beginning बहवः सूरचक्षसः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ*) is to be recited as a pragātha mantra, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra बहवः सूरचक्षसः इति प्रगाथाः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ iti pragāthāḥ*) (Ā. 6-5). And on the fifth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, when the Praüga śastra mantras are recited, this Ṛk is likewise to be recited as a pragātha, as set out by the sūtra बहवः सूरचक्षस इमा उ वां दिविष्टयः (*bahavaḥ sūracakṣasa imā u vāṃ diviṣṭayaḥ*) (Ā. 7-12).

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । ये । दधुः । शरदं । मासं । आत् । अहः । यज्ञं । अक्तुं । च । आत् । ऋचं ।  
> अनाप्यं । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । क्षत्रं । राजानः । आशत  ११

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मित्रादयः शरदं संवत्सरं वि दधुः अकुर्वन् अदनंतरमेव मासमनंतरमहरनंतरमहःसाध्यं यज्ञं अदनंतरमक्तुं रात्रिं च ऋचं मंत्रांश्च । यद्वा । सर्वत्रादित्यमुपीत्यर्थे वर्तते । तथा सति क्रमोऽविवक्षितः । ते वरुणो मित्रोऽर्यमा च त्रयोऽनाप्यमन्यैरप्राप्तं क्षत्रं बलं राजानो राजमाना आशत । व्याप्तवंतः ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Mitra and the others who established (वि दधुः (*vi dadhuḥ*)) the year (शरदं (*śaradaṃ*)), and next the month, next the day, the sacrifice to be accomplished by day, next the night (अक्तुं (*aktuṃ*)), and the Ṛk, the mantras. Or else, आत् (*āt*) has everywhere the sense "and"; then the order is not intended. Those three, Varuna, Mitra and Aryaman, shining as kings, have attained (आशत (*āśata*)) unattainable (अनाप्यं (*anāpyaṃ*)) power (क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)), not reached by others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—those Mitra and other deities who
- शरदं (*śaradaṃ*)—the measure of time called the year
- आत् (*āt*)—and (or, afterwards)
- मासं (*māsaṃ*)—the month, that is, the measure of a month
- अहः (*ahaḥ*)—the day
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrificial rite
- अक्तुं (*aktuṃ*)—the night
- ऋचं (*ṛcaṃ*)—the mantras
- विदधुः (*vidadhuḥ*)—who made, that is, created
- राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)—shining, or lords of all
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuna
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman, these three
- अनाप्यं (*anāpyaṃ*)—unattainable by others
- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—strength and capacity
- आशत (*āśata*)—have obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These deities, Mitra and the others, have made the measures of time, year, month, day and night, the sacrificial rites, and the mantras needed for them. These three shining deities, Mitra, Varuna and Aryaman, have obtained strength and capacity that others cannot attain.

##### English translation
Who have established the year, and then the month and the day, the sacrifice, the night, and the holy text, they the royal deities, Varuna, Mitra Aryaman, enjoy unrivalled might.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । वः । अद्य । मनामहे । सुउक्तैः । सूरे । उत्ऽइते ।  
> यत् । ओहते । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । यूयं । ऋतस्य । रथ्यः

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्प्रसिद्धमद्यास्मिन्यागकाले वो युष्मान्मनामहे । याचामहे । कैः साधनैः । सूक्तैः । कस्मिन्काले । सूर उदिते । प्रातःकाल इत्यर्थः । यद्धनं हे ऋतस्योदकस्य रथ्यो नेतारः यूयं वरुणादय ओहते । यूयमित्यनेन सामानाधिकरण्यादोहत इत्यत्र पुरुषव्यत्ययः । ओहध्व इत्यर्थः । तद्धनं मनामह इति ‖

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"That well-known (wealth), today, at this time of the sacrifice, we beg (मनामहे (*manāmahe*)) of you." By what means? By well-spoken hymns (सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)). At what time? When the sun has risen, that is, in the morning. "The wealth which you, O Varuna and the rest, leaders (रथ्यः (*rathyaḥ*)) of the water (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)), convey (ओहते (*ohate*))." Because of agreement with यूयं (*yūyaṃ*), in ओहते (*ohate*) there is a change of person; the sense is ओहध्व (*ohadhva*) ("you convey"). "That wealth we ask for."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- रथ्यः (*rathyaḥ*)—O Mitra and the rest, leaders
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- सूरे उदिते (*sūre udite*)—when the sun rises, that is, in the morning
- यत् (*yat*)—which wealth
- ओहते (*ohate*)—you carry for the praisers
- तत् (*tat*)—that well-known wealth (that you give us)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—of you
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*)—with hymns and the like
- मनामहे (*manāmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and the other deities who provide rain and water to people, as the sun rises we praise you with hymns at this time of the sacrifice and ask that you give us the wealth which you carry for your devotees.

##### English translation
Therefore to-day at sunrise we solicit you with hymns for (wealth) Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, bearers of water, you convey.

### Printed p. 475

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये यूयमृतावान ऋतवंतो यज्ञवंत उदकवंतो वा ऋतजाताः । उक्त ऋतशब्दार्थः । तदर्थमुत्पन्नाः । अथवा । ऋतात्प्रजापतेः सकाशादुत्पन्नाः । ऋतावृध उक्तार्थस्यर्तस्य वर्धयितारो घोरासो घोरा अनृतद्विषोऽयज्वद्वेष्टारः तेषां वो युष्माकं सुच्छर्दिष्टमे सुखतमे सुम्ने धनेऽत्यंतरमणीयेगृहयुक्ते सुखे वा ये वयं ये चास्ये सूरयः स्तोतारः ते सर्वे स्यामु । भवेमु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses the words of the verse. ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*) means those who possess ऋत (*ṛta*): rites or sacrifice, or water. ऋतजाताः (*ṛtajātāḥ*) means those born for that purpose, or else those born from Ṛta, that is, from Prajāpati. ऋतावृध (*ṛtāvṛdha*) means those who increase Ṛta in the sense already stated. *ghorāsaḥ* means the fierce. अनृतद्विषः (*anṛtadviṣaḥ*) means haters of those who do not sacrifice. सुच्छर्दिष्टमे (*succhardiṣṭame*) means "most pleasant", and सुम्ने (*sumne*) means "in wealth" or in a delightful happiness that includes a house. The sense is: "May we, and those others who are your praisers, all be in that happiness of yours."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*)—performers of sacrifice, or givers of water
- ऋतजाताः (*ṛtajātāḥ*)—those born for the sake of sacrifice, or for giving water
- ऋतवृधः (*ṛtavṛdhaḥ*)—those who increase the sacrifice or the water
- घोरासे (*ghorāse*)—those who behave cruelly toward enemies
- अनृतद्विषः (*anṛtadviṣaḥ*)—those who cannot bear liars, or who hate those who do not sacrifice
- तेषां वः (*teṣāṃ vaḥ*)—of you, who are distinguished by such qualities
- सुच्छर्दिष्टमे (*succhardiṣṭame*)—pleasant
- सुम्ने (*sumne*)—in the matter of giving wealth
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—we, the sacrificers
- ये च सूरयः (*ye ca sūrayaḥ*)—and the other people who praise
- स्यामु (*syāmu*)—may we become worthy of your favour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra, Varuṇa and the other deities! You are the managers of the sacrifice, or those who supply people with water in the form of rain; you are born for the sake of the sacrifice or of the water, and you make the sacrifice or the water increase. You are cruel by nature toward enemies and hate those who speak untruth or do not sacrifice. May we, the sacrificers, and the others who praise you, become worthy of your favour in your pleasant gift of wealth.

##### English translation
Acceptors of rites, generated for rites, augmenters of rites, fierce enemies of the neglector of rites, may we, as well as those men who are your adorers, be in (the enjoyment of) the highest felicity, all confirmed by you.
