> यत् । ईं । आशुः । वहति । देवः । एतशः । विश्वस्मै । चक्षसे । अरं ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोमातिरेके माध्यंदिनसवने नैमित्तिके शस्त्र उदु त्यदित्ययं प्रगाथोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । ब्रह्मा असि सूर्योदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । आ. ७. ७ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवनेऽयमेव वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । उदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरुदु त्ये मधुमत्तमाः । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> त्यत्तद्दर्शतं दर्शनीयं वपुर्मंडलं दिवोऽंतरिक्षस्य प्रतिह्वरे समीपे उद्येति । उदेति । उ इति पूरणः । यदीं यदेतन्मंडलमाशुः शीघ्रगाम्येतश एतवर्णोऽश्वो वहति धारयति । किमर्थं । विश्वस्मै सर्वस्मा अरं चक्षसे सम्यक्सर्वलोकदर्शनाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: at the midday pressing, in the occasional (naimittika) śastra when there is an excess of soma, this verse उदु त्यत् (*udu tyat*) is the pragātha anurūpa. It is stated in the sūtra: ब्रह्मा असि सूर्योदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*brahmā asi sūryodu tyaddarśataṃ vapuriti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. 7-7). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, this same verse is the optional stotriya tṛca; the sūtra is उदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरुदु त्ये मधुमत्तमाः (*udu tyaddarśataṃ vapurudu tye madhumattamāḥ*) (Ā. 7-4).
Meaning: that beautiful form, the orb, rises near the edge of the sky; उ (*u*) is a filler. The swift Etaśa, the white-coloured horse, bears that orb, for what purpose? For all to see well, that is, for the clear viewing of the whole world.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्यत् (*tyat*)—that well-known
- दर्शतं (*darśataṃ*)—visible to all, or beautiful
- वपुः (*vapuḥ*)—the orb of the sun
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the sky
- प्रतिह्वरे (*pratihvare*)—near, that is, at the edge
- उदु एति (*udu eti*)—rises
- यदीं (*yadīṃ*)—that sun-orb which is such
- आशुः (*āśuḥ*)—swiftly moving
- एतशः (*etaśaḥ*)—the sun's horse
- विश्वस्मै अरं चक्षसे (*viśvasmai araṃ cakṣase*)—so that all people may see well
- वहति (*vahati*)—carries

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known sun-orb, visible to all, is just now rising at the edge of the sky. The swift horse of the sun carries this orb along the path of the sky so that all people may see it well.

##### English translation
That beautiful orb (of the sun) rises on the near margin of the sky as the swift, divine, white-coloured (steed) bears it along for the beholding of all men.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When there is an excess of soma at the midday pressing, in reciting the mantras of the occasional śastra, this Ṛk beginning उदु त्यत् (*udu tyat*) is to be recited as the anurūpa pragātha mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra
### Printed p. 477
ब्रह्मा असि सूर्योदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*brahmā asi sūryodu tyaddarśataṃ vapuriti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. 7-7). And on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, this same Ṛk is to be recited as the optional stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra उदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुरुदु त्ये मधुमत्तमाः (*udu tyaddarśataṃ vapurudu tye madhumattamāḥ*) (Ā. 7-4).

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शी॒र्ष्णःशी॑र्ष्णो॒ जग॑तस्त॒स्थुष॒स्पतिं॑ स॒मया॒ विश्व॒मा रजः॑ ।  
> स॒प्त स्वसा॑रः सुवि॒ताय॒ सूर्यं॒ वहं॑ति ह॒रितो॒ रथे॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शीर्ष्णःऽशीर्ष्णः । जगतः । तस्थुषः । पतिं । समया । विश्वं । आ । रजः ।  
> सप्त । स्वसारः । सुविताय । सूर्यं । वहंति । हरितः । रथे ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शीर्ष्णः शीर्ष्णः सर्वस्यापि शिरसः । तृतीयार्थे पंचमी । स्वस्वशिरसेत्यर्थः । सूर्यं वहंतीत्यनेन संबध्यते । अथवा शिरःशब्देन श्रेष्ठपदार्थो लक्ष्यते । वीप्सया तस्य कार्त्स्न्यमुच्यते । सर्वस्य श्रेष्ठमित्यर्थः । जगतो जंगमस्य तस्थुषः स्थावरस्य पतिं स्वामिनं रथे वर्तमानं सूर्यं सुविताय कल्याणाय विश्वं रजः समया सर्वलोकस्य समीपे ॥ अभितः परितः समयेत्यादिना । म २-३-२-१ । समयाशब्दयोगात् द्वितीया ॥ सप्त सप्तसंख्याकाः स्वसारोऽन्यनिरपेक्षेण स्वयमेव सरंत्यो हरितो हरितवर्णा अश्वा वहंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शीर्ष्णः शीर्ष्णः (*śīrṣṇaḥ śīrṣṇaḥ*) means "of every head"; the fifth case is used in the sense of the third, so the meaning is "each by its own head", construed with सूर्यं वहंति (*sūryaṃ vahaṃti*). Or else the word "head" denotes the chief thing, and by repetition totality is expressed: the best of everything. He is the lord of the moving world and of the stationary, the sun in his chariot. विश्वं रजः (*viśvaṃ rajaḥ*) is in the accusative because of the word समया (*samayā*) ("near"), by the rule cited as Ma. 2-3-2-1: near the whole world, for its welfare. The seven self-moving, that is, independent, green-coloured horses carry him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शीर्ष्णःशीर्ष्णः (*śīrṣṇaḥśīrṣṇaḥ*)—supreme like the head
- जगतः तस्थुषः (*jagataḥ tasthuṣaḥ*)—of the whole world, moving and stationary
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—the lord
- रथे (*rathe*)—seated in the chariot
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—for the welfare of the world
- विश्वं रजः (*viśvaṃ rajaḥ*)—of all the worlds
- समया (*samayā*)—near
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—having the power to move by themselves
- सप्त हरितः (*sapta haritaḥ*)—the seven green-coloured horses of the sun
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—carry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven green horses of the sun, moving of themselves (without anyone's impulsion), carry the sun, lord of the whole world of the moving and the unmoving, seated in his chariot, for the welfare of the world, near the earth and sky, that is, so that all can see him.
### Printed p. 478

##### English translation
The seven gliding steeds convey the sun, the lord of every individual moving of stationary thing, traversing the whole world in his chariot for the good (of all).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तच्चक्षु॑र्दे॒वहि॑तं शु॒क्रमु॒च्चर॑त् ।  
> पश्ये॑मु श॒रदः॑ श॒तं जीवे॑मु श॒रदः॑ श॒तं ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । चक्षुः । देवऽहितं । शुक्रं । उत्ऽचरत् ।  
> पश्येम । शरदः । शतं । जीवेम । शरदः । शतं ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्प्रसिद्धं चक्षुः सर्वस्य प्रकाशकं देवहितं देवानां हितं । तेषां हविःस्वीकारस्यैतदधीनत्वात् । अथवा देवेन हितं । शुक्रं निर्मलं सूर्यमंडलमुच्चरत् । उद्गच्छति । तच्छरदः शतं शतसंवत्सरं पश्येमु । जीवेमु शरदः शतं । पुनः श्रुतिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known eye, the illuminator of all, is देवहितं (*devahitaṃ*), beneficial to the gods, since their acceptance of oblations depends on it; or else it is "set by a god". शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*) means the pure orb of the sun, which *uccarat* rises. "May we see it for a hundred autumns, a hundred years; may we live a hundred autumns." The repetition of the phrase is for emphasis.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तत् (*tat*)—that well-known
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—that which is like an eye for the whole universe, or which gives light
- देवहितं (*devahitaṃ*)—beneficial to the gods, or placed in the sky by the gods for the welfare of the world
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—the pure (bright) orb of the sun
- उत्चरत् (*utcarat*)—rises and moves (or moves westward in the upper region of the sky)
- तत् (*tat*)—that sun-orb
- शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*)—for a hundred years
- पश्येमु (*paśyemu*)—may we see
- शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*)—for a hundred years
- जीवेमु (*jīvemu*)—may we live

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sun-orb, which is like an eye for the whole world or sheds light, which is beneficial to the gods or placed in the sky by the gods for the world's good, and which shines pure, moves westward in the sky after rising. May we live a hundred years and see such a sun-orb; that is, may we live long.
### Printed p. 479

##### English translation
That pure eye (of the universe), beneficial to the gods, rises : may we behold it for a hundred years : may we live a hundred years.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> काव्ये॑भिरदा॒भ्या या॑तं वरुण द्यु॒मत् ।  
> मि॒त्रश्च॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> काव्येभिः । अदाभ्या । आ । यातं । वरुण । द्युऽमत् ।  
> मित्रः । च । सोमऽपीतये ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पृष्ठ्यभिप्लवषडहयोः स्तोमनिमित्त आवापे काव्येभिरदाभ्येति तृचः ।
> काव्येभिरदाभ्येति तिस्रः । आ. ७-५ । इति हि सूत्रितं ॥
> हे अदाभ्यादंभनीयौ हे वरुण त्वं मित्रश्च द्युमद्द्युतिमंतौ युवां काव्येभिरस्मत्कृतैः स्तोत्रैरा यातं । किमर्थं । सोमपीतये सोमपानाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: in the insertion (āvāpa) occasioned by the stomas in the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas, the tṛca काव्येभिरदाभ्या (*kāvyebhiradābhyā*) is used; the sūtra is काव्येभिरदाभ्येति तिस्रः (*kāvyebhiradābhyeti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 7-5).
Meaning: O Varuṇa, you and Mitra, unassailable and radiant, come with the praises made by us. For what purpose? To drink soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदाभ्या (*adābhyā*)—unassailable by enemies
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa, you
- मित्रः च (*mitraḥ ca*)—and Mitra
- द्युमत् (*dyumat*)—you two, radiant
- काव्येभिः (*kāvyebhiḥ*)—praised by the hymns we make
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for drinking soma
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, free from the molestation of enemies and radiant, come here, praised by our hymns and the like, to drink soma.

##### English translation
Unconquerable, resplendet Varuna and Mitra, (induced) by our praises, come to drink the soma juice.
### Printed p. 480

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, for the insertion of the stomas, this tṛca, that is, three Ṛks, beginning काव्येभिरदाभ्या (*kāvyebhiradābhyā*) is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra काव्येभिरदाभ्येति तिस्रः (*kāvyebhiradābhyeti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 7-5).

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वो धाम॑भिर्वरुण मि॒त्रश्चा या॑तम॒द्रुहा॑ ।  
> पिब॑तं॒ सोम॑मातु॒जे ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः । धामऽभिः । वरुण । मित्रः । च । आ । यातं । अद्रुहा ।  
> पिबतं । सोमं । आतुजी इत्याऽतुजी ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण त्वं मित्रश्चाद्रुहा द्रोग्धारौ युवां दिवो द्युलोकसंबंधिभ्यो धामभिर्धामभ्यः स्थानेभ्यः । पंचम्यर्थे तृतीया । अथवा धामभिस्तेजोभिर्विभूतिभिः सार्धमा यातं । अस्मद्यज्ञमागच्छतं । आगत्य चातुजे शत्रूणां सर्वतो हिंसकावादातारौ वा धनानां एवं रूपौ संतौ सोमं पिबतं ॥ तुजि पिजि हिंसाबलादाननिकेतनेषु । अत्र हिंसायामादाने वा वर्तते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, you and Mitra, अद्रुहा (*adruhā*), harming none, come with the abodes (धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)) belonging to the heavenly world; the instrumental is used in the sense of the ablative, "from the places". Or else, come together with your splendours and powers: come to our sacrifice. Having come, you two, who are आतुजे (*ātuje*), injurers of enemies on every side, or receivers of wealth, drink the soma. The root तुजि (*tuji*) (with पिजि (*piji*)) is used in the senses of harming, strength, taking, and dwelling; here it is in the sense of harming or taking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa, you
- मित्रः च (*mitraḥ ca*)—and Mitra
- अद्रुहा (*adruhā*)—you two, who wish no one harm
- दिवः धामभिः (*divaḥ dhāmabhiḥ*)—from the places of the heavenly world, or radiant
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—come (toward our sacrifice), and then
- आतुजे (*ātuje*)—you who harm enemies everywhere, or give wealth and the like to the praisers
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the soma juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, who do harm to none, set out from your places in the heavenly world, shining with radiance, and come to our sacrifice. Then, as destroyers of enemies or givers of wealth, drink the soma juice at our sacrifice.

### Printed p. 481

##### English translation
Gentle Mitra and Varuna, destroyers of foes, come from heaven with your glories, and drink the Soma juice.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ या॑तं मित्रावरुणा जुषा॒णावाहु॑तिं नरा ।  
> पा॒तं सोम॑मृतावृधा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । यातं । मित्रावरुणा । जुषाणौ । आऽहुतिं । नरा ।  
> पातं । सोमं । ऋतऽवृधा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ हे नरा योगनेतारौ आहुतिं सोमलक्षणां जुषाणौ प्रियमाणौ संतावा यातं । आगच्छतं यज्ञं । आगत्य च हे ऋतावृधा यज्ञस्य वर्धकौ युवां सोमं पातं । पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, O leaders (the guides of the rite), being pleased with the oblation, which consists of Soma, come (आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)) to the sacrifice. Having come, O augmenters of the sacrifice (ऋतावृधा (*ṛtāvṛdhā*)), drink (पातं (*pātaṃ*)) the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—O leaders of the sacrifice
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- आहुतिं (*āhutiṃ*)—the oblation, which consists of Soma
- जुषाणा (*juṣāṇā*)—loving it (or, in order to partake of it)
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—come to our place of sacrifice. (Then)
- ऋतवृधा (*ṛtavṛdhā*)—you, the augmenters of the sacrifice
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, conductors of the sacrifice, you who are fond of Soma, the oblation of the sacrifice, come to our place of sacrifice in order to partake of it. After you have come, you who augment the sacrifice, drink the Soma in our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Come, Mitra and Varuna, leaders of rites, propitiated by the oblation, and drink the Soma, augmenters of the sacrthe sacred rite.

### Printed p. 482
## Sūkta 67 (Maṇḍala 7)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta and in the seven sūktas that follow, the Aśvin deities are praised. We have explained the matter of the Aśvins many times before. Here we shall state only a brief introduction to them and, briefly, the details of the help they gave to those who praised them.

The Aśvin deities are two. One of them is named Dasra and the other Nāsatya, but in many places both are called by the dual word Dasrā or Nāsatyā.

**Origin of the Aśvins**
Yāska has spoken thus about the Aśvins in his Nirukta. It appears that even in his time there was a difference of opinion over who these Aśvins are.

अश्विनौ यद्व्यश्नुवाते सर्वं रसेनान्यो ज्योतिषान्यः । अश्वैरश्विनावित्यौर्णवाभः । तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके । अहोरात्रावित्येके । सूर्याचंद्रमसावित्येके । राजानौ पुण्यकृतावित्येके । (*aśvinau yadvyaśnuvāte sarvaṃ rasenānyo jyotiṣānyaḥ | aśvairaśvināvityaurṇavābhaḥ | tatkāvaśvinau dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke | ahorātrāvityeke | sūryācaṃdramasāvityeke | rājānau puṇyakṛtāvityeke |*) (Ni. 12-1)

One view is that, of these deities, one pervades everything with water and the other with light, and so they are called Aśvins. The view of Aurṇavābha is that they are called Aśvins because they are yoked with horses. According to some, they are Heaven and Earth. Others call them Day and Night. According to others they are the Sun and the Moon. According to the view of the historians, two meritorious kings attained this rank and became famous as the Aśvin deities. Having thus stated the differences of opinion, Yāska cited Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4 and another mantra, unspecified, and so expressed the doubt in this matter.

वसातिषु स्म चिरथोऽसितौ पेत्वाविव । कदेदमश्विना युवमभि देवा अगच्छतं ॥ (*vasātiṣu sma ciratho 'sitau petvāviva | kadedamaśvinā yuvamabhi devā agacchataṃ ‖*)

As stated in this mantra, one of them is the son of Vasāti, that is, the son of Night, and the other is the son of Uṣas. If the nature of the Aśvins is to be determined from the statements in the Ṛksaṃhitā, the evidence of the Ṛks cited below may be considered.

त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥ (*tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖*)

### Printed p. 483
अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । उताश्विनावभरद्यत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥ (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate | utāśvināvabharadyattadāsīdajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1, 2)

At the time of his daughter's wedding Tvaṣṭṛ arranged a svayaṃvara and caused the people of the whole world to assemble there. Saraṇyū, the mother of Yama and the wife of Vivasvān, became invisible after the marriage. That is, the immortal gods thought it improper that Saraṇyū had married the mortal Vivasvān, and they hid her so that nobody could see her. Then they made her of the same appearance and gave her to Vivasvān. Afterwards she bore the Aśvins and went away, leaving them, her sons. This is the purport of these Ṛks. And further:

यमा चिदत्र यमसूरसूत जिह्वाया अग्रं पतदा ह्यस्थात् । वपूंषि जाता मिथुना सचेते तमोहना तपुषो बुध्न एता ॥ (*yamā cidatra yamasūrasūta jihvāyā agraṃ patadā hyasthāt | vapūṃṣi jātā mithunā sacete tamohanā tapuṣo budhna etā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-3)

In this Ṛk it is said that the mother of the Aśvins bore twins (she herself bore the children), and that those two twins, embodied together, destroyed darkness. But many accept as universally agreed that Sāyaṇa, in his commentary, explains the word यमसूः (*yamasūḥ*) as उषोऽभिमानिनी देवता अत्र उषःकाले असूते (*uṣo 'bhimāninī devatā atra uṣaḥkāle asūte*), saying that the mother of the Aśvins is the goddess Uṣas. Moreover, the Bṛhaddevatā speaks as follows of Tvaṣṭṛ's giving his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to Vivasvān and of the Aśvins' being born of them:

अभवन्मिथुनं त्वाष्ट्रं सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह । स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत्स्वयमेव विवस्वते ॥ (*abhavanmithunaṃ tvāṣṭraṃ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchatsvayameva vivasvate ‖*)
ततः सरण्य्यां जज्ञाते यमयम्यौ विवस्वतः । तौ चाप्युभौ यमावेव ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ॥ (*tataḥ saraṇyyāṃ jajñāte yamayamyau vivasvataḥ | tau cāpyubhau yamāveva jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ‖*)
सृष्ट्वा भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यूः सदृशीं स्त्रियं । निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्यां अश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ॥ (*sṛṣṭvā bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyūḥ sadṛśīṃ striyaṃ | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyāṃ aśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ‖*)
अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुं । राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ॥ (*avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanuṃ | rājarṣirabhavatso 'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ‖*)
स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रांतां सरण्यूमश्वरूपिणीं । त्वाष्ट्रीं प्रति जगामाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ॥ (*sa vijñāya tvapakrāṃtāṃ saraṇyūmaśvarūpiṇīṃ | tvāṣṭrīṃ prati jagāmāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ‖*)
सरण्यूश्च विवस्वंतं विदित्वा हयरूपिणं । मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः । ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि । (*saraṇyūśca vivasvaṃtaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇaṃ | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ | tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi |*)

### Printed p. 484
उपाजिघ्रच्च सा त्वाष्ट्रा तच्छुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ॥ (*upājighracca sā tvāṣṭrā tacchukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ‖*)
आघ्रातमात्राच्छुक्रात्तु कुमारौ संबभूवतुः । नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ॥ (*āghrātamātrācchukrāttu kumārau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ‖*)
इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यूदेवते द्वृचे । विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वाष्ट्रेति सह मन्यते ॥ (*itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyūdevate dvṛce | vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvāṣṭreti saha manyate ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 6-163 to 7-6)

Tvaṣṭṛ had a daughter named Saraṇyū and a son named Triśiras. He gave his daughter Saraṇyū in marriage to Vivasvān. Afterwards two children, Yama and Yamī, were born to Vivasvān by his wife Saraṇyū. These two were twins, born together; of them Yama was the elder. One day, when her husband Vivasvān was absent, Saraṇyū created another woman who resembled herself, handed her twin children over to her charge, took the form of a mare, left that place, and went to another place without Vivasvān's knowledge, and remained unseen. But Vivasvān, unaware of this, united with the woman who had been put in Saraṇyū's place. As a result Manu was born. Manu too, like his father, became resplendent and a great royal sage; his fame spread through all the worlds. After some time true knowledge came to Vivasvān. Having learned that Saraṇyū had gone away in the form of a mare, he too took the form of a male horse, followed Tvaṣṭṛ's daughter to the place where she had gone, and tried to unite with her. Saraṇyū, knowing that Vivasvān had followed her, himself in the form of a horse, desired the pleasure of union with him. Then Vivasvān fulfilled her wish. In the excitement of their union Vivasvān's seed fell on the ground. Then Saraṇyū, desiring conception, smelled it. As soon as she had smelled that seed (semen), a conception arose in her, and from it two youths, Nāsatya and Dasra, were born. Afterwards they were called by the name Aśvins, and their greatness spread through all the worlds. So it is said.

**Chariot of the Aśvins, etc.**
The chariot of the Aśvins is golden, and all its parts, wheels, axle and the rest, are made of gold (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-44-4; 1-180-1; 8-5-39; 8-22-8, etc.). It is a peculiar chariot. It has three wheels, three felloes, and some other parts also in threes. It has the speed of thought. A three-wheeled chariot belongs to them alone; no one else has a chariot of that kind.

यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप । क्वैकं चक्रं वामासीत् क्व देष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ॥ (*yadayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryāmupa | kvaikaṃ cakraṃ vāmāsīt kva deṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-15)

### Printed p. 485
Here it is said that when they went to the wedding of the goddess Sūryā, one wheel of their chariot was ruined.

On this matter there is a story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

प्रजापतिः सवितुः दुहितरं सूर्यां सोमाय राज्ञे प्रायच्छत् । ये त्वन्ये देवाः तां वरयितुमागच्छन् । तेभ्यो विवाहादनंतरमृक्सहस्रमददात् । यदेतदाश्विनं नाम तस्मिन्देवा विवादमकुर्वन् । ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्त्विति । तेऽब्रुवन् । आजिं धावाम । यो नो जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति । तेऽग्नेर्गृहपतेरुपर्यादित्यं काष्ठां कृत्वाभिधावन् ! काष्ठा आज्यंत उच्यते । अश्वतरीरथेनाग्निराजिमधावत् । गोभिरुरुणैरुषाः । हरिरथेनेंद्रः । गर्दभरथेनाश्विनौ । तत्राश्विनावजयतां ॥ (*prajāpatiḥ savituḥ duhitaraṃ sūryāṃ somāya rājñe prāyacchat | ye tvanye devāḥ tāṃ varayitumāgacchan | tebhyo vivāhādanaṃtaramṛksahasramadadāt | yadetadāśvinaṃ nāma tasmindevā vivādamakurvan | mamedamastu mamedamastviti | te 'bruvan | ājiṃ dhāvāma | yo no jeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | te 'gnergṛhapateruparyādityaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ kṛtvābhidhāvan ! kāṣṭhā ājyaṃta ucyate | aśvatarīrathenāgnirājimadhāvat | gobhiruruṇairuṣāḥ | hariratheneṃdraḥ | gardabharathenāśvinau | tatrāśvināvajayatāṃ ‖*)

Brahmā gave Sūryā, the daughter of the god Savitṛ, in marriage to King Soma. Then the other gods came to woo her. After the marriage he gave them a thousand Ṛks. The name Āśvina Ṛks became well known for these Ṛks. The gods who had come there quarrelled with one another over these Ṛks, each saying: "I want them, I want them." Then they arranged a contest and decided among themselves that whoever won it might have these Ṛks. Then they decided that the contest was to run from the neighbourhood of Agni, the Gṛhapati, up to Āditya, and that whoever reached it first would be adjudged the winner. Then Agni made ready to run in a chariot yoked with mules. The goddess Uṣas came seated in a chariot yoked with red cows. Indra mounted a chariot yoked with his horses called Hari and came there. The Aśvins mounted their own chariot, yoked with asses called Rāsabhas, and came there. Then, as all of them ran, each mounted on his own vehicle, to reach the appointed place, victory fell to the Aśvins. The thousand Ṛks, which were the stake, came to them. Therefore the name Āśvina Ṛks became well known for those Ṛks. In this story the excellence of the Aśvins' chariot is stated. Although the word अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*) means those who possess horses (aśva), it is nowhere said that the name came to them because they were horse-riders. The horses that draw their chariot are said to be horses (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-2), birds (6-62-6), swans (4-45-4), Garuḍa birds (1-118-4), horses of the form of falcons (8-35-2). But their chief vehicle, as Yāska says, is रासभावश्विनोः (*rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ*) (Ni. 12-38): the vehicles of the Aśvins are asses.

कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः । (*kadā yogo vājino rāsabhasya yena yajñaṃ nāsatyopayāthaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-9)

### Printed p. 486
कद्रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय ॥ (*kadrāsabho nāsatyā sahasramājā yamasya pradhane jigāya ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-2)

In these and similar Ṛks it is stated clearly that the rāsabha (ass) is the vehicle of the Aśvins.

Those who perform sacrifices always invoke them in the morning. They are connected with the daughter of the Sun. Sūryā herself chose them (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-69-4); both of them are her husbands (4-43-6). Sūryā mounted their chariot (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-73-5; 8-8-10); the daughter of the Sun mounts their chariot (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-5; 1-117-12; 1-118-5; 6-63-5). They regard Sūryā as their own (7-68-3), and she goes with them in the chariot (8-26-8). There are descriptions of this kind.

**Help given by the Aśvins**
There are many narratives to show that they help people in distress. These have been explained at length in their respective places. Here, however, we have explained only a few of the chief ones:

जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वप्रिं प्रामुंचतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् । प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनां ॥ (*jujuruṣo nāsatyota vapriṃ prāmuṃcataṃ drāpimiva cyavānāt | prātirataṃ jahitasyāyurdasrāditpatimakṛṇutaṃ kanīnāṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-10)

The sage named Cyavana had grown very old; his body was worn out and he had no strength, and his people abandoned him. When this sage prayed to the Aśvins, they came, removed his worn-out body, made him a youth, and made him dear to his wife. And they increased his life. So it is said. Besides:

युवं च्यवनमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । (*yuvaṃ cyavanamaśvinā jaraṃtaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-13)
निष्टौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात्पुनश्च्यवानं चक्रथुर्युवानं । (*niṣṭaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrātpunaścyavānaṃ cakrathuryuvānaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-6)
प्र च्यवानाज्जुरुषो वप्रिमत्कं न मुंचथः । युवा यदी कृथः पुनरा काममृष्वे वध्वः ॥ (*pra cyavānājjuruṣo vaprimatkaṃ na muṃcathaḥ | yuvā yadī kṛthaḥ punarā kāmamṛṣve vadhvaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5)
उत त्यद्वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय प्रतीत्यं हविर्दे । (*uta tyadvāṃ jurate aśvinā bhūccyavānāya pratītyaṃ havirde |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-68-6)
युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वं । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ jaraso 'mumuktaṃ ni pedava ūhathurāśumaśvaṃ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-71-5)

### Printed p. 487
In these Ṛks too there is a description of how the aged sage Cyavana was made young. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as well there is an extended history on this subject. Likewise,

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-8)
In the Ṛk beginning thus, mention is made of how the old age of one called Kali was removed and he was made young.

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-13)
Here it is said that when the aforesaid Kali took a wife and married, they gave him their help and did many services for him.

And they granted a chariot (1-117-19) for the young women who were the wives of Vimada, or one wife for him (1-117-1). She appears to have been the daughter of Purumitra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20; 10-39-7), and her name was Kamadhyu (10-65-12).

They brought back and restored his lost son to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-23; 10-65-12). And in Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-85-1, 2 the names of Viśvaka and Viṣṇāpu are indicated.

The story of Bhujyu is told again and again. Bhujyu was the son of a king named Tugra. While he was making a sea voyage and was sinking, Bhujyu held on to a piece of wood and floated amid the waves. Then he took refuge in the Aśvins. In the great ocean whose depth could not be known, they seated him in a ship with a hundred oars and took him to his home. In an unbroken ship that seemed to fly in the sky, or in four winged boats, or in three flying chariots with a hundred feet and six horses, or in their own chariot with the speed of mind, with the help of their swift horses that fly along, they made Bhujyu sit and brought him and set him in his home. (1-116-3, 4, 5; 1-117-14, 15; 1-182-5, 6, 7; 7-68-7; 1-117-6, 20; 1-118-6; 1-166-4; 1-148-3; 6-62-6; 7-69-7; 8-5-22; 10-39-4; 10-40-2; 10-65-12; 10-143-5)

It is said in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-10; 1-116-15; 1-117-11; 1-118-9; 10-39-9 that a woman named Viśpalā had her leg cut off in battle, and when she prayed to the Aśvins they came, provided her with an iron leg and saved her.

### Printed p. 488
When the Aśvins' mount, the ass, was in the wolf's den, one named Ṛjrāśva cut up a hundred sheep from the flock he was tending and gave them to the wolf as food. His father was angered by this and had Ṛjrāśva's eyes torn out, making him blind. Then the wolf praised the Aśvins. Pleased, they gave Ṛjrāśva eyes. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-16; 1-117-17, 18) In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-17 there is mention of Ṛjrāśva praising Indra.

One called Pārāvṛja was blind and lame, and was not admitted into his caste. The Aśvins gave him the power of sight and the power of walking; that is, they favoured him by giving eyes and feet (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-8). The name of Pārāvṛja is indicated in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-12; 2-15-7, where Indra is the subject.

The sage called Rebha had been bound hand and foot by wicked men and thrown into a disused well. For nine days and ten nights he lay there, near death. The Aśvins lifted him out of the well as one lifts Soma juice with a ladle, and gave him life (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-116-24; 1-117-12; 1-117-4; 1-118-6; 1-189-6; 10-39-9).

Vandana likewise was carried off by wicked men and thrown into a dark place (a pit); the Aśvins rescued him from danger and brought him to the light. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-116-11; 1-117-5; 1-118-6; 10-39-8; 1-189-6, 7)

To Kakṣīvān of the Pajra family they gave boons abundantly, and made mead or honey flow by the hundred jars from a horse's hoof, as through a sieve (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-7; 1-117-6).

The sage Atri, thrown out of hatred and envy into a great pit enveloped in darkness and blazing with fire, was in distress; when he prayed to the Aśvins they came, quenched the fire with frost, gave him food and so on, comforted him and delivered him from that state (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7; 1-116-8; 1-117-3; 1-118-7; 1-189-6; 5-78-4, 5, 6; 7-72-5; 8-62-3, 7, 8, 9; 10-39-9). In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-3 it is indicated that Agni protected Atri.

Vadhrimatī, being childless and barren, prayed to the Aśvins, and they granted her a son named Hiraṇyahasta. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-13; 1-117-24; 6-62-7; 10-39-7)

### Printed p. 489
A woman named Ghoṣā, unmarried, remained in her father's house; at her prayer the Aśvins granted her a suitable husband. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7; 10-39-3, 6; 10-40-5). In the bhāṣya on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7 Sāyaṇa says that this Ghoṣā was suffering from leprosy and that the Aśvins cured that disease. In the tenth Maṇḍala there are two sūktas seen by this woman Ghoṣā (sūktas 39 and 40).

When the cow of one called Śayu had grown old and bore no calf, the Aśvins gave her the power to give milk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-22; 1-112-10; 1-118-8; 1-189-6; 10-39-13).

It is said that the Aśvins gave the king Pedu a white horse, as mighty as Indra, and that by it he conquered his enemies and obtained much wealth, conveyances and the like (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-6; 1-117-9; 1-118-9; 1-189-10; 2-21-3; 10-39-10).

Besides these, as stated in the sūktas 3, 116, 117, 118 and 189 of the first Maṇḍala, these Aśvins are said to have helped many human beings and also to have benefited animals, birds and others. In this connection it is said in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-14; 1-117-16; 1-118-8; 10-39-13 that when a wolf was carrying off a quail in its jaws, at the quail's prayer they freed it from the wolf's mouth and saved it. Besides these matters there are many more concerning the Aśvins; they will be explained in their proper contexts.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रति वां रथमिति दशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं । प्रति वां दशाश्विनं तु तदित्यनुक्रमणिका । ऋषिर्वसिष्ठः । छंदस्त्रिष्टुप् । तुह्यादिपरिभाषयैतदादीन्यष्ट सूक्तान्यश्विदेवत्यानि । प्रातरनुवाके आश्विने क्रतौ त्रैष्टुभे छंदस्येतदादिसूक्तसप्तकं द्वितीयवर्जं शंस्यं । तथा च सूत्रं । प्रति वां रथमिति सप्तानां द्वितीयमुद्धरेत् । आ-४-१५ ॥ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्रति वां रथं (*prati vāṃ rathaṃ*) has ten Ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says प्रति वां दशाश्विनं तु तत् (*prati vāṃ daśāśvinaṃ tu tat*). The seer is Vasiṣṭha, the metre Triṣṭubh. By the rule beginning तुह्यादि (*tuhyādi*) this and the following eight sūktas have the Aśvins as deity. In the Prātaranuvāka, in the Āśvina rite, in the Triṣṭubh metre, this group of seven sūktas, omitting the second, is to be recited. So the sūtra: प्रति वां रथमिति सप्तानां द्वितीयमुद्धरेत् (*prati vāṃ rathamiti saptānāṃ dvitīyamuddharet*) (Ā. 4-15).

The Anuvāda: this sūkta is the twelfth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka; the Anukramaṇikā says as above. Vasiṣṭha is the seer, Triṣṭubh the metre, and the eight sūktas from this onward have the Aśvins as deity. At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, this and the following seven sūktas, omitting the second, are employed for the Triṣṭubh mantras relating to the Āśvina rite, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्रति वां रथमिति सप्तानां द्वितीयमुद्धरेत् (*prati vāṃ rathamiti saptānāṃ dvitīyamuddharet*) (Ā. 4-15).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रति॑ वां॒ रथं॑ नृपती ज॒रध्यै॑ ह॒विष्म॑ता॒ मन॑सा य॒ज्ञिये॑न ।  
> यो वां॑ दू॒तो न धि॑ष्ण्या॒वजी॑ग॒रच्छा॑ सू॒नुर्न पि॒तरा॑ विवक्मि ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । वां । रथं । नृपती इति नृपती । जरध्यै । हविष्मता । मनसा । यज्ञियेन ।  
> यः । वां । दूतः । न । धिष्ण्यौ । अजीगः । अच्छ । सूनुः । न । पितरा । विवक्मि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नृपती नृणामृत्विग्यजमानानां स्वामिनावश्विनौ वां युवयो रथं जरध्यै । जरा स्तुतिः । स्तोतुं प्रति गच्छामीति शेषः । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । हविष्मता हविर्युक्तेन यज्ञियेन यज्ञार्हेण मनसा स्तोत्रेण । यो रथो वां हे धिष्ण्यौ धिषणार्हौ । धिषणा स्तुतिः । वां युवां दूतो न दूत इवाजीगः जागरयति प्रबोधयति अस्मान्प्रति गंतुं तं रथमच्छा विवक्मि । आवच्मि । प्रबोधने दृष्टांतः । सूनुर्न पितरा पुत्रो मातापितराविव । अथवात्र यो रथो युवामजीगः तेन रथेन गंतुं बुध्यमानौ युवामच्छा विवक्मीति वा योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O lords of men, that is, of the officiating priests and sacrificers, O Aśvins, I go towards your chariot to praise it; जरा (*jarā*) is praise. By what means: with हविष्मता (*haviṣmatā*), endowed with oblation, and यज्ञियेन (*yajñiyena*), fit for sacrifice, मनसा (*manasā*), that is, with praise. O धिष्ण्यौ (*dhiṣṇyau*), worthy of धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*) (praise): the chariot which, like a messenger, awakens you to come to us, that chariot I address. The example of awakening: as a son awakens his parents. Or else: the chariot by which you awake, I address you who are being awakened to go by that chariot.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृपती (*nṛpatī*)—O Aśvins, lords of men such as officiating priests and sacrificers
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—chariot
- यज्ञियेन (*yajñiyena*)—fit for sacrifice
- हविष्मता (*haviṣmatā*)—endowed with oblation
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with praise
- जरध्यै (*jaradhyai*)—in order to praise
- प्रति (*prati*)—I approach
- धिष्ण्यौ (*dhiṣṇyau*)—O Aśvins, worthy of our praise
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which chariot of yours
- सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—a son
- पितरा (*pitarā*)—as he awakens his parents with respect
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- दूतो न (*dūto na*)—like a messenger
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—awakens
- अच्छा विवक्मि (*acchā vivakmi*)—I praise (that chariot of yours)

### Printed p. 491

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, lords of all people beginning with officiating priests and sacrificers, having prepared the oblation, I approach to praise your chariot with praise fit to be recited in sacrifices and other rites. O Aśvins, worthy of our praise, as a son respectfully awakens his parents, so that chariot of yours awakens you like a messenger; such a chariot I praise.

##### English translation
Lords of men, (I approach) to adore your chariot with devout praise and oblation, I address it as if it were a messenger to awaken you, adorable deities, as a son (addresses) his parents.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अशो॑च्य॒ग्निः स॑मिधा॒नो अ॒स्मे उपो॑ अदृश्र॒न्तम॑सश्चि॒दंताः॑ ।  
> अचे॑ति के॒तुरु॒षसः॑ पु॒रस्ता॑च्छ्रि॒ये दि॒वो दु॑हि॒तुर्जाय॑मानः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अशोचि । अग्निः । सम्ऽइधानः । अस्मे इति । उपो इति । अदृश्रन् । तमसः । चित् ।  
> अंताः ।  
> अचेति । केतुः । उषसः । पुरस्तात् । श्रिये । दिवः । दुहितुः । जायमानः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मे अस्माभिः समिधानः समिध्यमानः सन्नग्निरशोचि । दीप्यते । तमसश्चित्तमसोऽप्यंताः पर्यंताः प्रदेशा उपो अदृश्रन् । उपदृश्यंते सर्वैः । केतुः सर्वस्य प्रज्ञापकः सूर्यो दिवो दुहितुरुषसः पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिशि श्रिये शोभायै जायमानः सन्नचेति । ज्ञायते । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्युवयोरागमनसमयः । अत आगच्छतमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, kindled by us, blazes. Even the extremities of the darkness are seen by all nearby. The Sun, the indicator of all, being born on the east of Dawn, daughter of heaven, for glory, is perceived. Since it is so, it is the time of your coming; hence "come" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*)—well kindled
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- अशोचि (*aśoci*)—is blazing
- तमसश्चित् (*tamasaścit*)—enveloped in darkness
- अंताः (*aṃtāḥ*)—even the edges of the sky

### Printed p. 492
- उपो अदृश्रन् (*upo adṛśran*)—are seen by people nearby
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—the Sun, the indicator for the whole world
- दिवः दुहितुः (*divaḥ duhituḥ*)—of the daughter of heaven or of the atmosphere
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of the goddess Dawn
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—in the forepart, that is, in the east
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—in order to shine
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—having arisen
- अचेति (*aceti*)—is known by all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This morning Agni, kindled by us for the sacrifice, blazes brilliantly. Since light is spreading round the sky that till now (in the night) was enveloped in darkness, all people see the Sun, the indicator of all worlds, rising in the east following the goddess Dawn, daughter of heaven.

##### English translation
Kindled by us, Agni blazes, the extremities of the darkness are seen nigh at hand, the banner (of the sun) is perceived rising with the glory on the east of the dawn, the daughter of heaven.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि वां॑ नू॒नम॑श्विना॒ सुहो॑ता॒ स्तोमैः॑ सिषक्ति नासत्या विव॒क्वान् ।  
> पू॒र्वीभि॑र्यातं प॒थ्या॑भिर॒र्वाक्स्व॒र्विदा॒ वसु॑मता॒ रथे॑न ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । वां । नूनं । अश्विना । सुहोता । स्तोमैः । सिसक्ति । नासत्या । विवक्वान् ।  
> पूर्वीभिः । यातं । पथ्याभिः । अर्वाक् । स्वः-विदा । वसुमता । रथेन ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विना वां युवां सुहोता सुष्ठु देवानां स्तोता विवक्वान् स्तुतीनां वक्ताहं हे नासत्या सत्यभूतौ । इदमश्विनावित्यत्र योज्यं । स्तोमैः सिषक्ति । सेवते । अतोऽर्वागस्मदभिमुखं पूर्वीभिः पथ्याभिः पूर्वक्षुण्णैर्मार्गैः स्वर्विदा स्वर्गमुदकं वा जानता स्वरणवता वा वसुमता धनवता वा रथेन यातं । गच्छतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, I, the good invoker (सुहोता (*suhotā*)), a fine praiser of the gods, and the speaker (विवक्वान् (*vivakvān*)) of praises, serve you with hymns; O नासत्या (*nāsatyā*), truthful ones. The words इदमश्विना (*idamaśvinā*) are to be supplied here. Therefore come towards us by the ancient, well-trodden paths, with a chariot that knows heaven or water (स्वर्विदा (*svarvidā*)), or is possessed of sound, and is laden with wealth.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, of the nature of truth, I who invoke you, the gods, praise and serve you with hymns. Therefore come toward us, that is, toward our sacrificial ground, setting out by the ancient paths, seated in your chariot, which gives rain and is laden with wealth.

##### English translation
Verily, Aswins, the pious priest repeating (your praises) glorifies you, Nasatyas, with hymns: come therefore by formerly-trodden paths to our presence with your chariot, familiar with heaven, laden with treasure.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनावश्विनौ अवो रक्षित्रोर्युवाभ्यां युवाकुर्युवां कामयमानोऽहं नूनमद्य स्वभूतो भवामीति शेषः । यद्यस्माद् हे माध्वी मधुरस्य सोमस्यार्हौ मधुविद्यासंबंधिनौ वा वां युवां सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे वसूयुर्वसुकामो हुवे स्तौमि अतो वां स्वभूतः । वां युवामा वहंतु । के । स्थविरासः स्थूलाः प्रवृद्धा अश्वाः । एतयोरतिशयस्थवृद्धत्वाच्छीघ्रगतेरपेक्षितत्वाच्च स्थविरैरेव भाव्यं । आगमनानंतरमस्मे अस्माभिः सुषुता सुष्ठ्वभिषुतानि मधूनि मधुररसान् पिबाथः । पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, protectors: I, desiring you, am now truly your own (this must be supplied). Since, O Mādhvīs, you who are worthy of the sweet Soma or connected with the Madhu-vidyā, I, wishing for wealth, invoke (praise) you when the Soma is pressed, therefore I am yours. Let your stout, grown horses bring you; since the two of you are exceedingly stout and old, and swift going is wanted, it must be stout horses. After coming, drink the sweet juices well pressed by us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvins, worthy of the sweet Soma-drink or knowing the Madhu-vidyā
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- सुते (*sute*)—at this time when Soma is pressed
- वसूयुः (*vasūyuḥ*)—I who desire wealth
- हुवे (*huve*)—pray to and call
- स्थविरासः (*sthavirāsaḥ*)—of stout form (well-fed)
- अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*)—your horses
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- आवहंतु (*āvahaṃtu*)—let them bring (to us); (afterwards you)
- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- सुषुता (*suṣutā*)—well pressed
- मधूनि (*madhūni*)—sweet Soma juices
- पिबाथः (*pibāthaḥ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, I, desiring your protection, am yours, who give protection to all. Therefore, O Aśvins, worthy of the sweet Soma-drink or knowing the Madhu-vidyā, I, desiring wealth, pray to and call you at this time when the Soma is pressed. May your stout and swift horses bring you to this our sacrificial ground. Then drink this sweet Soma juice pressed by us according to rule.

##### English translation
Relying on you, Aswins, as protectors, desirous of wealth, Madhwas, I invoke you when the Soma is effused: may your stout horse bring you (hither): drink the sweet juice poured out by us.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्राची॑मु देवाश्विना॒ धियं॒ मेऽमृ॑ध्रां सा॒तये॑ कृतं वसू॒युं ।

### Printed p. 495

> विश्वा अविष्टं वाज आ पुरंधीस्ता नः शक्तं शचीपती शचीभिः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्राचीं । ऊं इति । देवा । अश्विना । धियं । मे । अमृध्रां । सातये । कृतं । वसुयुं ।  
> विश्वाः । अविष्टं । वाजे । आ । पुरंधीः । ता । नः । शक्तं । शचीपती इति शचीपती ।  
> शचीभिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विनौ देवा देवौ युवां प्राचीमृज्वीममृध्रामहिंसितां वसूयुं धनमिच्छंतीं मे मम धियं बुद्धिं स्तुतिं कर्म वा सातये लाभायोचितां कृतं । कुरुतं । किंच वाज आ संग्रामेऽपि विश्वाः पुरंधीरस्मदीया बुद्धीरविष्टं । रक्षतं । हे शचीपती । शचीति कर्मनाम । कर्मणां पालकौ ता तौ युवां शचीभिरस्मदीयैः स्तुत्यादिरूपैः कर्मभिर्नोऽस्माञ्छक्तं । प्रयच्छतं धनमिति शेषः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O divine Aśvins, make my adoration (thought, praise or rite), which is straight (sincere), unharmed and desirous of wealth, fit for the winning of gain. Further, in battle too protect all our intelligences. O lords of Śacī (Śacī is a name for rite), protectors of rites, you, by our rites in the form of praise and the like, bestow (wealth, to be supplied) on us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- देवा (*devā*)—you who are divine
- प्राचीं (*prācīṃ*)—that which is of the nature of truth, that is, offered with devotion
- अमृध्रां (*amṛdhrāṃ*)—unharmed
- वसूयुं (*vasūyuṃ*)—and desiring wealth
- मे धियं (*me dhiyaṃ*)—this hymn or rite of mine
- सातये (*sātaye*)—as fruitful
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—make (and)
- वाजे आ (*vāje ā*)—even in battle
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- पुरंधीः (*puraṃdhīḥ*)—our intelligences
- अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)—protect
- शचीपती (*śacīpatī*)—protectors of rites such as sacrifice
- ता (*tā*)—you
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by the rites of praise and the like that we perform
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- शक्तं (*śaktaṃ*)—make endowed with wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, you who are divine, make this hymn of ours, which is of the nature of truth, free from obstacle and desirous of wealth, fruitful; and protect us, so that even in battle our intelligence may be a help to us. You who protect rites such as sacrifice, be pleased with our rites of praise and give us wealth and the like.

##### English translation
Divine Ashwins, render my sincere and undisturbed adoration, offered for the sake of riches, (efficacious) for their acquisition: preserve all my

### Printed p. 496
faculties in (the time of) battle: protectors of pious acts, (influenced) by our acts, bestow upon us (wealth).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒वि॒ष्टं धी॒ष्व॑श्विना न आ॒सु प्र॒जाव॒द्रेतो॒ अह्र॑यं नो अस्तु ।  
> आ वां॑ तो॒के तन॑ये॒ तूतु॑जानाः सु॒रत्ना॑सो दे॒ववी॑तिं गमेम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अविष्टं । धीषु । अश्विना । नः । आसु । प्रजावत् । रेतः । अह्रयं । नः । अस्तु ।  
> आ । वां । तोके । तनये । तूतुजानाः । सुरत्नासः । देववीतिं । गमेम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विनौ नोऽस्मानासु धीष्वेषु कर्मस्वविष्टं । रक्षतं । नोऽस्मभ्यमह्रयमक्षीणं प्रजावत्पुत्राद्युपेतं पुत्रोत्पादनसमर्थं रेतोऽस्तु । वां युवयोरनुग्रहाल्लब्धे तोके पुत्रे तनये तत्पुत्रादौ च तूतुजाना अभिमतं धनं प्रयच्छंतः सुरत्नासः शोभनधनाश्च संतो देववीतिं देवानां वीतिः प्राप्तिर्यस्मिंस्तादृशं यज्ञमा गमेम । आगच्छेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, protect us in these rites. May there be for us imperishable procreative power (रेतः (*retaḥ*)), endowed with offspring, able to beget sons. By your favour, having obtained a son and a grandson and the like, distributing to them the desired wealth, and being possessed of fine wealth, may we come to the sacrifice in which the gods' arrival takes place.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- आसु धीषु (*āsu dhīṣu*)—in these times of rites
- अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)—protect
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- अह्रयं (*ahrayaṃ*)—imperishable
- प्रजावत् (*prajāvat*)—endowed with sons and the like
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—wealth
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be granted
- वां (*vāṃ*)—obtained by your favour
- तोके (*toke*)—to sons
- तनये (*tanaye*)—and to grandsons
- तूतुजानाः (*tūtujānāḥ*)—distributing the desired wealth
- सुरत्नासः (*suratnāsaḥ*)—and possessing excellent wealth
- देववीतिं (*devavītiṃ*)—the sacrifice, the act of worship of the gods
- आ गमेम (*ā gamema*)—may we perform

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, protect us at this time of the rite. May there be for us imperishable wealth, endowed with sons and the like. Distributing wealth to our sons and grandsons obtained by your favour, and possessing excellent wealth, may we perform the sacrifice, the act of worship of the gods.

### Printed p. 497

##### English translation
Protect us, Aswins, in these pious acts, may our procreative power fail not: but (through your favour) possessing sons and grandsons, distributing desired riches and enjoying ample wealth, may we accomplish the worship of the gods.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्य वां॑ पूर्व॒गत्वे॑व॒ सख्ये॑ नि॒धिर्हि॒तो मा॑ध्वी रा॒तो अ॒स्मे ।  
> अहे॑ळता॒ मन॒सा या॑तम॒र्वाग॒श्नंता॑ ह॒व्यं मानु॑षीषु वि॒क्षु॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्यः । वां । पूर्वगत्वाऽइव । सख्ये । निधिः । हितः । माध्वी इति । रातः ।  
> अस्मे इति ।  
> अहेळता । मनसा । आ । यातं । अर्वाक् । अश्नंता । हव्यं । मानुषीषु । विक्षु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एष पुरतो दीयमानः स्य स युवयोः प्रियत्वेन प्रसिद्धः सोमो हे माध्वी मधुप्रियावश्विनौ वां युवयोः पुरतो निधिर्निधिस्थानीयो हितः स्थापितोऽस्मे अस्माभी रातो दत्तः संकल्पितः संनिहितः । किमिव । सख्ये सख्यार्थं पूर्वगत्वेव पुरतो गंता दूत इव । स यथा प्रियं जनयन् स्वामिनः पुरतो वर्तते कॆद्वदित्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं तस्मादहेळेताक्रुध्यता मनसानुग्रहयुक्तेन चेतसार्वागस्मदभिमुखमा यातं । आगच्छतं । अश्नंता हव्यं हविः सोमादिकमश्नंतावभ्यवहरंतौ । कुत्र । मानुषीषु विक्षु मनुष्यरूपासु प्रजासु वर्तमानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, offered before you and known as dear to you, O Mādhvīs, lovers of sweet drink, has been placed before you like a treasure; it has been given, appointed and set by us. Like what? Like a forerunner, a messenger, going before for the sake of friendship: as he stands before his master producing what is dear, so (is the Soma). Since this is so, come toward us with a mind not angry, full of favour, both of you eating the oblation, Soma and the rest, that is present among the human peoples.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities who desire the sweet Soma
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the famed
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Soma
- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- रातः (*rātaḥ*)—offered
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—to win friendship
- पूर्वगत्वेव (*pūrvagatveva*)—like the treasure that a messenger presents before a king
- वां (*vāṃ*)—before you
- निधिः (*nidhiḥ*)—in the form of a treasure
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—is offered
- मानुषीषु (*mānuṣīṣu*)—human
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among the sacrificers

### Printed p. 498
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- अश्नंता (*aśnaṃtā*)—accepting
- अहेळता (*aheḷatā*)—not angry
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—toward us
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities who desire the sweet Soma, this famed Soma, offered by us, has been presented before you in the form of an oblation, like the treasure a messenger presents before a king to win friendship. Accepting the oblation of the human sacrificers, come toward us with a mind free from anger.

##### English translation
This treasure given by us has been placed, Madhwis, before you, like (an envoy) who has come to the presence (of a prince) for (acquiring his) friendship: come to our presence with benevolent thoughts, accepting the oblations offered amongst human beings.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एक॑स्मि॒न्योगे॑ भुरणा समा॒ने परि॑ वां स॒प्त स्र॒वतो॒ रथो॑ गात् ।  
> न वा॑युंति सु॒भ्वो॑ दे॒वयु॑क्ता॒ ये वां॑ धू॒र्षु त॒रण॑यो॒ वहं॑ति ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एकस्मिन् । योगे । भुरणा । समाने । परि । वां । सप्त । स्रवतः । रथः । गात् ।  
> न । वायंति । सुभ्वः । देवयुक्ताः । ये । वां । धूःसु । तरणयः । वहंति ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे भुरणा सर्वस्य भर्तारौ युवयोरेकस्मिन् समान उभयसाधारणे योगेऽस्मद्विषये सति वां युवयो रथः सप्त स्रवतः सर्पणस्वभावाः सप्तसंख्याका वा गंगाद्याः परि गात् । परिगच्छति । शीघ्रमागच्छतीत्यर्थः । तद्रथानुकूलाः सुभ्वः सुभवना देवयुक्ता देवाभ्यां युवाभ्यां युक्ता अश्वाः शीघ्रगमने न वायंति। न शुष्यंति । न श्राम्यंते । येऽश्वा वां धूर्षु रथस्य तरणयस्तारकाः शीघ्रगंतारो वहंति युवां ते न वायंतीति॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Bhuraṇās, supporters of all: when there is one common yoke for you both with regard to us, your chariot goes around the seven streams, of gliding nature, or the seven rivers such as the Gaṅgā; that is, it comes swiftly. The horses favourable to that chariot, of good being, yoked by you two gods, do not dry up in swift going, are not wearied; the horses which, at the poles of your chariot, are bearers, swift-going, and carry you: they do not tire.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुरणा (*bhuraṇā*)—O Aśvin deities, who bear all the worlds
- एकस्मिन् समाने (*ekasmin samāne*)—engaged in one and the same work
- योगे (*yoge*)—when you are united
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your

- स्रवतः सप्त (*sravataḥ sapta*)—the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the others
- परि गात् (*pari gāt*)—carries across and brings you
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—in the chariots
- तरणयः (*taraṇayaḥ*)—swift
- ये (*ye*)—which horses
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—bear
- सुभ्वः (*subhvaḥ*)—excellent
- देवयुक्ताः (*devayuktāḥ*)—horses that bear you, who are divine
- न वायंति (*na vāyaṃti*)—do not become weary

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, who bear all the worlds, when you are united, engaged in one work, your chariot brings you across the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the others. The swift horses that bear you in the chariots, those excellent horses that bear you who are divine, do not become weary.

##### English translation
Nourishers of all, the chariot of you two who are associated in a common purpose, traverses the seven flowing (streams): the excellent horses harnessed by the gods, who bear you rapidly, careering in the car, are never wearied.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: you two, attached to nothing anywhere, be for the sake of the wealthy, those who possess oblations, the sacrificers. He asks what kind of persons they are to be favoured; the "favourable" ones are the ones further qualified.

### Printed p. 500

> ग्राह्या एव विशेष्यंते । ये राया धनेन निमित्तेन राया युक्ता वा मघदेयं दातव्यं मघं धनं हविर्लक्षणं वा जुषंते प्रेरयंति यच्छंति । ये च बंधुं । स्नेहेन बध्नातीति बंधुः । तं स्वसंबंधिनं । अथवा फलेन बध्नातीति बंधुरध्वर्य्वादिः । तं सूनृताभिः प्रियसत्यात्मिकाभिर्वाग्भिः प्र तिरंते प्रवर्धयंति । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः । किं कुर्वंतः । गव्या गोरूपाण्यश्व्या श्वरूपाणि च मघानि धनानि पृंचंतोऽर्थिभ्यः प्रयच्छंतः । केभ्यो मघवद्भ्यो भूतमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those who, by wealth or endowed with wealth, send forth and give the wealth that is to be given, or wealth in the form of oblation; and who foster their kinsman. A bandhu is one who binds by affection, one's own relation; or else one who binds by the fruit (of the rite), such as the Adhvaryu. They foster him with pleasant, truthful words; प्र तिरंते (*pra tiraṃte*) means "they cause to grow", the root tir with pra having the sense of growth. What are they doing? Giving to petitioners wealth in the form of cattle and of horses. For whom? "Be for the wealthy."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvin deities) ये (*ye*)—who
- राया (*rāyā*)—being endowed with wealth
- मघदेयं (*maghadeyaṃ*)—the oblation fit to be offered
- जुषंते (*juṣaṃte*)—offer
- ये (*ye*)—who
- गव्या (*gavyā*)—consisting of cattle
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—and of horses
- मघानि (*maghāni*)—wealth
- पृंचंतः (*pṛṃcaṃtaḥ*)—distributing
- बंधुं (*baṃdhuṃ*)—their own household
- सूनृताभिः (*sūnṛtābhiḥ*)—with excellent words
- प्र तिरंते (*pra tiraṃte*)—nourish
- मघवद्भ्यः (*maghavadbhyaḥ*)—for such sacrificers who possess oblations
- असश्चता (*asaścatā*)—with a mind free of sloth
- भूतं हि (*bhūtaṃ hi*)—be their protectors

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, for those sacrificers endowed with wealth who offer you the oblation fit for offering, who distribute wealth of cattle and horses and nourish their own kinsfolk by speaking excellent, respectful words, be protectors with a mind free of sloth.

##### English translation
Be propitious to those who are affluent (in oblations), who offer the wealth that is to be offered for the sake of riches : they who encourage a kinsman with kind commendations, distributing wealth of cattle and of horses.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू मे॒ हव॒मा शृ॑णुतं युवाना यासि॒ष्टं व॒र्तिर॑श्विना॒विरा॑वत् ।  
> ध॒त्तं रत्ना॑नि॒ जर॑तं च सू॒रीन् यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः ॥

### Printed p. 501

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । मे । हवं । आ । शृणुतं । युवाना । यासिष्टं । वर्तिः । अश्विनौ । इरावत् ।  
> धत्तं । रत्नानि । जरतं । च । सूरीन् । यूयं । पात । स्वस्ति-भिः । सदा । नः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे युवाना नित्ययौवनौ अद्य युवां मे हवमस्मदीयां स्तुतिमा शृणुतं । श्रुत्वा च हे अश्विनौ इरावद्धविर्युक्तं वर्तिर्गृहं यासिष्टं । आगच्छतं । आगत्य च रत्नानि रमणीयानि धनानि दत्तं । धत्तं । सूरीन् स्तोतॄन् जरतं । वर्धयतं ॥ धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात् ॥ शिष्टं स्पष्टं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ever-youthful ones, today hear my invocation, that is, our praise. Having heard, O Aśvins, come to the house provided with oblation. Having come, bestow delightful riches, and जरतं (*jarataṃ*) the praisers: make them grow, since roots have many meanings. The rest is clear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवाना (*yuvānā*)—ever-youthful
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- नु (*nu*)—now
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—praise
- आ शृणुतं (*ā śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear
- इरावत् (*irāvat*)—provided with oblation
- वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)—our house
- यासिष्टं (*yāsiṣṭaṃ*)—enter
- रत्नानि (*ratnāni*)—delightful riches
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give
- सूरीन् (*sūrīn*)—the praisers
- जरतं (*jarataṃ*)—nourish
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with auspicious gifts
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O ever-youthful Aśvin deities, hear my praise now. Enter our house provided with oblation. Give us delightful riches. Nourish the praisers. Protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
Ever youthful Aswins, hear to-day my invocation : come Ashwins, to the dwelling where the oblation is prepared : grant wealth (to the offerer): elevate the worshipper : and do you ever cherish us with blessings.

### Printed p. 502
## Sūkta 68 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ शुभ्रा यातमिति नवर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षमाश्विनं । आदितः सप्त विराजोऽष्टमीनवम्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ । अनुक्रम्यते च । आ शुभ्रा नव सप्ताद्या विराज इति । सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The thirteenth sūkta, आ शुभ्रा यातं (*ā śubhrā yātaṃ*), of nine Ṛks, belongs to the seer Vasiṣṭha and is addressed to the Aśvins. The first seven Ṛks are virāj; the eighth and ninth are triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: आ शुभ्रा नव सप्ताद्या विराजः (*ā śubhrā nava saptādyā virājaḥ*). The use of the sūkta is by indication (laiṅgika).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, आ शुभ्रा यातं (*ā śubhrā yātaṃ*), is the thirteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer; the Aśvin deities are the deity. The first seven Ṛks are in the virāṭ metre; the eighth and ninth in triṣṭup. The Anukramaṇī says: आ शुभ्रा नव सप्ताद्या विराजः (*ā śubhrā nava saptādyā virājaḥ*). The use is laiṅgika.

Sūkta 68. Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 68. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 5; Varga 14, 15. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: the Aśvins. Metre: 1–7 virāṭ; 8, 9 triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ शु॑भ्रा यातमश्विना॒ स्वश्वा॒ गिरो॑ दस्रा जुजुषा॒णा यु॒वाकोः॑ ।  
> ह॒व्यानि॑ च॒ प्रति॑भृता वी॒तं नः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । शुभ्रा । यातं । अश्विना । सुअश्वा । गिरः । दस्रा । जुजुषाणा । युवाकोः ।  
> हव्यानि । च । प्रतिभृता । वीतं । नः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुभ्रा दीप्तौ स्वश्वा शोभनाश्वौ हे अश्विनावश्विनौ आ यातं । अस्मद्यज्ञमागच्छतं । दस्रा शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारौ युवां युवाकोर्युवां कामयमानस्य मम गिरः स्तुतीर्जुजुषाणा सेवमानौ भवतमिति शेषः । न केवलं स्तुतिं किंतु नोऽस्मदीयानि प्रतिभृता संभृतानि हव्यानि हवींषि च वीतं भक्षयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bright ones, possessed of fine horses, O Aśvins, come to our sacrifice. O Dasras, destroyers of enemies, being desirous of you, may you be favourable to my praises; this is the remaining supplement. Not only the praise, but also eat our gathered oblations.

### Printed p. 503

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुभ्रा (*śubhrā*)—radiant
- स्वश्वा (*svaśvā*)—possessed of excellent horses
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- आयातं (*āyātaṃ*)—come to us
- दस्रा (*dasrā*)—you destroyers of enemies
- युवाकोः (*yuvākoḥ*)—of me who seek your service
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises
- जुजुषाणा (*jujuṣāṇā*)—accepting
- नः (*naḥ*)—by us
- प्रतिभृता (*pratibhṛtā*)—acquired
- हव्यानि च (*havyāni ca*)—and the oblations
- वीतं (*vītaṃ*)—partake of

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Aśvin deities, possessed of excellent horses, come to us. You destroyers of enemies, accepting the praises of me who seek your service, partake of the oblations acquired by us.

##### English translation
Illustrious Aswins, lords of handsome horses, come hither, propitia-ted, Dasras, by the praises of your adorer, and partake of our consecrated oblations.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वा॒मंधां॑सि॒ मद्या॑न्यस्थु॒ररं॑ गंतं ह॒विषो॑ वी॒तये॑ मे ।  
> ति॒रो अ॒र्यो हव॑नानि श्रु॒तं नः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वां । अंधांसि । मद्यानि । अस्थुः । अरं । गंतं । हविषः । वीतये । मे ।  
> तिरः । अर्यः । हवनानि । श्रुतं । नः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र वामंधांसीत्येषाश्विनशस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र वामंधांसि मद्यान्यस्थुरुभा पिबतमश्विना । आ—६—५ । इति ॥
> हे अश्विनौ वां युवाभ्यां मद्यानि मदजनकान्यंधांसि सोमलक्षणान्यन्नानि प्रास्थुः । प्रास्थिषत । गृहीतान्यासन्नित्यर्थः । अतो युवां मे मम हविषो वीतये पानायारमत्यर्थं शीघ्रं गंतं । आगच्छतं । अर्योऽरेरस्मद्विरोधिनो हवनानि तिरस्कृत्य नः । अस्मदाह्वानमित्यर्थः । तच्छ्रुतं । शृणुतं ॥ श्रुतमित्यस्य काव्यादित्वादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk, प्र वामंधांसि (*pra vāmaṃdhāṃsi*), is the yājyā of the Aśvinaśastra. It is prescribed in the sūtra: प्र वामंधांसि मद्यान्यस्थुरुभा पिबतमश्विना (*pra vāmaṃdhāṃsi madyānyasthurubhā pibatamaśvinā*) (Ā. 6-5). O Aśvins, exhilarating viands in the form of Soma have been set out for you, that is, have been taken up and are at hand. Therefore come quickly to drink my oblation, abundantly. Disregarding the invocations of the foe, the adversary, hear our call.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvin deities) वां (*vāṃ*)—for you
- मद्यानि (*madyāni*)—exhilarating
- अंधांसि (*aṃdhāṃsi*)—viands in the form of Soma
- प्र अस्थुः (*pra asthuḥ*)—have been set out
- मे (*me*)—my
- हविषः (*haviṣaḥ*)—oblations
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—to drink
- अरं (*araṃ*)—quickly
- गंतं (*gaṃtaṃ*)—come
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—of our enemy
- हवनानि (*havanāni*)—the invocations
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—disregard
- नः (*naḥ*)—our invocation
- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, exhilarating Soma has been set out for you. Come quickly to drink my oblations (the Soma juices). Disregard the invocations of your enemy; hear only our invocation.

##### English translation
The exhilarating viands have been prepared for you : come quickly to partake of my oblation: disregarding the invocations of an adversary, listen to ours.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk प्र वामंधांसि (*pra vāmaṃdhāṃsi*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra among the mantras of the Aśvinaśastra, as is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the sūtra प्र वामंधांसि मद्यान्यस्थुरुभा पिबतमश्विना (*pra vāmaṃdhāṃsi madyānyasthurubhā pibatamaśvinā*) (Ā. 6-5).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वां॒ रथो॒ मनो॑जवा इयर्ति ति॒रो रजां॑स्यश्विना श॒तोतिः॑ ।  
> अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ सूर्यावसू इया॒नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मभ्यं । सूर्यावसू इति । इयानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सूर्यावसू सूर्यायाः सह रथे वसंतौ वां युवयो रथोऽस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थमियानो याच्यमानः सन्नियर्ति । आगच्छत्यस्मद्यज्ञं । अथवा वां

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūryāvasū, who dwell in one chariot together with Sūryā, your chariot, being asked for our sake, comes to our sacrifice. Or else, of you…

### Printed p. 505

> प्रेरयति गमनाय । कीदृशो रथः । मनोजवा मनोवेगः शतोतिरपरिमितास्मद्विषयरक्षणः । किं कुर्वन् । रजांसि लोकांस्तिरस्कृत्यातिक्रम्येयर्तीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes his gloss of the verse. The chariot is set in motion for going. It is described as swift as the mind, and as having countless protections that guard what concerns us. What does it do? Passing beyond the worlds, it comes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यावसू (*sūryāvasū*)—seated in the chariot together with Sūryā
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvins
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- मनोजवाः (*manojavāḥ*)—possessing the speed of the mind
- शतोतिः (*śatotiḥ*)—possessing many kinds of protection
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—the chariot
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—all the worlds
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—crossing over
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—for us
- इयानः (*iyānaḥ*)—being entreated
- प्र इयर्ति (*pra iyarti*)—comes (brings you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, seated in the chariot together with Sūryā, your chariot, swift as the mind and possessing many kinds of protection, crosses all the worlds and comes for us, being entreated. It brings you.

##### English translation
Your chariot, Ashwins, in which you ride with Surya, hastens towards us at our solicitation, traversing the regions as swift as thought, and laden with a hundred blessings.

> अ॒यं ह॒ यद्वां॑ देव॒या उ॒ अद्रि॑रू॒र्ध्वो विव॑क्ति सोम॒सुद्यु॒वभ्यां॑ ।  
> आ व॒ल्गू विप्रो॑ ववृतीत ह॒व्यैः ॥ ४ ॥

> युवभ्यां ।  
> आ । वल्गू इति । विप्रः । ववृतीत । हव्यैः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 506

> यद्यदा वां युवां प्रति देवया देवौ युवां कामयमानः । उ इति पूरणः । अयमद्रिरभिषवग्रावा सोमसुत् सोममभिषुण्वन् युवभ्यां । युवाभ्यामर्थायाभिषुण्वन्निति संबंधः । एवं कुर्वन्नूर्ध्व उन्नतः सन् विवक्ति उच्चैः शब्दयति तदानीं वल्गू सुंदरौ युवां विप्रो मेधावी यजमानो हव्यैर्हविर्भिरा ववृतीते । आवर्तयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When this pressing-stone, desiring you two gods, is raised aloft and presses out Soma for you, it sounds loudly. Then the wise sacrificer, the vipra, turns you, the beautiful ones, towards himself with oblations. उ (*u*) is an expletive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वां (*vāṃ*)—addressing you
- देवयाः (*devayāḥ*)—desiring you who are gods
- अयं अद्रिः (*ayaṃ adriḥ*)—this pressing-stone
- युवभ्यां (*yuvabhyāṃ*)—for you
- सोमसुत् (*somasut*)—pressing Soma
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—raised aloft
- विवक्ति (*vivakti*)—sounds; then
- वल्गू (*valgū*)—you of beautiful form
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise sacrificer
- हव्यैः (*havyaiḥ*)—with oblations
- आ ववृतीते (*ā vavṛtīte*)—makes you turn back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, when this pressing-stone, desiring you who are gods, is raised aloft and sounds as it presses Soma for you, then the wise sacrificer makes you of beautiful form turn back with oblations.

##### English translation
When the stone, seeking to propitiate you two divinities, is raised aloft and loudly sounds, expressing for you the Soma juice, then the pious worshipper brings you back, beautiful divinities, by his oblations.

> यः । वां । ओमानं । दधते । प्रियः । सन् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोश्चित्रं चायनीयं यद्भोजनं धनमस्ति ह अस्ति खलु । न्विति पूरणः । तदस्मभ्यं दत्तमित्यर्थः । अथ शयोः स्तुतिः । अत्रये एतन्नामकादृषेः । पंचम्यर्थे चतुर्थी । तस्मान्महिष्वंतम्बीसं नि युयोतं । पृथक्कृतवंतौ । योऽत्रिः प्रियः सन् स्तोत्रैरात्मानं वाभ्यां प्रियभूतः सन् युवाभ्यामेव कृतोमानं रक्षणं सुखं दधते धारयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, the wondrous, desirable wealth that is yours indeed exists; नु (*nu*) is an expletive. The sense: it is given to us. Then there is praise of the two: from the sage named Atri (the fourth case in the sense of the fifth) you separated the confinement महिष्वंतं (*mahiṣvaṃtaṃ*). Atri, being dear and having made himself dear to you through praises, holds protection and happiness made by you alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वां (*vāṃ*)—belonging to you
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—attractive
- यत् भोजनं (*yat bhojanaṃ*)—whatever wealth fit for enjoyment
- अस्ति ह (*asti ha*)—exists, give it to us
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Atri
- प्रियः सन् (*priyaḥ san*)—being worthy of your affection
- वां ओमानं (*vāṃ omānaṃ*)—your protection
- दधते (*dadhate*)—holds
- अत्रये (*atraye*)—from such an Atri
- महिष्वंतं (*mahiṣvaṃtaṃ*)—the exceedingly great bondage
- नि युयोतं (*ni yuyotaṃ*)—you separated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, give us whatever attractive wealth fit for enjoyment belongs to you. You freed from bondage that Atri who, being worthy of your affection, had obtained your protection.

##### English translation
Wonderful, verily, is the wealth that is yours : you have liberated from the cave Atri, who is dear to you, and enjoys your protection.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त त्यद्वां॑ जुर॒ते अ॑श्विना भू॒च्च्यवा॑नाय प्र॒तीत्यं॑ हवि॒र्दे ।  
> अधि॒ यद्वर्प॑ इ॒तऊ॑ति ध॒त्थः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । त्यत् । वां । जुरते । अश्विना । भूत् । च्यवानाय । प्रतीत्यं । हविःदे ।  
> अधि । यत् । वर्पः । इतःऊति । धत्थः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 508

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे अश्विनावश्विनौ वां युवयोः कर्म कुर्वते जुरते जूर्णाय हविर्दे हविर्दात्रे च्यवानायर्षये महर्षये त्यत्तत्प्रतीत्यं प्रतिगमनं तस्य रूपस्य प्रत्याप्त्यै भूत् । अभूत् । किं तदिति । यद्वर्पो रूपमितऊतीतोगमनाख्यं मृत्योः सकाशादितःप्राप्तिरूपमधि धत्थः अध्यधत्तं । युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । ऋ. १-११७-१३ । इत्यादिषु च्यवानस्य युवयोर्नवीकरणं प्रसिद्धं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, for the aged Cyavāna, the sage who performs rites for you and gives oblations, that return to his former form came about, to regain it. What is it? The form, the appearance, that you established, the going back from death, the attainment of coming back from it. Sāyaṇa cites युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । (*yuvaṃ cyavānamaśvinā jaraṃtaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-13) and says that in such passages the renewal of Cyavāna by the two is well known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvins
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- त्यत् (*tyat*)—the famous deed
- जुरते (*jurate*)—who praises
- हविर्दे (*havirde*)—who offers oblation
- च्यवानाय (*cyavānāya*)—to the great sage named Cyavāna
- प्रतीत्यं (*pratītyaṃ*)—possessing the power to give back his youth
- भूत् (*bhūt*)—became
- यद्वर्पः (*yadvarpaḥ*)—that same beauty of his
- इतऊति (*itaūti*)—the return from death
- अधि धत्थः (*adhi dhatthaḥ*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, your famous deed became, for the great sage Cyavāna, who praises and offers oblations, one with the power to restore his youth. That same beauty of his escaped from the mouth of death.

##### English translation
Such was your benevolence, Ashwins, to Chyavana, praising and offering oblations, that you in requital rescued his body from departure.

> उ॒त त्यं भु॒ज्युम॑श्विना॒ सखा॑यो॒ मध्ये॑ जहुर्दु॒रेवा॑सः समु॒द्रे ।  
> निरीं॑ पर्ष॒दरा॑वा॒ यो यु॒वाकुः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । त्यं । भुज्युं । अश्विना । सखायः । मध्ये । जहुः । दुःएवासः । समुद्रे ।  
> निः । ईं । पर्षत् । अरावा । यः । युवाकुः ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 509

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च त्यं तं भुज्युमेतन्नामानं समुद्रे मध्ये समुद्रोदकस्य मध्ये सखायो भुज्युसखिभूता दुरेवासो दुष्टगमना जहुः । त्यक्तवंतः । ईमेनं समुद्रमध्ये क्षिप्तं निः पर्षत् । निरपारयतं । यो भुज्युर्युवाकुर्युवां कामयितारावारणपानभिगंता च तमेनं निरपारयतं । अत्राश्विनेषु सूक्तेषु कथाः सूच्यंते । अत्रिभुज्य्वादीनामग्निजलादिभ्यो रक्षणरूपास्ताः सर्वा महता प्रपंचेनास्माभिर्नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव । ऋ. १-११६-१ । इत्यत्र प्रपंचिताः । तास्तत्र द्रष्टव्याः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Bhujyu, in the midst of the sea-water, was abandoned by those who had been his friends, ill-going. You brought out this one who had been cast into mid-ocean. Bhujyu, desiring you and approaching you with devotion, was rescued by you. Sāyaṇa says that the stories of the Aśvins' rescues of Atri, Bhujyu and others from fire, water and so on are indicated in these sūktas. They were set out at great length by him at नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव (*nāsatyābhyāṃ barhiriva*) (Ṛ. 1-116-1) and are to be seen there.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvins
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Bhujyu
- युवाकुः (*yuvākuḥ*)—desired your service
- अरावा (*arāvā*)—was devoted to you alone
- त्यं भुज्युं (*tyaṃ bhujyuṃ*)—that Bhujyu
- समुद्रे मध्ये (*samudre madhye*)—in the middle of the sea
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—those who were like his friends
- दुरेवासः (*durevāsaḥ*)—those who wished him harm
- जहुः (*jahuḥ*)—threw (him) away; then
- ईं (*īṃ*)—him
- निः पर्षत् (*niḥ parṣat*)—protect completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, when enemies who were like friends threw into the middle of the sea that Bhujyu who desired your service and was devoted to you, you protected him completely.

##### English translation
When faithless friends had abandoned Bhujyu in the midst of the ocean, you brought him to shore, devoted to and relying upon you.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृका॑य चि॒ज्जस॑मानाय शक्तमु॒त श्रु॑तं श॒यवे॑ हू॒यमा॑ना ।  
> याव॒घ्न्यामपि॑न्वतम॒पो न स्त॒र्यं॑ चिच्छ॒क्र्य॑श्विना॒ शची॑भिः ॥
